Schedule: 7:30am - 4pm

jobs.title: Product Cost Management Lead - AI Infrastructure
jobs.description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization is building the infrastructure foundation for frontier AI systems. The Supply Chain organization enables scalable, resilient, and efficient supply chains across custom silicon, systems, networking, memory, storage, and rack-scale infrastructure.

Our team connects engineering, supplier strategy, manufacturing, planning, deployment, and finance to make hardware cost, supply, and execution tradeoffs clear from early architecture through production and sustaining operations.

About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a Product Cost Management Lead to own the official costed bill of materials (BOM), system and cluster cost and price baseline, and platform-to-platform total cost of ownership (TCO) for our 1P AI infrastructure. You will turn component, system, POD, manufacturing, deployment, DC, service, and lifecycle inputs into a trusted view of product economics that informs technical and business decisions, including transition timing.

You will partner with Engineering, Strategic Sourcing, Manufacturing-partner management, Finance, Planning, Supply Chain Program Management, Operations Program Management, and infrastructure teams to evaluate engineering / design changes, compare alternatives, identify cost-reduction opportunities, and track realized benefits.

This is an individual contributor role with broad cross-functional ownership. The ideal candidate combines hardware cost expertise, rigorous modeling, sound judgment, and the ability to explain complex tradeoffs clearly to engineering, operations, and senior leaders.

In this role, you will:

 - Own the official costed BOM and system/pod roll-up by platform, generation, configuration, build phase, volume, and mix. Maintain version control and traceability to quotes, source owners, assumptions, and engineering revisions.

 - Publish and maintain the system/pod cost and price baseline, reconciling component pricing and manufacturing-partner inputs with approved configurations and planning assumptions.

 - Build platform-to-platform TCO comparisons covering component content, non-recurring engineering, tooling, manufacturing labor and overhead, yield, scrap, test, logistics, deployment, housing and site costs, power and cooling, networking, spares, service, warranty, and lifecycle costs.

 - Partner with housing and site teams to integrate their cost inputs into product economics, documenting scope, timing, allocation assumptions, and gaps so platform comparisons are consistent and avoid double counting.

 - Quantify the cost impact of engineering change orders and notices (ECOs/ECNs), architecture, specification, configuration, and qualification changes before approval. Assess recurring and one-time costs, implementation timing, inventory exposure, and expected benefits.

 - Develop a prioritized cost-reduction, value-engineering, and second-source opportunity funnel with Engineering, Strategic Sourcing, and manufacturing-partner management. Evaluate qualification costs, investment, payback, supply improvements, and execution risk.

 - Analyze actual, forecast, quoted, committed, and purchase-price costs against the baseline. Explain material variances, identify root causes, and track recovery actions with accountable owners and dates.

 - Build sensitivity and scenario analyses for supplier and manufacturing-partner options, capacity, volume and mix, yield, configuration, site, deployment timing, and lifecycle tradeoffs. Present clear recommendations with assumptions, confidence ranges, and decision deadlines.

 - Validate savings and cost avoidance with Finance and accountable source owners. Distinguish identified opportunities, approved actions, and realized benefits, including offsets and implementation costs.

 - Establish cost-data definitions, BOM hierarchy, allocation methods, currency and volume assumptions, refresh expectations, and change-control processes. Flag stale, incomplete, or unsupported inputs before they affect decisions.

 - Lead recurring product-cost and TCO reviews. Publish concise cost bridges, opportunity updates, risks, and decision packages while retaining the supporting detail needed for technical and financial review.

 - Build scalable models, reporting, and data workflows that improve baseline completeness, refresh speed, analysis turnaround, and decision quality as the hardware portfolio grows.

 - You will own integrated product economics and the cost-analysis methodology and the cost analysis itself. Strategic Sourcing and manufacturing-partner management retain commercial negotiations; Engineering retains design and qualification authority; DC and site teams own their source inputs; Finance retains budgets, accounting, and financial approvals; Planning owns the demand baseline; SCPM owns material readiness; and OPM owns operational execution.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - Significant experience in hardware product costing, cost engineering, supply chain finance, manufacturing cost analysis, or a related role supporting complex technology products.

 - Experience building and maintaining multi-level costed BOMs, system cost roll-ups, and lifecycle or TCO models across product development, production ramp, and sustaining operations.

 - Strong understanding of hardware cost drivers, including component pricing, manufacturing labor and overhead, NRE, tooling, yield, scrap, test, logistics, and service costs.

 - Demonstrated ability to evaluate engineering changes, second-source options, and cost-reduction opportunities using comparable scenarios and transparent assumptions.

 - Advanced spreadsheet and quantitative modeling skills, with disciplined data reconciliation, version control, and source traceability.

 - Ability to turn incomplete or changing technical and commercial inputs into defensible analysis, identify uncertainty, and drive input gaps to closure.

 - Strong cross-functional influence and communication skills, including concise leadership recommendations and detailed working sessions with engineering, sourcing, manufacturing, and finance teams.

 - High ownership and sound judgment in a fast-moving environment with evolving requirements and competing priorities.

Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience with AI infrastructure, hyperscale data centers, custom silicon, servers, networking, storage, or rack-scale systems.

 - Experience analyzing JDM, CM, or ODM cost structures and open-book manufacturing models.

 - Familiarity with DC and site economics, power and cooling, deployment timing, spares, and service costs in infrastructure TCO.

 - Experience with ERP, MRP, and PLM systems, BOM change control, and business intelligence or automation/AI tools.

 - A background in engineering, finance, supply chain, manufacturing, or a related analytical discipline.

What Success Looks Like

 - Teams use a complete, current, and traceable costed BOM and system/pod baseline as the source of truth for product economics.

 - Platform TCO comparisons use consistent scope and assumptions, with inputs validated by their owners.

 - Material engineering and sourcing decisions include timely cost-impact analysis and explicit tradeoffs.

 - Cost variances have clear explanations, accountable owners, and recovery actions; savings and cost avoidance are validated.

 - Leadership receives clear recommendations, and cost-management processes scale with the complexity of the 1P hardware roadmap.

jobs.description:
About Us

One Medical is a primary care solution challenging the industry status quo by making quality care more affordable, accessible and enjoyable. But this isn’t your average doctor’s office. We’re on a mission to transform healthcare, which means improving the experience for everyone involved - from patients and providers to employers and health networks. Our seamless in-office and 24/7 virtual care services, on-site labs, and programs for preventive care, chronic care management, common illnesses and mental health concerns have been delighting people for the past fifteen years.

In February 2023 we marked a milestone when One Medical joined Amazon. Together, we look to deliver exceptional health care to more consumers, employers, care team members, and health networks to achieve better health outcomes. As we continue to grow and seek to impact more lives, we’re building a diverse, driven and empathetic team, while working hard to cultivate an environment where everyone can thrive.

Employment type:

• Full time

What you'll be working on:

• Managing a patient panel with a broad array of patient needs; conducting a mix of acute, chronic, and well visits

• Treating patients in-office or in testing centers as well as conducting occasional tele-health visits

• Continuous learning during weekly Clinical Rounds and through other modalities

• Ongoing collaboration with in-office teammates via daily huddles, as well as with virtual clinical teams

• Utilization of your specific clinical training and opportunities to perform in-office procedures

• Supervising one or more NP or PA colleagues

• Willing to obtain additional state licensure and credentialing for One Medical virtual primary care in additional states

• Enrolled in, or have completed, an accredited Internal or Family Medicine residency program

• Practiced at least 2 of the last 5 years in an outpatient primary care setting

• State licensed in California, obtained before your One Medical start date

One Medical providers also demonstrate:

• A passion for human-centered primary care

• The ability to successfully communicate with and provide care to individuals of all backgrounds

• The ability to effectively use technology to deliver high quality care

• Clinical proficiency in evidence-based primary care

• The desire to be an integral part of a team dedicated to changing healthcare delivery

• An openness to feedback and reflection to gain productive insight into strengths and weaknesses

• The ability to confidently navigate uncertain situations with both patients and colleagues

• Readiness to adapt personal and interpersonal behavior to meet the needs of our patients

This is a full-time role based in our Two Embarcadero Center, San Francisco office.

One Medical is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices.

The base salary range for this role is $308,700 to $369,000 based on a full-time schedule. Taking care of you today

• Free One Medical memberships for yourself, your friends and family

• Employee Assistance Program - Free confidential services for team members who need help with stress, anxiety, financial planning, and legal issues

• Competitive Medical, Dental and Vision plans

• Pre-Tax commuter benefits

• PTO cash outs - Option to cash out up to 40 accrued hours per year

Protecting your future for you and your family

• Credit towards emergency childcare

• Company paid maternity and paternity leave

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager, Claude Corps (Fellow Experience)
jobs.description:
CodePath is the largest educator of college computer science students in the country. We've trained over 40,000 students from 1,000+ universities, and our partners include Amazon, Google, and other leading technology companies. We've spent nearly a decade training the next generation of technical talent, and we just launched a $150M initiative with Anthropic, building one of the most ambitious AI workforce programs in the world.

We're now expanding into new markets and scaling our team so we can move at the speed AI is transforming the workforce. People joining CodePath now will have the opportunity to help architect the next frontier of our work.

We believe technical skill is the fastest way to turn raw talent into real opportunity. We train the engineers the AI era runs on, building toward millions of learners, hundreds of millions in revenue, and billions in economic impact. If you want to own something and be part of a 0-to-1 journey at an organization moving at the speed of AI, this is the place to build it.

Location: Remote (U.S.), with regular travel for in-person events
Role type: Full-time
Reports to: Kelly Mosher, Program Lead, Claude Corps
Compensation: $130,000 to $155,000

About Claude Corps

In June 2026, Anthropic and CodePath launched Claude Corps, a $150M national fellowship. It places 1,000 paid, AI-skilled fellows in 12-month roles at mission-driven organizations across the country. Anthropic funds the program and sets strategy. CodePath employs the fellows and leads their training and programming.

The program is growing fast. Cohort 1 started in October 2026 with 100 fellows. Cohort 2 starts in March 2027 with 300. Cohort 3 starts in late summer 2027 with 600. Many fellows relocate to a new city for the year, so their experience, from offer letter to last day, decides whether the program works.

About the role

You'll be the Program Lead's right hand: a senior program manager who can take a whole area of Claude Corps, set the plan, and run it without being managed day to day. That frees Kelly to focus on program operations and strategy across the fellowship.

Your first area is the fellow experience, which today has no single end-to-end owner. You'll own how we communicate with, connect, and gather fellows, from offer through their last day. As the program scales, your scope will shift to wherever the biggest gap is. That could mean host organization experience or another part of the program, and future hires (for example, a community manager) may report to you.

This is a generalist role by design. We're hiring for strong program management judgment, not a single specialty.

What success looks like

First 30 days: learn it and take the wheel

• Get to know Cohort 1 (100 fellows live now), the mentor team, and our Anthropic partners

• Map the fellow journey from offer to day one, and name the three biggest gaps

• Take over day-to-day fellow communications (program inbox, fellow Slack, regular updates) from your manager

• Lock the Cohort 2 onboarding plan for 300 fellows: timeline, host matching updates, and relocation guidance

Days 31 to 60: deliver Cohort 2 Basecamp

• Run the week-long Cohort 2 Basecamp kickoff (starting Feb 22) with our event agency and curriculum team. You'll own the run of show, attendee experience, and on-site problem solving

• Get every Cohort 2 fellow from signed offer to day one with clear, consistent communication

Days 61 to 90: build for scale

• Launch a fellow support model that a small team can run for 1,000 fellows: self-serve resources, AI-assisted answers, and clear escalation to mentors, HR, and program leads

• Stand up community rituals and peer structures that don't depend on you to run

• Report engagement, satisfaction, and retention to CodePath and Anthropic leadership

6 to 12 months

• Cohort 3 (600 fellows) onboards on playbooks you wrote, with fewer people and fewer hours than Cohort 2

• You've documented what works so another team could pick it up and run it

• You've taken on a second program area where we need it most

What you'll do

• Own the plan. Set direction for your program area, make clear trade-offs, and tie the work to outcomes like fellow retention and engagement

• Run the details. Keep many workstreams moving at once and close loops without reminders

• Communicate well. Set honest expectations with fellows, keep the Claude Corps voice consistent, and keep host organizations informed in coordination with Anthropic's host team

• Build systems, not heroics. Use AI, including Claude, every day, and choose tools that let a small team serve thousands of people

• Partner widely. Work closely with the mentor team, curriculum, HR, outside vendors, and Anthropic partners

What we're looking for

Required

• 7+ years in program management, including owning a cohort-based program, fellowship, or member community end to end

• You've set direction for a program area yourself, not only carried out someone else's plan

• You can show how you run a heavy, changing workload: your system, what slipped once, and what you changed afterward

• You've moved work from manual to systematic, and you use AI tools hands-on in your daily work

• You write clearly and warmly and adjust your tone for fellows, executives, and partners

• You can travel to multi-day events several times a year, including February and late summer 2027

Preferred Experience

• Experience in two or more of: participant communications, community building, or large in-person events with an outside agency

• Fellowships, service programs like AmeriCorps, or early-career talent programs

• Supporting participants through a relocation or major life transition

• Experience at a nonprofit, in education, or at a fast-growing startup

Full-Time Employee Benefits

This is a remote position—work from anywhere in the US! CodePath prioritizes employee well-being with a competitive benefits package to support your health, financial security, and work-life balance.

• Health & Wellness: Medical, dental, and vision insurance (90% employer-covered for employees and dependents), employer-funded healthcare reimbursement, FSAs, and Employee Assistance Program

• Financial Security: 401(k), employer-paid life & disability insurance, and identity theft protection

• Work-Life Balance: Generous PTO, paid holidays, 10 weeks of fully paid parental leave, and an annual year-end company closure (Dec 24 – Jan 2)

• Professional Growth: $1,000 annual professional development stipend and home office setup support

• ​​Student Loan Forgiveness: CodePath is a qualifying employer for Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), helping employees manage student loan debt

• Additional Perks: Pet wellness plans, legal services, home/auto insurance discounts, and exclusive marketplace savings

Pay range

$130,000—$155,000 USD

jobs.title: Business Development Director - Utilities
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Atwell, LLC is a bold leader in the consulting, engineering, and construction services industry, delivering a broad range of creative solutions to clients in the real estate & land development, and energy markets. We have a strong national presence and a diverse, award-winning project portfolio. Atwell is a privately owned company, with 2,000+ passionate team members across 75+ locations and growing!

Atwell, LLC is a proud recipient of the following 2025 awards:

• Ten consecutive years in a row as a “Best Place to Work” by Zweig Group (#11)

• Recognized as #70 in the ENR Top 500 Design Firms, ranked in every region

• Recognized in Crain's “Fast 50” as one of the fastest-growing companies (#14)

• Recognized as the 2025 ENR Design Firm of the year for the Southeastern US

About the Position

The Business Development Director - Utilities is responsible for opening and developing priority utility relationships that create sustainable growth for the Power & Energy business. The role is primarily a new-logo and early-stage relationship-development position: building access to targeted investor-owned utilities, municipal utilities, and electric cooperatives; understanding how each client buys; identifying the right entry point; and creating qualified opportunities that can grow into long-term strategic accounts.

This role works as part of a coordinated commercial team. The Business Development Director leads relationship creation and early opportunity development, while Strategic Account Management focuses on expanding established strategic accounts. Seller-doers, technical leaders, executive sponsors, estimating, and Sales Operations are brought into pursuits at the right time. Success requires disciplined prioritization - focusing resources on the utility accounts where Atwell and NEI have an attractive market opportunity, a credible right to win, and a clear path to meaningful work.

Salary Range: $175,000-$225,000 / year

The salary range above is based upon the Denver, Colorado labor market. NEI bases salaries on the Denver, Colorado labor market for both local and remote team members.

Essential Responsibilities

• Meet or exceed assigned order intake targets while supporting appropriate profitability and pursuit discipline.

• Build meaningful relationships and executive access within a defined portfolio of priority utility targets rather than broadly pursuing every available opportunity.

• Create and execute account-entry plans for assigned targets, including relationship maps, buying centers, procurement pathways, incumbent providers, likely entry points, and clear 30/60/90-day actions.

• Identify the most credible initial opportunity to open a relationship, then coordinate the appropriate technical and commercial resources to pursue it.

• Develop relationships across multiple levels of the client organization, including business leaders, engineering, project/program leadership, procurement, and other key influencers.

• Use existing Atwell and NEI relationships, referrals, executive sponsors, seller-doers, industry contacts, and market networks to accelerate access to target accounts.

• Qualify opportunities before significant pursuit resources are committed, considering strategic fit, relationship strength, client need, funding, timing, competitive position, delivery capacity, profitability, and probability of win.

• Coordinate with Strategic Account Managers when a developing relationship reaches the point where the primary growth motion shifts from market entry to systematic account expansion.

• Partner with utility technical leaders and seller-doers to establish technical credibility and translate client needs into solutions across transmission, substations, distribution, system studies, field services, land, environmental, permitting, and other relevant Atwell capabilities.

• Identify opportunities to bring multiple Atwell capabilities to the client while maintaining one coordinated client experience.

• Maintain an accurate, current view of assigned accounts, relationships, opportunities, next actions, and expected timing in the CRM.

• Provide realistic pipeline and order intake forecasts and proactively communicate changes, risks, and resource needs.

• Capture market intelligence including capital programs, procurement cycles, MSAs and vendor qualification requirements, competitive dynamics, client priorities, and emerging utility needs.

• Represent the organization at targeted industry events and client meetings where participation directly supports priority-account development.

• Work with Sales Operations, estimating, pursuit support, and marketing to ensure opportunities move through a consistent commercial process from qualification through proposal and handoff.

How Success Will Be Measured

• Order intake and qualified pipeline created from assigned utility targets.

• Progress penetrating priority new-logo accounts, including meaningful relationships, executive access, vendor/MSA qualification, and first opportunities.

• Quality and depth of relationship coverage within assigned accounts, not simply number of contacts or meetings.

• Conversion of early-stage targets into qualified pursuits, first wins, and ultimately strategic accounts.

• Forecast accuracy, CRM discipline, and clear next actions across the assigned portfolio.

• Pursuit selectivity and efficient use of technical and estimating resources.

• Collaboration across Power & Energy and the broader Atwell platform, including successful cross-service opportunities

Requirements

• Demonstrated success developing business with electric utilities, preferably investor-owned utilities, municipal utilities, and/or electric cooperatives.

• Established utility-industry relationships and the ability to create credible access to senior decision-makers are strongly preferred.

• Working knowledge of how utilities plan, procure, qualify vendors, establish MSAs, fund capital programs, and award engineering or construction-related work.

• Ability to understand client needs and credibly coordinate technical discussions involving transmission, substations, distribution, interconnection, system studies, grid modernization, and related infrastructure.

• Strong commercial judgment with the discipline to prioritize the right accounts and opportunities rather than simply maximize bid volume.

• Ability to build trust across commercial and technical teams and work effectively in a seller-doer culture.

• Excellent communication, relationship-building, facilitation, and executive-presence skills.

• Self-motivated, organized, accountable, and comfortable operating in a fast-paced professional-services environment.

• Coachable, curious, and committed to continuous improvement.

• Proficiency with CRM systems and willingness to maintain timely, accurate account and opportunity information.

• Ability to travel regularly for priority client development, industry events, and internal coordination.

Qualifications & Experience

Experience: 8+ years of business development, strategic account, utility, engineering, construction, or related industry experience; direct utility-market experience strongly preferred.

Education: Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution preferred. Relevant utility-industry experience and relationships may be considered in lieu of a specific degree discipline.

Industry knowledge: Commercial understanding of engineering, construction, and power infrastructure markets.

Working Conditions

Work Environment: Office, remote, client, conference, and project-site settings as required.

Travel: Approximately 30-40%, with travel concentrated around priority accounts and targeted industry activity.

Physical Activities: Ability to travel and participate in client/project-site meetings; must be able to lift up to 25 lbs.

Managerial Responsibility: Individual contributor role unless otherwise assigned. Responsible for independently managing assigned account-development plans, priorities, CRM activity, and commitments in coordination with commercial leadership.

Pay Range

$175,000—$225,000 USD

Atwell Benefits: To attract and retain the best professionals in the industry, we aim to provide an excellent working environment and a progressive benefits program designed to support your personal and professional needs.

Work/Life:

• Generous Paid Time Off

• Paid Parental Leave

• Flexible work schedules are available for some positions

• Tenure Awards — Travel Vouchers to see the world based on your travel preferences

Compensation:

• Competitive Compensation packages

• Annual bonuses, spot bonuses and peer recognition awards

• 401K match - 1:1 up to 4% of compensation

• Tuition Assistance

• Student Loan Repayment

• Paid Licensing / Certification Fees and Renewals

• Financial Rewards for Obtaining Licensure

• Employee Referrals

• Annual Wellness Reimbursement for anything wellness related (Gym memberships, fitness tracker, home gym equipment, etc.)

• Dependent Care Match

‘Atwell’ness:

• Medical (BC/BS), Dental (Delta), and Vision (VSP)

• Family Planning & IVF Benefits

• Pet Insurance

• Health Savings Account & Flex Spending Account options

• Employer paid LTD, STD, and life insurance

• Metlife Supplemental Benefits covering accident, hospitalization, and critical illness

• Member Assistance Program (MAP) with complimentary counseling sessions, legal benefits, financial consultations, and work/life referral services

jobs.title: Strategic Finance Associate
jobs.description:
STRATEGIC FINANCE ASSOCIATE

Freeform builds AI-native manufacturing systems that unify software, hardware, and physics to produce industrial-scale parts at the speed of human ideation. By treating manufacturing as a single integrated system, we unlock a new era of innovation where complex hardware is designed, built, and scaled without limits.

We are looking for an Associate to join our Strategic Finance team and contribute to the financial infrastructure that drives company-wide decision-making. This is an early-career role with significant ownership and visibility. You will support the financial models that power our planning cycles, assist with M&A and partnership activity, and work alongside leadership as a hands-on analytical contributor. If you are eager to develop deep financial modeling skills in a fast-moving environment and want your work to have direct influence on a company scaling a world-changing technology, this role is for you.

Responsibilities:

• Own and maintain the company’s fully integrated financial model, including three-statement modeling, bottoms-up budget build, and rolling forecasts across all business units

• Lead monthly and quarterly variance analysis (actuals vs. budget vs. prior year), translating financial results into clear, executive-ready commentary for leadership and the Board

• Build and maintain customer and product-level pricing models, including unit economics, contribution margin by segment, and scenario/sensitivity analysis to support commercial decisions

• Lead financial modeling for M&A opportunities, including target evaluation, DCF/LBO valuation, synergy modeling, accretion/dilution analysis, and post-close integration tracking

• Own the long-range financial plan (3–5 year), converting strategic initiatives into detailed financial projections with well-documented assumptions and risk sensitivities

• Support structuring and evaluation of joint ventures and strategic partnerships, including economic modeling, waterfall/return attribution, and term sheet analysis

• Drive capital allocation frameworks across the business, helping leadership evaluate trade-offs between organic investment, M&A, and balance sheet decisions

• Prepare board materials, investor reporting, and ad hoc analyses for senior leadership and external stakeholders including venture and growth equity investors

• Partner cross-functionally with Operations, Sales, and Engineering to embed financial rigor into business decisions and provide real-time analytical support on strategic initiatives

Basic Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree in finance, economics, accounting, or related field

• 2+ years of experience in investment banking, private equity, or a strategic finance role at a high-growth company

• Experience with variance analysis, budgeting, and financial reporting in an operating company context

Nice to Have:

• MBA or advanced degree in finance or business

• Exceptional financial modeling skills

• Strong command of Excel; comfortable working with large, complex datasets and building dynamic, assumption-driven models

• Private equity or growth equity experience, particularly at the portfolio company level

• Experience working in a manufacturing, deep tech, or hardware-intensive business

• Experience with financial planning tools (Mosaic, Pigment, Adaptive, or similar)

• “No job too big or small” mindset — willing to roll up sleeves and build from zero

Location:

• Based in Hawthorne, our vertically integrated facility brings technology development, R&D, and production together under one roof. We operate at the center of LA’s deep tech ecosystem, surrounded by some of the most ambitious hardware innovation happening anywhere in the country.

• Our fast-paced, cross-functional environment is built on close collaboration, and as such, this role requires full-time onsite presence (five days a week), with very limited exceptions.

Why Freeform?

• We have an inclusive and diverse culture that values collaboration, learning, and making deliberate data-driven decisions

• We offer a unique opportunity to be an early and integral member of a rapidly growing company that is scaling a world-changing technology

• Benefits Significant stock option packages 100% employer-paid Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance (premium PPO and HMO options) Life insurance Traditional and Roth 401(k) Paid vacation, sick leave, and company holidays Generous Paid Parental Leave and extended transition back to work for the birthing parent Free daily catered lunch and dinner, and fully stocked kitchenette Casual dress, flexible work hours, and regular catered team building events

• Compensation As an early-stage startup, the salary range is intentionally wide as we determine the most appropriate package for each individual taking into consideration years of experience, educational background, and unique skills and abilities as demonstrated throughout the interview process. Our intent is to offer a salary that is commensurate for the company’s current stage of development and allows the employee to grow and develop within a role. In addition to the significant stock option package, the estimated salary range for this role is $110,000 – $135,000. The upper end of the range is reserved for individuals who demonstrate exceptional experience, deep domain mastery, and a proven history of high performance and impact.

Freeform is an Equal Opportunity Employer that values diversity; employment with Freeform is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

jobs.title: Manager, Sales Engineering
jobs.description:
About Us

Socket helps devs and security teams ship faster by cutting out security busywork. Thousands of orgs use Socket to safely find, audit, and manage open source code. Our customers - from Anthropic to xAI, and Figma to Vercel - love Socket (just check out their tweets https://socket.dev/love to see for yourself!)


Founded by Feross Aboukhadijeh https://www.linkedin.com/in/feross/, a long-time open source maintainer with software downloaded over a billion times a month, Socket has raised $ https://socket.dev/blog/series-b125M in funding https://socket.dev/blog/series-c from top angels, operators, and security leaders.



About the Role

Socket is looking for a Manager, Sales Engineering to lead the team that helps security and engineering buyers understand our product, validate its value, and confidently choose Socket.

Our buyers are technical. They expect clear answers, credible demonstrations, and evaluations grounded in their actual workflows; not generic pitches. You'll coach Sales Engineers to connect software supply chain security to customer priorities, partner closely with Sales leadership, and build a repeatable technical sales motion that scales without relying on a few people to rescue every deal.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You'll hire and develop strong SEs, improve discovery and proof-of-concept execution, and join strategic customer conversations when your experience can change the outcome. Success means your team gets stronger and more independent, not that every difficult deal needs you in the room.



What You'll Do

 - Lead, coach, and grow a regional SE team. Implement Socket’s established hiring, onboarding, development, and performance-management practices, and help drive adoption within Socket’s framework and standards. Run interview loops and help close strong candidates against the established hiring bar.

 - Partner with Sales leaders and AEs on deal strategy, qualification, coverage, and prioritization. Help the team earn the technical win while Sales owns the commercial close.

 - Implement a consistent evaluation motion: agreed success criteria, customer owners, timelines, technical risk tracking, and documented outcomes.

 - Inspect strategic deals and stalled evaluations. Identify the real blocker, coach the SE, and escalate product or implementation gaps with clear context.

 - Stay technical enough to support demos, integrations, and complex customer conversations, and turn what works into reusable demos, playbooks, and onboarding.

 - Be the voice of the field to Product and Engineering, and partner with TAMs and Customer Success on clean pre-to-post-sales handoffs.

 - Report on the metrics that matter: technical win rate, POC durations, POC starts, quota attainment. Find what’s not working and create informed strategies for improvement.



What You'll Bring

Required: 

 - 7+ years as a Sales or Solutions Engineer and 2+ years directly managing SEs, including hiring and ramping them

 - Experience leading technical sales for commercial or enterprise customers, from discovery through demos, POCs, and technical validation, selling to developers and security teams

 - A track record of improving team performance through specific coaching and operating changes, not by taking over difficult deals

 - Credibility in a technical conversation: CI/CD, package managers, the open source ecosystem, and how developers work, plus comfort with Linux and scripting in a language like Python or JavaScript

 - Experience building or materially improving pre-sales systems such as evaluation frameworks, coverage models, demo standards, or onboarding

 - Experience managing through growth at a startup where process and resources were still evolving

 - Strong partnership with Sales leadership: you prioritize support, challenge weak qualification constructively, and separate technical validation from close probability

 - Clear communication with practitioners, CISOs, engineering leaders, and executives

 - Willingness to travel up to 25%

Preferred: 

 - Experience in software supply chain security, AppSec, DevSecOps, or SCA

 - Experience managing SEs across more than one segment

 - Practical use of automation and AI tools to improve SE productivity, with sound judgment about accuracy and customer data



Our Interview Process

 1. Phone Screen with our Talent Team

 2. Virtual f2f with the Hiring Manager

 3. Virtual f2f with a few members of the team

 4. Presentation

 5. Final call with our Founder

 6. References

 7. Offer

Hiring is a big decision on both sides. Read more about our Hiring Philosophy  https://socket.dev/hiring-philosophyand how we approach the process at Socket.



Benefits: Our benefits are crafted to support you and your family, so you can take care of what matters most and thrive in and outside of work. We offer:

 - Market competitive salary bands

 - Meaningful equity program

 - Comprehensive health benefits for you and your family (99% coverage)

 - Flexible time-off, holidays, and winter shutdown to rest & recharge

 - Paid parental leave

 - Remote-first, with quarterly team off-sites 



At Socket, we

 1. Pursue Excellence: We set ourselves apart by consistently delivering work of exceptional quality and distinction.

 2. Move with urgency and focus: We prioritize swift, decisive action.

 3. Think rigorously: We care about being right and it often takes reasoning from first principles to get there. We value alternative perspectives and have constructive discussions.

 4. Trust and amplify: We overtrust, always assume good intent, and give specific feedback to help each other improve.

 5. Feel a strong sense of ownership: We wear many hats and feel a strong sense of overall ownership of the company and we're non-territorial regarding our nominal domains.

 6. Are customer obsessed: We relentlessly prioritize the needs of our customers, striving to exceed their expectations and delight them at every interaction.

jobs.title: Principal Designer
jobs.description:
The Trade Desk is a global technology company and the world’s leading independent platform for digital advertising, with over 3,000 employees across more than 30 offices. Our technology helps advertisers reach the right audiences across the open internet — from streaming TV and podcasts to mobile apps, news, and more.

Advertising powers the content people love. By making it more transparent, effective, and responsible, we help support trusted journalism, quality entertainment, and creators worldwide. The world’s brands and agencies rely on us to reach their customers and grow their businesses responsibly.

The scale of our platform brings unique technical challenges — from processing massive datasets in real time to building systems that operate reliably on a global scale. When you work here, your impact is worldwide. We welcome diverse perspectives, encourage curiosity, and build teams that learn from one another. If you’re driven to solve meaningful challenges, we’d love to meet you.

What We Do

The Trade Desk is seeking a Principal Design Lead to own and evolve our Digital Playbook and to modernize how our design practice works. Partnering closely with Product, Product Marketing, and Brand, you will set a best-in-class standard for how our platform looks, feels, and evolves.

This is a senior individual-contributor design leadership role for someone who can see around corners on where our product language and platform experience need to go, and who can take that vision from concept through shipped, polished product. You will guide the evolution of our design language and systems so they stay cohesive and scalable as the platform grows and AI reshapes what advertisers and agency partners expect.

You bring deep, hands-on fluency with AI tools and use them to change how design gets done: faster exploration, tighter design-to-build handoff, and higher craft. You will help evolve our workflows, standards, and practices as we modernize, and you will work in lockstep with the design lead driving AI experience vision so the Playbook and product language support AI-powered capabilities consistently across the platform.

You are adept at product and brand integration, storytelling, and visual design, and you can bridge these domains to accelerate our product language and evolution.

This role reports to the Senior Director of UX Design and is a core leader of the UX team’s impact.

What You Will Be Doing

As Principal Design Lead at The Trade Desk, you will:

Own & Evolve the Digital Playbook

• Define, maintain, and evolve the Digital Playbook, including design foundations, style guide, component anatomy, and the guidance that connects them, as the source of truth for how our product and brand show up across the platform

• Set the standards and principles that help teams design with consistency, clarity, and craft

• Keep the Playbook a living resource: adopted in daily work, responsive to product change, and measurable in its impact on quality and speed

• Translate ambiguous product and brand needs into clear, usable guidance that teams can apply with confidence

Partner on Core Platform Evolution

• Work in close partnership with the Director leading Core Platform Evolution to ensure the Playbook and the platform’s direction evolve together

• Guide the evolution of our product design language as the platform grows, helping unify the experience, reduce fragmentation, and close quality gaps

• Identify shared patterns and align teams on best practices, raising the bar for coherence and usability across the product suite

• Lead hands-on, high-fidelity design of foundational elements, from early concept through detailed specification and adoption

Define the Modern Design System

• Help define what a modern design system is at The Trade Desk: how it is structured, how it scales, and how it supports both designers and builders

• Partner with our Design Technologist to bridge design and code, ensuring foundations, anatomy, and patterns translate cleanly into the product

• Shape how the system evolves alongside the Playbook so guidance, components, and implementation stay in sync

Bridge Product, Brand & Storytelling

• Partner with Product Marketing and Brand to integrate brand expression into the product in a way that feels intentional, distinctive, and consistent

• Build a shared visual and narrative language that connects what we say about The Trade Desk with how the platform looks and feels

• Present vision and direction to senior leadership with compelling storytelling that aligns stakeholders and accelerates decisions

Partner on the AI Experience

• Collaborate with the design lead for AI experience to translate their vision into consistent patterns, standards, and guidance within the Playbook

• Ensure the product language, components, and visual conventions support AI-powered capabilities (assistive, predictive, generative, and agentic) in a cohesive, trustworthy way

• Contribute to cross-functional conversations with Product, Engineering, and Data Science to keep platform standards and AI capabilities evolving together

Champion AI-Native Ways of Working

• Model hands-on use of AI tools in exploration, prototyping, craft, and design-to-build handoff, and share what works across teams

• Help evolve design, product, and engineering workflows so teams move faster and with higher quality

• Bring a strong point of view on where AI accelerates the work and where human judgment must stay in the loop

• Establish standards and practices that make AI-enabled workflows repeatable across the design organization

Elevate Craft & Mentor Design Talent

• Set the craft standard for visual and interaction design across the UX organization

• Provide critique and design direction that helps teams apply the Playbook and raise the quality of their work

• Mentor designers on systems thinking, visual craft, storytelling, and AI-enabled ways of working

• Lead by example through visible, hands-on work, fostering a culture where design quality is everyone’s responsibility

Represent TTD’s Design Point of View

• Share perspective on design modernization, product brand integration, and AI-enabled design practice at industry events and in the broader design community

• Position TTD as a company at the forefront of cohesive, modern, customer-centered product design in adtech

What You Bring to the Table

You are an experienced design leader with a track record of shaping the look, feel, and coherence of complex products. You combine strong visual and systems craft with product sense, brand sensibility, and genuine fluency in how AI is changing the way design gets done. You are energized by ambiguity, driven by user outcomes, and skilled at turning emerging tools and technology into practices and experiences that feel clear, confident, and human.

• Bachelor’s degree in Design, HCI, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience (Master’s preferred)

• 10+ years of experience in product design or UX design, including work on enterprise-grade or data-rich applications

• 4+ years leading high-impact design initiatives or strategic projects across teams or product areas

• Proven track record owning or evolving a design language, style guide, design system, or playbook that teams adopt at scale

• Strong visual and interaction design skills, with a portfolio demonstrating high standards of craft, clarity, and user-centered problem solving. Please include a viewable link or access instructions with your resume.

• Experience integrating brand and product, with the ability to partner effectively with Product Marketing and Brand teams

• Deep, hands-on fluency with AI tools for design exploration, prototyping, and workflow, with examples of how you have changed the way a team works

• Strong command of Figma and modern prototyping tools, used for fast, high-fidelity exploration at multiple levels of fidelity

• Experience partnering with design technologists or engineers to connect design foundations to implementation

• Exceptional communication and storytelling skills, with strong executive presence and experience presenting vision and direction to senior leadership

• Experience working in cross-functional teams, influencing outcomes through collaboration, systems thinking, and storytelling

• Ability to navigate ambiguity and drive clarity and alignment in complex, fast-moving environments

• Familiarity with how AI-powered experiences are designed, including patterns for trust, explainability, and error handling (preferred)

• Familiarity with advertising technology, programmatic platforms, or campaign optimization tools (preferred)

• Published thought leadership, talks, or case studies on design systems, design modernization, or AI-enabled design practice (preferred)

Why This Role Matters

At The Trade Desk, we design powerful, enterprise-grade tools that give advertisers and agencies extraordinary power to describe and reach their target audiences. As the platform evolves and AI becomes a defining layer of how customers plan, optimize, and decide, the experience has to feel like one product with one voice.

How cohesive, confident, and modern that experience feels is a design problem before it is a technology problem. The Digital Playbook is how we make it real: a shared standard that connects product, brand, and the way our teams work.

As Principal Design Lead, you will own that standard, modernize how our design practice operates, and help ensure every part of the platform reflects the quality our customers expect. If you are energized by the intersection of design craft, product and brand integration, and the way AI is transforming how great design gets made, this is your role.

The Trade Desk does not accept unsolicited resumes from search firm recruiters. Fees will not be paid in the event a candidate submitted by a recruiter without an agreement in place is hired; such resumes will be deemed the sole property of The Trade Desk. The Trade Desk is an equal opportunity employer. All aspects of employment will be based on merit, competence, performance, and business needs. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, marital status, age, national origin, ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, pregnancy, genetic information, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other status protected under federal, state, or local law.

[LA JOBS ONLY] The Trade Desk will consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment in a manner consistent with the requirements of the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring, Ordinance No. 184652.

[SF JOBS ONLY] Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

In accordance with various US state laws, the range provided is the Trade Desk's reasonable estimate of the base compensation for this role. About You

You are a highly organized, detail-oriented, and proactive professional who thrives in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment. You anticipate needs, identify issues, and execute with precision. You bring consistency and rigor to accounting processes and ensure high-quality outputs. You communicate effectively with cross-functional stakeholders and are a natural collaborator within a finance team.

About the Role

You’ll ensure timely and accurate financial reporting, support audits, and partner across the organization to contribute to building scalable infrastructure aligned with long-term growth.

jobs.title: Clinical Navigator - PT (Shift:  8:30am - 5:30pm CT)
jobs.description:
About TailorCare

TailorCare is transforming the experience of specialty care. Our comprehensive care program takes a profoundly personal, evidence-based approach to improving patient outcomes for joint, back, and muscle conditions. By carefully assessing patients' symptoms, health histories, preferences, and goals with predictive data and the latest evidence-based guidelines, we help patients choose and navigate the most effective treatment pathway for them every step of the way.

TailorCare values the experiences and perspectives of individuals from all backgrounds. We are a highly collaborative, curious, and determined team passionate about scaling a high-growth start-up to improve the lives of those in pain. TailorCare is a remote-first company with our corporate office located in Nashville.

About the Role

The Clinical Navigator is a licensed Doctor of Physical Therapy responsible for delivering high-quality clinical navigation through both telephonic and video-based member interactions in a fast-paced, metrics-driven clinical operations environment. This role serves as the primary point of contact for members throughout their TailorCare journey, engaging members through outbound and inbound calls, virtual visits, and digital touchpoints to assess needs, build trust, drive participation, and support adherence to evidence-based care plans.

Success in this role requires a strong balance of clinical expertise, operational excellence, communication skills, and the ability to consistently meet engagement, productivity, quality, and member outcome goals. Clinical Navigators spend the majority of their workday actively engaging with members while leveraging technology, AI-enabled tools, predictive insights, and standardized workflows to personalize care, improve efficiency, and optimize outcomes.

The ideal candidate thrives in a high-volume virtual environment, is energized by member engagement, embraces innovation, and demonstrates accountability for both member outcomes and operational performance.

As TailorCare continues to evolve its clinical offerings, this role will play a foundational part in expanding virtual musculoskeletal care navigation. Clinical Navigators will help shape and support future virtual physical therapy programs, leveraging their clinical expertise to deliver increasingly comprehensive care experiences through digital and video-enabled platforms.

Primary Responsibilities

Member Engagement & Clinical Navigation

• Serve as the primary navigator for an assigned member population, managing members from intake through program completion in a contact center environment.

• Conduct comprehensive clinical intake assessments to evaluate MSK conditions, functional limitations, treatment history, goals, and readiness for care.

• Deliver clinical navigation through both telephonic and video-based interactions, selecting the most effective engagement modality to support member needs and outcomes.

• Maintain a high volume of daily member interactions through outbound and inbound outreach while delivering a personalized, empathetic, and clinically sound experience.

• Build trust and engagement through motivational interviewing, behavioral coaching, and evidence-based communication techniques.

• Educate members on treatment options, clinical recommendations, and available resources to support informed decision-making.

• Proactively follow up with members to drive adherence, address barriers to care, reinforce treatment plans, and improve engagement outcomes.

• Monitor member progress and identify opportunities for intervention, escalation, or additional support.

• Act as a trusted advocate throughout the member journey, ensuring continuity of care and a seamless member experience.

• Support the evolution of TailorCare’s virtual care capabilities by participating in the development, implementation, and future delivery of virtual physical therapy services and digital MSK care programs.

Operational Excellence & Performance

• Consistently achieve established operational performance metrics, including member engagement targets, outreach productivity, call and video visit quality, follow-up completion rates, documentation accuracy, and care plan adherence metrics.

• Effectively manage daily workflows, outreach queues, and member caseloads while balancing quality and efficiency in a call center-like environment.

• Demonstrate strong time management, accountability, and discipline within a high-volume call center and virtual care environment.

• Maintain readiness and availability for scheduled member interactions throughout the workday.

• Utilize performance dashboards, reporting tools, and operational data to prioritize outreach activities and maximize member engagement.

• Embrace continuous improvement initiatives and adapt quickly to evolving workflows, processes, technologies, and organizational priorities.

Technology, AI & Innovation

• Leverage AI-powered tools, predictive analytics, automation, and workflow technologies to enhance member interactions and improve operational efficiency.

• Utilize clinical decision-support tools and data-driven recommendations to personalize engagement strategies and support evidence-based care navigation.

• Identify opportunities to improve workflows, member experiences, and operational effectiveness through innovative thinking and feedback.

• Maintain proficiency across multiple technology platforms, communication tools, telehealth systems, CRMs, and documentation systems.

• Contribute to the adoption and optimization of emerging technologies that support scalable, high-quality clinical navigation and virtual care delivery.

Care Coordination & Collaboration

• Collaborate closely with interdisciplinary care teams, providers, health plan partners, and internal stakeholders to ensure a coordinated and seamless member experience.

• Communicate timely updates regarding member progress, barriers, escalations, and clinical concerns.

• Escalate complex clinical or operational issues appropriately while maintaining ownership of the member experience.

• Partner with colleagues across Clinical Operations, Product, Technology, and Provider Success teams to continuously improve the member journey.

• Contribute to a collaborative team culture through knowledge sharing, peer support, and participation in team meetings, training initiatives, and workflow improvement efforts.

Documentation & Compliance

• Accurately document all member interactions, assessments, care plans, and outreach efforts within established timelines.

• Ensure compliance with clinical protocols, quality standards, documentation requirements, and organizational policies.

• Maintain confidentiality and adhere to all applicable regulatory requirements and professional standards.

• Other duties as assigne

Qualifications

Required

• Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT) or Masters in Physical Therapy (MPT)

• Current unrestricted Physical Therapy license in Georgia, Texas, Colorado and/or Indiana (Compact License preferred).

• Willingness to obtain and maintain additional state licenses as TailorCare expands.

• Minimum 3 years of experience in physical therapy, musculoskeletal care, care navigation, telehealth, or related clinical settings.

• Demonstrated success managing patient interactions in high-volume, performance-oriented environments.

• Strong communication, motivational interviewing, and patient engagement skills.

• Experience utilizing technology and data to improve workflow efficiency and patient outcomes.

• Ability to work independently while maintaining accountability to productivity, engagement, and quality expectations.

• Comfortable working across multiple technology platforms, communication tools, and dual-monitor environments.

• Ability and willingness to travel up to 10% as needed for onsite meetings, team collaboration, and company events.

Preferred

• Experience in telephonic care navigation, virtual care, care management, population health, utilization management, or digital health environments.

• Experience working within a call center, contact center, or metrics-driven healthcare operations setting.

• Familiarity with AI-enabled clinical tools, workflow automation, and digital health technologies.

• Experience in value-based care, employer-sponsored healthcare programs, or population health initiatives.

• Experience in high-growth startup environments.

• Bilingual - Spanish/English

Skills

• Member Engagement & Relationship Building

• High-Volume Telephonic & Video-Based Communication

• Motivational Interviewing & Behavior Change Coaching

• Clinical Assessment & Care Planning

• Operational Excellence & Productivity Management

• Data-Driven Decision Making

• Virtual Care Delivery & Telehealth Excellence

• AI & Technology Utilization

• Adaptability & Continuous Improvement

• Cross-Functional Collaboration

• Accountability & Results Orientation

Pay Range

$87,500—$90,000 USD

What's In It For You

• Meaningful Work: We are dedicated to our mission and deeply value our patients and each other. Each day offers the opportunity to make a positive impact.

• Work Environment: We operate as a remote-first company with options for a hybrid work model in Nashville.

• Time Off: Our generous paid time off (PTO) and holiday plans ensure you have ample time to rest and recharge.

• Family First: We offer paid parental leave and support a healthy work-life balance, encouraging flexibility and autonomy. We love talking about our family and pets!

• Comprehensive Benefits: From Day 1, employees enjoy medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance, wellness resources and an employer HSA contribution.

• Fair Compensation: We are committed to equitable pay for all team members and support your future goals with a 401k plan that includes employer matching.

• Community: We foster an inclusive environment where you can rely on your teammates, share honest feedback, and feel comfortable being your authentic self at work each day.

TailorCare seeks to recruit and retain staff from diverse backgrounds and encourages qualified candidates to apply. TailorCare is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of age, sex, gender identity/expression, sexual orientation, color, race, creed, national origin, ancestry, religion, marital status, political belief, physical or mental disability, pregnancy, military, or veteran status.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, AI Training - United States
jobs.description:
Contract | Remote, worldwide | $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location | 10-20 hrs/week



Please note that eligibility may vary depending on your location, as some regions may not be supported by the client.


Check out this Loom video for more details: https://www.loom.com/share/b0d1b0bf24c44ae8b95dca84b9db60e5



We're looking for highly experienced software engineer (SR+) to help evaluate the quality of interactions with modern coding agents such as OpenAI Codex and Claude Code.



This is not a traditional engineering role. You won't be writing production code. You'll be evaluating something harder: whether the model thinks like a great engineer.




WHAT THIS ROLE ACTUALLY IS

You will assess how AI coding agents behave in real-world scenarios, focusing on:

• Whether the response makes sense

• Whether the preamble and reasoning are useful

• Whether the output reflects strong engineering judgment

• Whether the interaction feels right to an experienced developer

This role is about engineering taste. Syntax correctness is the easy part.




WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

• Evaluate AI-generated coding interactions end to end

• Judge whether outputs are useful, correct at a high level, and aligned with how a strong engineer would think

• Assess the quality of explanations and reasoning, not just the code

• Distinguish between levels of response quality (what makes something a 2 vs a 4)

• Give clear, opinionated feedback in writing on what worked, what didn't, and what felt off or misleading

• Help define what great looks like when working with tools like Cursor, Codex and Claude Code




WHAT WE MEAN BY "TASTE"

We're looking for engineers who can answer questions like:

• Does this feel like something a strong engineer would actually say?

• Is this explanation helpful, or just technically correct?

• Is the model guiding the user well, or just dumping output?

• Would this interaction build or erode trust?

You should be comfortable making subjective but rigorous judgments, and explaining them clearly.




WHO YOU ARE

• Senior, Staff or Principal-level engineer (or equivalent experience)

• Strong background in TypeScript/JavaScript or Python

• Hands-on experience with at least one of OpenAI Codex, Claude Code or Cursor

• Deep familiarity with modern AI-assisted dev workflows

• Able to evaluate code without executing it or reviewing every line

• Strong written and spoken English (B2 or above). You'll be writing detailed feedback and recording short video explanations, so this is a hard requirement

• Comfortable giving direct, opinionated feedback

• High bar for what good engineering looks like




NICE TO HAVE

• Prior exposure to prompt design or evaluation workflows

• Experience mentoring senior engineers or defining engineering standards




ENGAGEMENT DETAILS

• Rate: $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location

• Hours: 10-20 hours/week, flexible

• Duration: ongoing. Projects run from about two weeks to a few months each, and we offer new ones to evaluators who do well

• Start: as soon as you clear the take-home and a project has an open seat

• Process: one take-home evaluation exercise with a recorded Loom walkthrough. No interview

jobs.title: Senior Director, Clinical Operations
jobs.description:
About TailorCare

TailorCare is transforming the experience of specialty care. Our comprehensive care program takes a profoundly personal, evidence-based approach to improving patient outcomes for joint, back, and muscle conditions. By carefully assessing patients' symptoms, health histories, preferences, and goals with predictive data and the latest evidence-based guidelines, we help patients choose and navigate the most effective treatment pathway for them every step of the way.

About the Role

The Senior Director, Clinical Operations owns the performance, scalability, and operational direction of TailorCare's clinical operations, spanning both the Clinical Navigation team and the business operations that keep it running and connected across the care journey. This is a senior leadership role for a strong operator: someone with advanced business acumen who can build and run an operations function at scale, set and own the team's OKRs, and drive it toward measurable targets.

This leader owns the contact center operations for their team, including staffing, forecasting, scheduling, queue and service-level management, and escalation, and partners closely with the Central Operations and Performance Excellence teams on the shared infrastructure and standards behind it. Beyond running the day-to-day operation, the role owns the business operations that keep the team performing and shape how it connects with other teams across the care journey.

This leader brings strong business and operational acumen and sets the strategic direction for their own team, while partnering closely with the Sr. Director, Performance & Strategy and the Director, Clinical Digital Solutions on broader clinical strategy and digital innovation. The role also reaches across functions outside Clinical Operations to keep the patient journey continuous from end to end. The ideal candidate is a proven operator who can build and scale, and candidates who bring both operational depth and clinical fluency are especially welcome.

Primary Responsibilities

Operational Strategy & OKR Ownership  (20%)

• Set, own, and cascade the OKRs for the team; translate functional strategy into operating plans and drive the team to hit measurable targets.

• Own the strategy and operational direction for the Clinical Navigation operation, including the business operations that support it and its connections across the care journey, with direct accountability for the success or failure of its business objectives.

• Set the strategic vision and direction for the team, and shape the longer-term operating model as TailorCare scales, influencing senior leadership on where the function needs to go.

• Hold budget accountability for the function and make resourcing and prioritization decisions with a high degree of autonomy.

• Drive cross-functional collaboration between Digital Solutions and Clinical Strategy to innovate, validate, and operationalize new clinical models — ensuring strong clinical outcomes and informing the discovery and scope of future digital solutions.

Contact Center Operations  (25%)

• Own end-to-end operational performance of the team's contact center: staffing models, forecasting, capacity planning, scheduling, and real-time queue management.

• Set and monitor service-level standards (speed to answer, average handle time, abandonment rate, outreach productivity) alongside clinical quality standards, ensuring neither is sacrificed for the other.

• Build and maintain escalation pathways for complex clinical or operational issues, with clear ownership and timely resolution.

• Partner with the Central Operations and Performance Excellence teams on the shared backbone the contact center runs on, including the workforce management platform and contact-center tooling, quality, and audits, consuming that infrastructure rather than standing up a duplicate of it.

Business Operations & Care Journey Integration  (20%)

• Own the business operations that keep the team performing: operating rhythm, capacity and workforce planning, SOP execution, and readiness for new market and payer launches.

• Own how the operation connects with other teams across the care journey, ensuring smooth handoffs and a continuous experience for the patient.

• Own the team's technology stack in partnership with IT/Product and the Director, Clinical Digital Solutions, including dialer/CRM, telehealth platforms, and documentation systems, and pilot and scale AI-enabled tools and digital workflows within the operation.

• Ensure compliance with clinical protocols, documentation standards, and regulatory requirements across all operational touchpoints, partnering with Compliance, Legal, and Quality to maintain governance and audit-readiness.

People & Organizational Leadership  (20%)

• Directly manage and develop the managers who lead the Clinical Navigation and care teams across markets and payers, ensuring consistent leadership practices, coaching quality, and accountability standards.

• Indirectly lead the broader Clinical Navigation organization, including Navigators, Senior Navigators, and Lead Navigators, by setting standards, reviewing outcomes, and holding managers accountable for team-level execution.

• Own workforce management and succession planning across the Clinical Navigation career ladder, and coach managers on how to coach so quality scales with headcount.

• Mentor and develop emerging leaders across the function, a defining expectation of this role, building a deliberate leadership pipeline in partnership with the management team.

Performance, Data & Cross-Functional Partnership  (15%)

• Own the KPI framework connecting operational performance (engagement, adherence, productivity, service levels) to clinical outcomes and business impact (utilization, medical cost savings, quality).

• Build and maintain dashboards that give managers and executive leadership real-time visibility into team and program performance, and ensure metrics roll up cleanly into enterprise OKRs and client-facing reporting.

• Partner with the Analytics team and the Sr. Director, Performance & Strategy to root-cause performance gaps and translate insights into operational change.

• Represent clinical operations in client conversations, executive briefings, and cross-functional planning, and partner with teams across the care journey to keep the end-to-end patient experience continuous.

• Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree (MBA, MHA, or related) preferred.

• 10+ years of progressive experience in healthcare or clinical operations, contact/call center leadership, or business operations, including within value-based care, digital health, or population health settings.

• 5+ years leading leaders (managing managers or multi-layered teams), with a demonstrated track record of driving organizational change.

• Advanced business and operational acumen: a proven operator with the ability to build and run an operations function to measurable targets, own OKRs, and drive teams to hit them. This is the core requirement for the role.

• Demonstrated experience running a high-volume, telephonic/virtual contact-center-style operation, including staffing, forecasting, capacity planning, and service-level management.

• Experience owning a budget and making resourcing and prioritization decisions with significant autonomy.

• Strong data and analytics acumen; comfortable building and using dashboards to manage both people performance and business outcomes.

• Experience translating operational KPIs into business and clinical impact (utilization, cost of care, quality metrics).

• Active clinical licensure (PT, RN, or equivalent) is a plus, not required. The priority is a proven business operator, and candidates who bring both an operations background and clinical fluency are especially welcome.

• Proficiency with workforce management, CRM, and EHR/documentation systems; strong Excel and dashboarding tool skills (Tableau or similar).

• Excellent communication skills, with a track record of leading through influence across clinical and non-clinical, internal and executive audiences.

• Comfortable operating in ambiguity and scaling systems within a fast-growing startup environment.

• Ability and willingness to travel up to 10% as needed for onsite meetings, team collaboration, and company events.

Skills

• Leadership of leaders: building manager capability, not just individual performance

• Cross-functional collaboration and influence (Central Operations, Performance Excellence, Performance & Strategy, Clinical Digital Solutions, Product, Data, Compliance)

• Change management and process design at scale

What's In It For You

• Meaningful Work: We are dedicated to our mission and deeply value our patients and each other. Each day offers the opportunity to make a positive impact.

• Work Environment: We operate as a remote-first company with options for a hybrid work model in Nashville.

• Whether the preamble and reasoning are useful

• Whether the output reflects strong engineering judgment

• Whether the interaction feels right to an experienced developer

This role is about engineering taste. Syntax correctness is the easy part.




WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

• Evaluate AI-generated coding interactions end to end

• Judge whether outputs are useful, correct at a high level, and aligned with how a strong engineer would think

• Assess the quality of explanations and reasoning, not just the code

• Distinguish between levels of response quality (what makes something a 2 vs a 4)

• Give clear, opinionated feedback in writing on what worked, what didn't, and what felt off or misleading

• Help define what great looks like when working with tools like Cursor, Codex and Claude Code




WHAT WE MEAN BY "TASTE"

We're looking for engineers who can answer questions like:

• Does this feel like something a strong engineer would actually say?

• Is this explanation helpful, or just technically correct?

• Is the model guiding the user well, or just dumping output?

• Would this interaction build or erode trust?

You should be comfortable making subjective but rigorous judgments, and explaining them clearly.




WHO YOU ARE

• Senior, Staff or Principal-level engineer (or equivalent experience)

• Strong background in TypeScript/JavaScript or Python

• Hands-on experience with at least one of OpenAI Codex, Claude Code or Cursor

• Deep familiarity with modern AI-assisted dev workflows

• Able to evaluate code without executing it or reviewing every line

• Strong written and spoken English (B2 or above). You'll be writing detailed feedback and recording short video explanations, so this is a hard requirement

• Comfortable giving direct, opinionated feedback

• High bar for what good engineering looks like




NICE TO HAVE

• Prior exposure to prompt design or evaluation workflows

• Experience mentoring senior engineers or defining engineering standards




ENGAGEMENT DETAILS

• Rate: $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location

• Hours: 10-20 hours/week, flexible

• Duration: ongoing. Projects run from about two weeks to a few months each, and we offer new ones to evaluators who do well

• Start: as soon as you clear the take-home and a project has an open seat

• Process: one take-home evaluation exercise with a recorded Loom walkthrough. No interview
