jobs.title: Senior Delivery Manager
jobs.description:
About Us

Chorus Innovations is a fast-growing healthcare technology company with an adaptive platform as a service (PaaS) that enables the rapid development of mobile, desktop, text messaging and interactive voice applications. Chorus’ platform currently powers transformative healthcare, biomedical research and community health projects across institutions and public health agencies nationwide. We believe every community should have world-class health technology so they can thrive.

Our mission is to improve the lives of people and communities by democratizing technology development in health and research.

About the Role

The Senior Delivery Manager is responsible for driving complex healthcare technology implementations from early discovery through go-live and stabilization. This role sits at the center of client delivery and is expected to bring structure, urgency, and clarity to work that often starts out ambiguous.

You will serve as the operational owner across assigned accounts, partnering closely with clients, Product, Design, Engineering, Data, Clinical Solutions, and SLT. Your job is to turn scope, client priorities, discovery outputs, and technical inputs into a clear delivery path that teams can execute against. That means owning the plan, surfacing risks early, driving decisions, and making sure the right people are engaged at the right moments.

This is not a passive project tracking role. A successful Delivery Manager at Chorus actively leads delivery forward by shaping requirements, coordinating discovery and design, ensuring backlog readiness, managing governance, and preparing teams and clients for launch. You will be expected to create momentum, reduce churn, and ensure delivery stays aligned to scope, quality, timeline, and client outcomes.

What You’ll Be Doing

Client & Account Ownership

• Serve as the day-to-day delivery owner for assigned client accounts, ensuring clear visibility into priorities, status, risks, blockers, decisions, and next steps.

• Own the operational rhythm of the account, including internal account team meetings, client delivery updates, RAID management, milestone tracking, and escalations.

• Build trust with client stakeholders through clear communication, follow-through, and thoughtful expectation management.

• Ensure client commitments are tracked against scope, timeline, budget, and delivery capacity.

Discovery, Design & Requirements Leadership

• Lead and coordinate discovery sessions with the appropriate Product, Design, Engineering, Data, Clinical, and client stakeholders.

• Ensure discovery produces usable outputs, including workflow decisions, process flows, business rules, requirements, open questions, and follow-up actions.

• Partner with Product and Design to move from client input to validated requirements, concepts, designs, and implementation-ready artifacts.

• Identify gaps in workflows, requirements, edge cases, dependencies, data needs, and operational assumptions before work enters development.

• Drive documented alignment or written sign-off on key requirements and design decisions when needed.

Scope-to-Delivery Planning

• Translate contractual scope, product requirements, and client priorities into a sequenced delivery plan.

• Partner with Product, Engineering, and leadership to validate feasibility, sequencing, dependencies, and delivery capacity.

• Create and maintain delivery plans, milestone views, Gantt charts, delivery health updates, and executive-ready summaries as needed.

• Proactively surface misalignment between contracted scope, sales commitments, product readiness, engineering capacity, and client expectations

Delivery Governance & Execution

• Establish and maintain strong governance across assigned accounts, including RAID logs, decision logs, action trackers, recurring cadences, and escalation paths.

• Track delivery health across timeline, budget, scope, quality, dependencies, risks, and resource needs.

• Identify risks and blockers early, assess impact, drive mitigation plans, and escalate with clear recommendations.

• Ensure internal teams understand what is being delivered, why it matters, what is blocked, and what decisions are needed.

Backlog & Readiness Management

• Partner with Product Managers, Technical Leads, and Engineering teams to translate client-specific work into a healthy and prioritized backlog.

• Support refinement of epics, user stories, acceptance criteria, test considerations, dependencies, and sequencing.

• Ensure tickets meet the agreed definition of ready before entering development.

• Help prevent churn by identifying unclear requirements, missing decisions, or incomplete handoffs before sprint work begins.

Cross-Functional Coordination

• Align the right contributors across Product, Design, Engineering, Data, QA, Clinical Solutions, Client Success, and leadership.

• Facilitate structured handoffs across discovery, design, build, testing, UAT, launch, and hypercare.

• Drive follow-through by clarifying ownership, documenting decisions, and ensuring next steps are visible and actionable.

• Serve as the connective tissue between client needs, product direction, technical execution, and operational delivery.

Launch Readiness, UAT & Hypercare

• Own delivery readiness for UAT, launch, go-live, and post-launch stabilization.

• Coordinate UAT planning, test scenarios, client validation, defect triage, launch checklists, training readiness, operational handoffs, and hypercare support.

• Partner with Product, QA, Engineering, and client teams to ensure issues are tracked, prioritized, resolved, and communicated clearly.

• Drive post-launch retrospectives and incorporate lessons learned into future delivery practices.

Delivery Standards & Continuous Improvement

• Contribute to Chorus delivery playbooks, templates, operating rhythms, and standards.

• Help standardize practices for discovery, requirements validation, backlog readiness, RAID management, executive reporting, UAT, launch, and hypercare.

• Identify process gaps across the delivery lifecycle and help implement practical improvements that increase clarity, accountability, and consistency.

What We’re Looking For

• 5+ years of experience in delivery management, project management, implementation leadership, client delivery, or consulting within a technology, healthcare, public sector, or SaaS environment.

• Proven experience managing complex, multi-stakeholder software implementations from planning through launch.

• Strong ability to lead cross-functional teams through ambiguity, competing priorities, and evolving client needs.

• Experience translating scope, requirements, designs, and technical inputs into actionable delivery plans.

• Demonstrated ability to manage timelines, milestones, risks, dependencies, decisions, and executive-level delivery updates.

• Strong client-facing communication skills, with the ability to create clarity, manage expectations, and escalate risks thoughtfully.

• Experience working with Product, Design, Engineering, QA, Data, and business stakeholders to move work from discovery through delivery.

• Familiarity with agile delivery practices, sprint planning, backlog refinement, and associated tooling. i.e. Jira.

• Structured, proactive, detail-oriented, and comfortable bringing order to ambiguity.

• Strong judgment and ownership mindset, with the ability to identify what needs to happen next and drive it forward.

• Background in user acceptance testing, go-live planning, training coordination, launch readiness, and hypercare delivery.

Nice to Have

• Experience working in public health, behavioral health, Medicaid, government technology, or healthcare delivery environments.

• Understanding of healthcare workflows, care coordination, referrals, assessments, case management, crisis response, EHRs, interoperability, or data migration concepts.

• Experience supporting enterprise or public-sector clients with complex governance structures and multiple stakeholder groups.

• Experience with contract-to-scope mapping, implementation planning, resource forecasting, budget tracking, or utilization management.

• Ability to create executive-ready delivery summaries, portfolio views, dashboards, and operational health reports.

• Experience improving delivery operations, creating playbooks, or standardizing delivery processes across multiple accounts or teams.

Why Join Us?

• A mission-driven company – be part of a team that is helping to improve people’s lives by democratizing technology development in health!

• Full medical, dental, vision and life insurance benefits

• 401K plan

• Company stock options

• Unlimited paid vacation

• Performance bonuses

• Company support for career and skill development

• Fun company events and outings

• Chorus is an equal opportunity employer with a commitment to diversity and inclusion

Compensation Disclosure
The anticipated base salary range for this position is $120,000 – $135,000 in the Los Angeles market. Actual offers depend on skills, experience, and location, and may include additional components such as performance bonuses, stock options, and benefits.

Chorus Innovations is proud to be an equal-opportunity employer committed to building a diverse team. We welcome applicants of every background and provide reasonable
accommodations throughout the hiring process. If you need assistance, email careers@joinchorus.com

Chorus Innovations values diversity as a core principle of the work we do and the communities we serve.  We are committed to equal employment opportunity, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religious creed, citizenship, marital status, age, national origin, ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, sex, sexual orientation, military and veteran status, gender, gender identity, gender expression, or any other protected characteristic.

Disability Accommodation for Applicants to Chorus Innovations

At Chorus Innovations, we are committed to fostering an inclusive and accessible workplace environment for all individuals, including job applicants with disabilities. We recognize the value that individuals with diverse abilities bring to our organization and are dedicated to providing equal opportunities for all applicants.

If you require accommodations at any stage of the job application process due to a disability, please inform us of your needs. We will do our best to work with you to ensure that reasonable accommodations are made to facilitate your participation in the recruitment process.

Please note that accommodations will be provided in a manner that respects your privacy and confidentiality. Disclosing a disability or requesting accommodations will not affect your candidacy or opportunities for employment with Chorus Innovations.

To request accommodations or discuss your needs further, please contact careers@joinchorus.com. We encourage you to reach out as early as possible to ensure that appropriate arrangements can be made.

Thank you for considering Chorus Innovations as a potential employer. We look forward to the opportunity to work together and to creating an inclusive workplace where all individuals can thrive.

jobs.title: Events & Student Outreach Coordinator, Higher Ed
jobs.description:
EVENTS & STUDENT OUTREACH COORDINATOR

Open to Remote in EST or CST Locations




CLASP TALENT ABOUT US



Clasp is a mission-driven, venture-backed startup transforming access to education and career pathways—starting with the healthcare workforce. By enabling employers to invest in future talent where it matters most—easing overwhelming student debt—our platform creates lasting bonds between employers and employees. We believe that when employers have a stake in the cost of education, we can create a more sustainable, equitable, and skilled workforce.

Fresh off our Series B, we’re entering our next phase of growth. Clasp is a Forbes Fintech 50 company, an SHRM portfolio company, and has been named by Business Insider as one of the “Top 14 Healthcare Startups to Watch in 2026” and one of the “43 Startups to Bet Your Career On in 2025.” Most recently, our Loan-Linked Hiring solution was named to TIME’s Best Inventions of 2026 list.

We’re not just building a fintech product—we’re driving economic mobility. If you’re excited to build, grow, and make a real impact, join us.




WHAT WE NEED

Events are where we meet students and school partners face to face, and you’ll be the person who makes every one of them run smoothly. You’ll own the behind-the-scenes work that makes an event a success, from event selection and registration to shipping and calendar management, and making sure every lead we collect gets a timely, thoughtful follow-up. You’ll also pick up the phone and write to students directly, turning event momentum into real conversations about how Clasp can help them find a job with student loan repayment benefits. If you’re organized, energized by people, and love closing the loop, this is a great first step into a fast-growing team.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Research and identify events to attend, coordinating sponsorship, exhibition, and presentation opportunities based on ROI

 - Plan, coordinate, and manage team events from start to finish, including timelines, registration, travel and booth logistics, and budget tracking

 - Manage the team’s event calendar and keep everyone aligned on dates, owners, and deadlines

 - Ship event materials and order swag on time and on budget

 - Work with external vendors, sponsors, and event organizers, and represent Clasp professionally in every interaction, responding and following up in a timely manner

 - Capture and log leads from events and make sure each one is followed up on promptly; write and share event recaps covering attendance, leads, takeaways, and next steps

 - Run bulk marketing email and SMS outreach to our student database

 - Build and improve checklists and processes so every event is repeatable and maximizes ROI; track event and outreach results and work to improve conversion from event leads to applications

 - Travel to conferences and events to represent Clasp, and to team gatherings and company offsites

 - Conduct direct outreach to students, making up to 50 student calls per week plus personal email outreach
   
   


WHAT YOU’LL NEED

 - Experience coordinating events with multi-step logistics including vendor relationships, travel, and budget management

 - Comfort making outbound phone calls and writing clear, professional emails

 - Exceptional organization, attention to detail, and follow-through

 - Polished, professional communication, with the judgment to represent Clasp well with vendors, partners, and students, and the discipline to follow up quickly

 - Ability to work independently in a remote, fast-paced environment in the EST or CST time zone

 - Willingness and ability to travel for conferences, events, team gatherings, and company offsites

 - Experience with HubSpot, Notion, and Claude preferred, or comparable CRM, workspace, and AI tools

 - A genuine interest in education access and working with students

 - A plus: experience in field marketing, admissions, campus programming, or business development
   
   


WHAT WE GIVE IN RETURN

 - Competitive cash and equity compensation

 - Health benefits (health, dental, & vision), 401k

 - Commuter benefits

 - Flexible PTO policy

 - Opportunities to grow and perform in a fast-paced environment alongside a stellar team.
   
   


SALARY

The salary range for this position is competitive and will be commensurate with the candidate's experience, qualifications, and industry knowledge, ranging between $75,000 - $85,000 annually. In addition to the base salary, we offer an attractive equity component as part of our compensation package, providing an opportunity for eligible employees to share in the success and growth of our company. We are committed to offering competitive compensation and benefits packages to attract and retain top talent.




WORKING AT CLASP

Clasp is moving to a remote-first model in 2027. We've built our tools and norms to support flexible, focused work wherever you do your best thinking. To keep collaboration real-time, we hire team members based in the Eastern and Central time zones. Remote-first doesn't mean remote-only. We invest in intentional in-person time to strengthen relationships and stay connected to our mission. Team members should expect company-paid travel up to seven times per year, typically two to four days at a time, for team and company-wide gatherings, in addition to any role-specific travel.




WORK AUTHORIZATION

This role is not eligible for immigration sponsorship, now or in the future. Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States for any employer.




HOW WE USE AI IN HIRING

Clasp uses AI-assisted tools in parts of our hiring process, such as AI notetakers transcribing or summarizing interviews, scheduling, and supporting evaluation in technical assessments. Humans review applications and make every hiring decision. AI tools don't make final decisions about any candidate. You're welcome to use AI to research Clasp and prepare, but during live interviews and assessments we want to hear your own thinking, so please don't use AI tools that generate or feed you responses in real time. If you'd like to be evaluated without AI tools, need an accommodation, or have questions about how we use these tools, email recruiting@clasp.com and we'll arrange another process where we can.




CLOSING

If you are a highly driven individual with a passion for technology, and you thrive in a dynamic and fast-paced environment, we want to hear from you! Join us in revolutionizing the workforce solution industry and making a meaningful impact on businesses worldwide. Apply now to be a part of our growing team!



We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace where all employees feel valued, respected, and empowered to contribute their unique perspectives and talents. Clasp is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind. We embrace diversity and are dedicated to providing equal employment opportunities to all individuals regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Research Associate Intern
jobs.description:
A Rare Opportunity to Shape the Future of Genomics

Join a team of brilliant, passionate innovators determined to transform healthcare. At BillionToOne, we've built a category-defining, publicly traded company on Nasdaq where transparency fuels trust, collaboration drives breakthroughs, and every contribution moves the needle on our mission to make life-changing diagnostics accessible to all. We don't just aim for incremental improvements; we build products that are 10x better than anything that exists today.

Our scientists, engineers, sales executives, and visionaries are united by an unwavering commitment to changing the standard of care in prenatal and cancer diagnostics. This is where cutting-edge science meets human compassion, and every innovation you contribute helps remove the fear of the unknown from some of life's most critical medical moments.

If you're driven by purpose, energized by innovation, and ready to help shape the future of precision medicine at scale, this is where you belong.

The Research Associate Intern position at BillionToOne is exceptionally rare at the undergraduate or early-career level. At BillionToOne, you will do much more than simply run routine protocols. Your work will shape the development of high-impact molecular diagnostic products that are actively changing patient outcomes in both oncology and prenatal medicine. jobs.title: Order Quality Analyst
jobs.description:
At Tactile Medical, we specialize in developing at-home therapy devices to treat lymphedema, chronic venous insufficiency and respiratory illnesses.

Position Summary
The Order Quality Analyst evaluates the quality, accuracy, compliance, and integrity of patient orders throughout the order lifecycle. This role conducts holistic end-of-process audits before critical milestones, including prior authorization, claim submission, and patient or shipment readiness, and performs targeted quality control reviews at key process junctions to identify defects early and reduce rework. The analyst identifies system, process, data, and human performance issues and translates audit findings, trends, and root causes into actionable improvements across Order Excellence. As Tactile transitions to Salesforce, this role also supports the execution, monitoring, testing, and auditing of SOX-related controls to maintain a strong internal control environment and audit readiness.

Accountabilities & Responsibilities
• Conduct comprehensive end-to-end quality assurance audits of patient orders to validate accuracy, completeness, and compliance before prior authorization, claim submission, shipment readiness, and other defined release points.
• Perform targeted quality control reviews at critical points in the order lifecycle to identify defects, mitigate risk, and reduce downstream rework.
• Evaluate patient orders for adherence to standard operating procedures, payer requirements, regulatory standards, documentation requirements, and system workflow expectations.
• Identify and document system, process, data, and human errors that affect order quality, compliance, reimbursement, patient progression, or operational performance.
• Investigate root causes of quality defects and collaborate with operational leaders to identify corrective and preventive actions.
• Maintain audit results, quality scorecards, dashboards, and trend reports to identify recurring issues and improvement opportunities across teams, workflows, systems, and processes.
• Partner with Operational Excellence, Order Operations, Training, Compliance, IT, and Business Systems teams to improve process quality and operational execution.
• Support quality control checkpoints, participate in calibration activities, and validate corrective actions and process improvements through follow-up audits.
• Ensure compliance with HIPAA, regulatory requirements, company policies, and payer guidelines.
• Assist with testing and validation of new workflows, system enhancements, automation initiatives, and business process changes, and perform other duties as assigned.

SOX Controls & Compliance Responsibilities
• Support the execution, monitoring, and auditing of SOX controls related to order management and revenue-impacting processes within Salesforce and associated systems.
• Perform periodic control testing and validation to confirm adherence to documented control requirements.
• Maintain audit documentation that supports internal and external audit requests.
• Identify control deficiencies, process risks, and compliance gaps and partner with stakeholders to implement remediation plans.
• Collaborate with Compliance, Internal Audit, Finance, and Technology teams to support ongoing SOX compliance and audit readiness.
• Support the design and continuous improvement of operational and system controls associated with order processing, revenue recognition, and patient services workflows.
• Assist in developing and documenting control procedures, testing methodologies, and audit evidence requirements.

Additional Competencies
• Quality Assurance & Control
• Root Cause Analysis
• Risk Assessment & Mitigation
• Internal Controls and Compliance Management
• Audit Management
• Statistical & Trend Analysis
• Continuous Improvement
• Process Governance
• Systems Thinking

Role Purpose & Measures of Success
Success in this role is measured by reduced process defects and rework, improved first-time quality, stronger internal controls, increased compliance, successful audit outcomes, and improved order accuracy and patient progression throughout the end-to-end order lifecycle.

Qualifications
Required:
• Bachelor’s degree in business, healthcare administration, quality, finance, information systems, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
• Two or more years of experience in quality assurance, quality control, auditing, compliance, healthcare operations, order management, revenue cycle, or a related operational environment.
• Experience reviewing transactional or patient-order records for accuracy, completeness, adherence to documented procedures, and regulatory or payer requirements.
• Working knowledge of quality assurance methods, root cause analysis, corrective actions, process controls, and continuous improvement practices.
• Strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and ability to identify trends, assess risk, document findings, and translate data into clear, actionable recommendations.
• Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and experience maintaining audit documentation, scorecards, dashboards, or trend reports.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate across operations, compliance, training, finance, and technology teams.
• Ability to handle protected health information and confidential business information in accordance with HIPAA, company policy, and applicable requirements.
• Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and exercise sound judgment in a changing operational environment.
• Ability to perform the essential functions of a primarily computer-based role, with or without reasonable accommodation.

Preferred:
• Experience in a medical device, healthcare services, patient access, reimbursement, prior authorization, claims, or revenue cycle environment.
• Experience using Salesforce or a comparable customer relationship management, workflow, order management, or healthcare operations platform.
• Experience supporting internal controls, SOX compliance, control testing, audit evidence, or remediation activities.
• Experience with data visualization or reporting tools such as Power BI or Tableau.
• Knowledge of payer guidelines, healthcare documentation requirements, and regulated operational processes.
• Quality, audit, compliance, process improvement, or project management certification, such as CPHQ, ASQ, Lean Six Sigma, CIA, or CISA.

Our total compensation package includes medical, dental and vision benefits, retirement benefits, employee stock purchase plan, paid time off, parental leave, family medical leave, volunteer time off and additional leave programs, life insurance, disability coverage, and other life and work wellness benefits and discounts. Benefits may be subject to generally applicable eligibility, waiting period, contributions, and other requirements and conditions.

Below is the starting salary or hourly range for this position, although offers may differ based on the candidate's location, job-specific knowledge, skills and experience.

US Pay Range

$61,500—$86,205 USD

jobs.title: Physical Security – Facilities Lead
jobs.description:
About the Company

Armada is the hyperscaler for the edge, delivering modular AI infrastructure from first deployment to AI factory with speed, scale and sovereignty. Named one of Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies and to the CNBC Disruptor 50, Armada’s solutions are deployed in over 60 countries globally for organizations ranging from energy to defense.

With nearly $500 million in funding to date, Armada is backed by leading investors including Founders Fund, Lux, BlackRock and Microsoft (M12), alongside strategic partnerships with Microsoft, Dell, Palantir, NVIDIA, SpaceX, and Skydio. We are building the infrastructure layer for sovereign and edge AI - rugged, deployable compute for customers that cannot rely on centralized cloud.

Working at Armada means taking ownership, driving autonomy, and delivering impact. You’ll tackle challenges that haven’t been solved before and help build something transformative from the ground up. What you do here will not only define your career but help further Armada’s mission to bridge the digital divide for customers around the world.

About the Role

Armada is seeking a Physical Security – Facilities Lead to own classified design, construction, and accreditation of Galleons for the U.S. Defense sector.

Galleons are built, configured, shipped, and stood up in months, not years. Defense customers need those units accredited as SCIFs, SAPFs, collateral open-storage or closed areas, and related secure processing environments. You will turn ICD 705, DoDM 5205.07, and NISPOM (32 CFR Part 117) physical construction standards into repeatable design requirements, factory and site practices, and accreditation packages that scale with the product line.

You will be the company authority on physical security for secure builds. You will sit with hardware, form-factor, manufacturing, deployment, federal, and security partners from concept through accreditation of the space. Where corporate facility protection overlaps a secure build, you will also set access control, intrusion detection, CPTED, and guard-force requirements as applicable. Corporate physical security is not a separate program. It is in scope only where it touches classified design, construction, or accreditation.

This is a senior, hands-on individual contributor role. You will write the standard, walk the line, brief the Accrediting Official, and close the findings. You will exercise independent judgment on problems without precedent, be accountable for results across Armada's secure-build function, and direct the work of contractors, integrators, and cross-functional partners without having direct reports.

Location. United States (Remote). Travel to U.S. factory, integration, and customer sites as needed to support design reviews, construction surveillance, and accreditation.

What You'll Do (Key Responsibilities)

Classified design and construction standards

• Own physical construction and accreditation requirements for defense Galleons, including SCIFs and SAPFs under ICD 705 and the ICS 705 Technical Specifications, SAPFs under DoDM 5205.07, and collateral open-storage, closed, and discussion areas under 32 CFR Part 117 (NISPOM).

• Translate those standards into design criteria, drawing notes, BOM constraints, and factory work instructions that hardware, mechanical, electrical, and manufacturing teams can build to.

• Lead security design reviews across the Galleon family. Read and redline architectural, structural, electrical, and low-voltage drawings against ICD 705, TEMPEST, and NISPOM.

• Define perimeter, access-control, intrusion-detection, and video requirements for secure configurations, including door, lock, and wall assemblies, STC and acoustic performance, and inspectable materials.

• Own TEMPEST and emissions-security design input. Set red/black separation, shielding, filtering, grounding, and penetration criteria, and coordinate countermeasure reviews with customer TEMPEST authorities.

• Specify Protected Distribution Systems where a Galleon or site requires them and inspect against the applicable CNSSI standard.

• Build a repeatable secure-Galleon configuration so accreditation is a productized path, not a one-off for every build.

Accreditation and government liaison

• Serve as Armada’s liaison to Accrediting Officials, Special Security Officers, Facility Security Officers, DCSA Industrial Security Representatives, and customer security staff.

• Author and maintain Construction Security Plans, Fixed Facility Checklists, inspectable-materials lists, TEMPEST questionnaires, and accreditation submittals.

• Plan and run construction surveillance, site inspections, and quality assurance on factory, integration, and customer-site work. Hold general contractors, integrators, and internal build teams to the CSP.

• Drive accreditation from design approval through inspection, remediation, and operational accreditation. Own the punch list.

• Support capture and proposal teams on DD-254, contract security classification specifications, and physical-security volumes so bids do not promise a configuration that cannot be accredited.

Program execution

• Own the security workstream on defense Galleon programs. Set milestones, dependencies, and risks against hardware design, factory slot, shipment, and customer required-accreditation dates.

• Partner with Large Form Factor and Edge Hardware leads, deployment, logistics, and federal mission teams so security requirements are in the design before steel is cut.

• Stand up the operating rhythm for classified builds: design gates, inspection hold points, documentation control, and lessons learned into the next hull.

• Author and maintain Armada's internal physical-security policies and standards for classified builds, and mentor engineering, manufacturing, and deployment teams so secure-build expertise scales across the company.

Required Qualifications

• U.S. citizenship.

• Active U.S. Secret clearance required.

• Bachelor's degree and 12+ years (or Master's degree and 8+ years) in physical security, industrial security, or secure-facility construction, with at least 5 years hands-on in design, build, and accreditation of SCIFs, SAPFs, or collateral open-storage areas.

• Demonstrated ability to apply ICD 705 Technical Specifications to construction drawings and field conditions, not just cite them.

• Working knowledge of 32 CFR Part 117 physical safeguards and of DoDM 5205.07 as it applies to SAPF construction and accreditation.

• Experience as the technical interface to an Accrediting Official, Cognizant Security Office, or DCSA representative through accreditation.

• Experience authoring Construction Security Plans and fixed-facility or equivalent accreditation packages.

• Ability to read construction documents and reject noncompliant details on walls, doors, penetrations, power, grounding, and electronic security systems.

• Experience with access control, intrusion detection, and alarm monitoring on accredited spaces (UL 2050 or equivalent).

• Track record of driving a build to a date with engineers, contractors, and government security staff in the same room.

• Recognized subject-matter expert who has set physical-security standards or policy for an organization and persuaded diverse senior internal and government stakeholders.

Required Qualifications

• 10+ years in Business Systems, Enterprise Applications, or related roles with increasing scope.

• Platform-agnostic technical fluency in how enterprise systems work: relational database structures, data flows, API and webhook integration patterns, static vs. dynamic configuration, and how upstream changes propagate downstream. The right candidate can describe any enterprise system — regardless of whether they’ve used it before — in terms of its underlying data model and CRUD operations.

• Ability to read (not necessarily write) JavaScript and Apex code: you need to understand what custom logic is doing and assess compatibility with proposed changes, not just know it exists.

• Demonstrated experience owning and scaling core systems for G&A and/or Finance functions.

• Solid integration and data fluency: APIs, iPaaS tools (e.g., Workato, Boomi, MuleSoft), data quality concepts, and reporting infrastructure.

• Strong change management instincts: you bring stakeholders along, drive adoption, and create durable operating habits.

• Excellent communication and stakeholder management — able to translate between business outcomes and technical implementation, facilitate cross-functional trade-off conversations, and influence without authority.

• Genuine enthusiasm for and working knowledge of AI/LLM tooling — and a track record of helping teams actually adopt new tools, not just deploy them.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience designing or implementing enterprise AI enablement programs (tool stack, training, workflow redesign).

• Familiarity with GTM tooling (CRM, CPQ, forecasting) and/or R&D/engineering systems at a level sufficient to establish standards and ensure interoperability.

• Experience with revenue workflows and controls (billing, collections, revenue recognition concepts).

• Comfort prototyping or validating logic using SQL and/or scripting, or deep partnership with technical teams to do so.

• Experience implementing security and compliance controls across business systems (audit readiness, access governance).

• Relevant certifications (nice-to-have): NetSuite, Workday, Rippling, iPaaS platform certs.

Citizenship Requirements

For select roles, due to the nature of our clientele and the technologies involved, there may be specific nationality or citizenship indicated in the required qualifications section. These roles may involve access to sensitive information that is subject to export control regulations or other legal restrictions. In such cases, employment offers will be contingent upon your ability to comply with these requirements.

Compensation & Benefits

For U.S. Based candidates: To ensure fairness and transparency, the starting base salary range for this role for candidates in the U.S. are listed, varying based on location experience, skills, and qualifications.  In addition to base salary, this role will also be offered equity and subsidized benefits (details available upon request).

We use a geographic pay structure based on cost-of-labor markets.

• Tier 1 (e.g., SF Bay Area, NYC, Seattle): $187,500 - $234,370

• Tier 2 (most U.S. metro areas): $163,040 - $203,800

• Tier 3 (other cities): $154,890 - $193,610

Final compensation will be determined by experience, scope, and level, and may vary from the posted range.

Benefits

• Competitive base salary and equity

• Medical, dental, and vision (subsidized cost)

• Health savings accounts (HSA), flexible spending accounts (FSA), and dependent care FSAs (DCFSA)

jobs.title: Infrastructure Lead, DoD / DoW
jobs.description:
About the Company

Armada is the hyperscaler for the edge, delivering modular AI infrastructure from first deployment to AI factory with speed, scale and sovereignty. Named one of Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies and to the CNBC Disruptor 50, Armada’s solutions are deployed in over 60 countries globally for organizations ranging from energy to defense.

With nearly $500 million in funding to date, Armada is backed by leading investors including Founders Fund, Lux, BlackRock and Microsoft (M12), alongside strategic partnerships with Microsoft, Dell, Palantir, NVIDIA, SpaceX, and Skydio. We are building the infrastructure layer for sovereign and edge AI - rugged, deployable compute for customers that cannot rely on centralized cloud.

Working at Armada means taking ownership, driving autonomy, and delivering impact. You’ll tackle challenges that haven’t been solved before and help build something transformative from the ground up. What you do here will not only define your career but help further Armada’s mission to bridge the digital divide for customers around the world.

About the Role

Armada is seeking an Infrastructure Lead to own day-to-day Department of Defense (DoD)/Department of War (DoW) infrastructure workstreams and to serve as a primary technical voice on federal capture. This is a senior individual contributor role. You will not manage a team on day one. You will influence product, manufacturing, deployment, capture, and customer stakeholders across every DoD/DoW opportunity and awarded program you touch.

The role is split evenly between capture and delivery. On the capture side, you engage defense and government customers, shape technical responses to RFIs and RFPs, and translate mission and installation requirements into solution architectures Armada can actually build and field. On the delivery side, you drive Statement of Work (SOW) execution from award through site readiness, production, deployment, integration, and handover with accountability for schedule, technical performance, risk, and change control.

You will work across Armada's Federal infrastructure portfolio, including Galleon ruggedized Modular Data Centers (MDCs), Leviathan megawatt-scale AI-factory form factors, and the Armada Platform. The work sits at the intersection of hardware, power and cooling, connectivity, secure edge software, and the compliance regimes that govern warfighter and installation environments: disconnected operations, classified and air-gapped workloads, zero trust, and Authority to Operate.

This is a hands-on, high-expectation role in a fast-growing, mission-critical environment. You will determine your own methods on new assignments, exercise judgment across ambiguous and sensitive requirements, and make decisions with imperfect information. You are the person who makes sure what we propose to the Department can be manufactured, transported, installed, commissioned, and sustained.

Location. United States (Remote) with expected travel to the Washington, D.C., customer sites, Armada offices, fabrication partners, and deployment locations.

What You'll Do (Key Responsibilities)

DoD / DoW workstream ownership

• Own day-to-day execution of assigned DoD/DoW infrastructure workstreams, from early customer engagement through deployment and sustainment.

• Establish operating rhythms, KPIs, risk registers, and accountability mechanisms so federal infrastructure delivery is predictable, not reactive.

• Translate mission requirements into scalable product and deployment patterns.

• Balance classified and unclassified customer needs while protecting a unified core product architecture across Galleon, Leviathan, and the Armada Platform.

RFI / RFP technical engagement

• Lead technical engagement on DoD/DoW RFIs, RFPs, and similar proposals for infrastructure and edge-compute opportunities.

• Shape technical volumes, compliance matrices, bases of estimate, and solution narratives with Capture, Federal Product, Customer Engineering, and Legal.

• Conduct customer technical exchanges, site surveys, and capability briefings. Translate warfighter, installation, and program-office problems into specific, actionable requirements.

• Advise capture and go-to-market teams on what Armada can commit to: form factor, power and cooling envelope, deployment timeline, accreditation path, and manufacturing readiness.

• Represent Armada as a trusted technical advisor to government technical evaluators, program managers, and mission owners.

SOW and Program Execution

• Own SOW execution on awarded infrastructure efforts: scope, integrated schedule, technical performance, risk, issue, and change control.

• Build and run the delivery cadence to include program reviews, working groups, customer status, and internal execution forums.

• Partner with Finance, Legal, and Supply Chain on contract execution, delivery commitments, CLIN/SLIN traceability, and change management.

• Drive integrated plans across engineering, manufacturing, logistics, and field deployment so cost, schedule, and technical performance stay in balance as customer priorities move.

• Proactively surface execution risk, long-lead constraints, and critical-path slips, and drive mitigation rather than report them.

• Support transition from capture assumptions to an executable baseline at award, including site conditions, interface control, and acceptance criteria.

Infrastructure, manufacturing, and site delivery

• Own the infrastructure thread from site due diligence and design review through fabrication, transport, installation, integration, and commissioning for Galleon and Leviathan deployments in defense environments.

• Partner with Form Factors, manufacturing, and supply chain on production readiness: factory strategy, throughput, quality, and long-lead items such as power, cooling, steel, switchgear, and IT infrastructure.

• Validate that proposed designs are manufacturable, transportable, and installable against real site constraints — crane and access, laydown, sequencing, tolerances, and fit-up — before they are locked into a proposal or an issued-for-construction package.

• Build repeatable deployment playbooks and methods of procedure so defense sites execute against a productized pattern, not a one-off plan.

• Coordinate civil, structural, mechanical, electrical, ICT, and IT interfaces with fabricators, general contractors, and government public-works stakeholders.

• Feed field lessons — constructability, quality escapes, commissioning gaps — back into product design and future proposals.

Security, compliance, and mission assurance

• Partner with Security and Compliance on DoD security requirements, NIST, RMF, zero trust, and classified or air-gapped deployment models.

• Guide the infrastructure and accreditation features needed to support Authority to Operate and government compliance and keep proposal language consistent with what the platform can evidence.

• Drive secure edge-to-cloud and disconnected, intermittent, and limited (DIL) operating concepts for defense customers who cannot rely on centralized cloud.

• Ensure delivery artifacts including as-builts, test and acceptance packages, configuration baselines, and sustainment handoff meet mission-assurance expectations.

Required Qualifications

• U.S. citizenship and an active U.S. Secret clearance. Must be able to obtain and maintain the clearance required by assigned programs.

• 12+ years of experience in infrastructure, data center, critical facilities, hardware program, or technical program roles.

• 5+ years supporting U.S. Government or Defense customers (DoD/DoW, Intelligence Community, or federal civilian agencies), including direct customer engagement.

• Demonstrated ownership of technical RFI/RFP responses, proposals, or customer technical evaluations for infrastructure, data center, or mission-critical systems.

• Demonstrated SOW or contract execution experience: integrated schedule, risk and change control, and delivery against government acceptance criteria.

• Ability to translate defense customer problems into specific, actionable requirements and into commitments engineering and manufacturing can execute.

• Excellent written and verbal communication with technical, operational, contracting, and senior government audiences.

Preferred Qualifications

• Active TS/SCI clearance.

• Direct experience with modular or prefabricated data centers, edge compute, or expeditionary infrastructure in defense, intelligence, or austere environments.

• Experience with DoD acquisition and contracting artifacts: SOW, CDRL/SDRL, RFI/RFP technical volumes, bases of estimate, and integrated master schedules.

• Familiarity with RMF, ATO, ICD 503, NIST 800-53, zero trust, IL4/IL5/IL6, or classified deployment models.

• Experience with disconnected, intermittent, and limited operations, sovereign or air-gapped AI infrastructure, or installation energy and power constraints.

• Prior military, intelligence, or government service, or experience as a program manager, TPM, capture lead, or customer engineer on a defense hardware program.

Citizenship Requirements

For select roles, due to the nature of our clientele and the technologies involved, there may be specific nationality or citizenship indicated in the required qualifications section. These roles may involve access to sensitive information that is subject to export control regulations or other legal restrictions. In such cases, employment offers will be contingent upon your ability to comply with these requirements.

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Researcher - CORDAP
jobs.description:
About the California Academy of Sciences

Founded in 1853, the California Academy of Sciences is a globally renowned, AZA-accredited non-profit scientific and cultural institution located in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park. Home to a world-class planetarium, aquarium, rainforest, research institute, and natural history museum—all under one living roof—our mission is to regenerate the natural world through science, learning, and collaboration.

Our living collection reflects Earth’s vast biodiversity, consisting of nearly 60,000 animals representing over 800 species. Our research collections are the largest west of the Mississippi,  spanning nearly 46 million plants, animals, fossils, and cultural artifacts from across the globe and throughout history. Our diverse team includes leading biodiversity scientists, educators, storytellers, designers, and communicators who are passionate about advancing knowledge and catalyzing action through science and storytelling.

Whether you're conducting research behind the scenes or engaging the public on the museum floor, your work will help connect people to the natural world and empower them to protect it.

About the Opportunity

Organizational Culture

When you join the California Academy of Sciences, you become part of a mission-driven community that values curiosity, collaboration, and innovation, and celebrates its accomplishments together. Staff share a commitment to executing a new strategic plan that will strengthen the organization's financial foundations, cultivate a vibrant internal culture, and foster smart growth to secure the Academy’s future.

We hope you are inspired by what we do and are motivated to contribute to our mission. The Academy is looking for candidates who do great work, and we know they may come from a number of different backgrounds and experiences. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every qualification for the position.

This position is based in San Francisco, California. The specific onsite/hybrid schedule for this position is listed below.

This position is part of a bargaining unit represented by Cal Academy Workers United, and will be subject to the terms and conditions of that contract.

This one-year position is funded by the Coral Research & Development Accelerator Platform (CORDAP), will be supervised by Dr. Rebecca Albright, and will work closely with scientists in the Department of Invertebrate Zoology and Geology (IZG), the Steinhart Aquarium, and partners at Roatán Marine Park (Honduras). The postdoc will help deliver CORDAP-funded project outcomes by running coral spawning and early life stage experiments in the Academy’s ex situ coral spawning systems, and by running in situ coral spawning work in Roatán in collaboration with Roatán Marine Park. The position requires international travel, fieldwork, and scientific diving. The postdoc will analyze data, write scientific papers, and contribute to outreach and education efforts at the Academy and in the field.

The California Academy of Sciences welcomes people of all backgrounds, identities, and beliefs to join us in achieving our mission to explore, explain, and sustain life. We place diversity, equity, and inclusion at the heart of our recruiting efforts and strive to build a culture centered on mutual respect, equal treatment, and the opportunity to succeed.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Help deliver CORDAP-funded project deliverables, including contributing to project planning, timelines, and progress reports to the funder and partners.

• Run coral spawning and early life stage experiments in the Academy’s ex situ coral systems, including broodstock care, spawning monitoring, gamete collection and fertilization, larval rearing, settlement, and recruit grow-out.

• Run in situ coral spawning work in Roatán, Honduras, in conjunction with Roatán Marine Park, including night spawning dives, gamete collection, and field-based larval rearing. This requires international travel for up to 2–4 weeks per trip, boat-based fieldwork, and SCUBA diving.

• Design experiments, manage and analyze data, and lead and contribute to scientific papers; present results at (inter)national conferences and write reports for audiences of varying scientific backgrounds.

• Contribute to outreach and education efforts at the Academy and in the field, including public presentations, community engagement with partners and local communities in Roatán, and in-person and online programs for Academy audiences.

• Work collaboratively within IZG, the Steinhart Aquarium, and across the Academy, including with Development and Marketing as requested.

• Represent the CORDAP project and the Academy at internal and external events.

• Follow all Academy safety procedures, protocols, and regulations, including dive safety protocols and protocols for the ethical and humane handling of living specimens in the field and at the Academy.

• Other duties as assigned.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

The preferred qualifications listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required or preferred.

EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE:

The ideal candidate will possess a combination of the following education and/or equivalent experience:

• Doctoral degree (Ph.D.) in a relevant discipline, with all requirements completed by the starting date of the postdoc appointment, is required.

• Demonstrated laboratory and field skills with corals, including work on tropical coral reefs, with proper safety precautions followed in each.

• Experience with coral biology, coral spawning, and early life stages (gametes, larvae, settlement, recruits) required.

• Experience with experimental design and statistics required.

• Experience with genomics and/or bioinformatics desired.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

• Ability to conduct original, high-quality scientific research and to follow through on project deliverables within a fixed one-year timeline, with a strong academic record (relative to opportunity) that includes first-author publications.

• Strong knowledge of coral biology and reproduction, including spawning and early life stage husbandry.

• Proficiency with experimental design and statistical analysis using R and/or Python (ideally demonstrated through a shared code repository); familiarity with the Unix command-line and bioinformatics workflows is a plus.

• Field work experience, including in remote locations with difficult living conditions.

• Scientific diving experience and appropriate qualifications (or the ability to obtain them), with comprehensive knowledge of SCUBA diving theory and its application to safe diving practice; night diving experience preferred.

• Knowledge of scleractinian coral species identification/taxonomy, including Caribbean species.

• Demonstrated interest and experience in science communication, outreach, and education, including with public and community audiences.

• Ability to work independently and as a member of a team, with strong communication and interpersonal skills with diverse stakeholders and audiences.

• Must have or be able to obtain a valid passport; willingness to travel internationally.

LANGUAGE SKILLS:  Ability to read and interpret documents such as scientific papers, safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals. Ability to write reports, correspondence, and scientific articles. Ability to speak effectively to groups or individuals of varying levels of scientific knowledge.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS & WORK ENVIRONMENT:  The physical demands and work environment described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable persons with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to stand, sit, walk, reach with hands and arms, talk and hear. Fieldwork involves boat-based SCUBA diving, including night dives, in tropical conditions. Must be able to lift 50 lbs. Must be able to perform repetitive motions 25 % of the time.

Compensation and Benefits:
The salary range for this position is $39.52 to $41.12 per hour. Actual compensation will be commensurate with the final candidate's qualifications and experience, including skills, knowledge, relevant education, certifications and aligned with the internal peer group. We believe in fair and equitable compensation practices and are committed to providing competitive salaries within the industry and market standards. The Academy offers a total compensation package that emphasizes both base salary and comprehensive benefits based on the hours per week worked. Further details regarding compensation and benefits will be discussed during the interview process.

Schedule: Full-Time On site, 40 hours per week

How to Apply:  Interested candidates should submit a resume and application through our Careers Page portal.

The California Academy of Sciences will give full consideration for employment to all qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance (SF Police Code, Article 49). For more information visit: https://sfgov.org/olse/fair-chance-ordinance-fco.

The California Academy of Sciences is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is committed to ensure that all employees and applicants receive equal consideration and treatment, regardless of race, color, creed, gender (including gender identity or gender expression), religion, marital or domestic partner status, age, national origin or ancestry, physical, mental or medical disability, sex, sexual orientation, citizenship, military service status, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by state or federal law or local ordinance.

The California Academy of Sciences is a non-smoking facility. Smoking is also prohibited in Golden Gate Park.

jobs.title: Marine Recovery Engineer
jobs.description:
At Stoke, we believe a thriving space economy will enable a vibrant, sustainable, and equitable future here on Earth. That is why we’re building Nova, our fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. Designed for daily flight, Nova tackles the core challenges of space transportation by reducing cost, increasing availability, and improving reliability. By radically lowering launch costs and increasing flight cadence, we’re helping create a truly scalable space industry.

Our team is mission-driven, collaborative, and empowered to take ownership of their work. If you want to work alongside some of the most dedicated and talented people on Earth, we’d love to have you join us.

The Role
Reusable systems with frequent launch cadence are the key to connecting Earth and space, and a reliable recovery system is integral to a fully reusable launch vehicle. As Marine Recovery Engineer, you will build Stoke’s capability to locate, capture, and recover Nova flight hardware from the open ocean and return it safely to port.

There is no established playbook. You will develop recovery techniques, select and adapt the vessels, write the procedures, and then go offshore and run the operation yourself. You’ll own the work from CONOPS through commissioning and live recovery campaigns, as part of a small team spanning Florida and Washington.

This role is a fit if you:

• Have personally planned and led non-routine offshore operations such as salvage, at-sea retrieval, heavy-lift, or towing, where you made the calls on deck rather than supporting someone else’s plan

• Can engineer the solution (rigging calculations, lift plans, stability, structural loads) and then execute it at sea

• Are comfortable building procedures and techniques from first principles when nothing off the shelf fits

This role is probably not a fit if:

• Your offshore experience is primarily routine vessel operations, crewing, or executing established procedures

• Your engineering experience is primarily office-based design without significant time offshore or involved in unique operations.

• You’re looking for a project management or vessel management position

• You are not prepared to relocate to Cape Canaveral and spend extended periods offshore

Responsibilities

• Develop and own recovery CONOPS for retrieving flight hardware from the ocean environment across a range of sea states, scenarios, and operational conditions

• Develop and prove out unconventional at-sea capture, lifting, securing, and transit techniques for recovering floating hardware

• Plan and lead offshore recovery test and demonstration campaigns, iterating rapidly on technique and equipment to build the operational maturity needed to eventually support full recovery

• Lead vessel strategy: identify, charter, and integrate support vessels and associated offshore equipment suited to each recovery scenario

• Serve as the engineering lead for recovery hardware and systems, providing oversight across structural, mechanical, rigging, lifting, and operational disciplines

• Develop safety cases, risk assessments, and operational procedures for offshore crews

• Interface directly with external vendors, regulatory bodies, and classification societies (United States Coast Guard (USCG), American Bureau of Shipping (ABS), Det Norske Veritas (DNV), etc.)

• Author, review, and approve test and operational procedures

• Develop and manage technical specifications

• Provide technical direction for operations personnel

• Coordinate across multi-discipline engineering and operations across Florida and Washington

• Develop an innate understanding of the Nova launch vehicle and ensure recovery systems enable rapid return-to-launch

Qualifications

• 5+ years of hands-on offshore operations experience, with direct involvement in salvage, marine recovery, heavy-lift, towing, or at-sea retrieval of hardware

• Demonstrated experience chartering and directing support vessels and crews for non-routine offshore operations

• Hands-on experience with offshore lifting, crane operations, rigging, and/or towing operations

• Proven ability to develop and execute recovery or salvage operations from first principles in dynamic, ambiguous conditions at sea

• Experience adapting commercial or off-the-shelf vessels and equipment to new uses in lieu of purpose-built, long-lead assets

• Bachelor's degree in naval architecture, marine engineering, mechanical engineering, or similar field

• Strong engineering fundamentals across multiple disciplines (naval architecture, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, etc.)

• Proven hands-on experience building, operating, or troubleshooting complex systems in a marine environment

• Ability to troubleshoot problems and implement solutions real time

• Ability to prioritize and execute

• Excellent written and verbal communication

• Ability to lead and follow

• Willing to relocate to Cape Canaveral, FL

• Willingness and ability to travel, including internationally, and TDY (Temporary Duty) from days to weeks offshore

• Ability to pass USSF background check for Cape Canaveral Space Force Station

• Ability to hold and maintain a TWIC card

• Ability to hold a Merchant Mariner Credential

Preferred Qualifications

• 10+ years of experience in a related role engineering, building, and/or operating high-performing systems in the maritime, offshore, or salvage industry

• Direct experience recovering high-value, sensitive, or non-standard objects from the water (e.g., salvage, debris field recovery, subsea search and recovery)

• A genuine interest in aerospace and a desire to contribute to spaceflight

• Experience working directly with IACS surveyors

• Experience working with U.S. Coast Guard and Port Authorities

Benefits

• Equity – We know that our employees are the reason we succeed. To give everyone a stake in our future, we are pleased to offer equity in the form of stock options to all regular, full-time employees.

• Comprehensive benefits program including subsidized medical, dental, and vision insurance

• Company-paid life and disability insurance

• 401(k) plan with employer match

• 4 weeks’ Paid Time Off

• Holidays – 10 days (including an end-of-year closure)

• Paid Family/Parental Leave

• On-site gym or monthly wellness stipend (depending on location)

• Dog friendly offices!

Compensation

Target Levels:

• Level 3 Range: $129,150 - $193,620

• Level 4 Range: $151,305 - $252,105

Our job posts are intentionally written to attract a wide variety of experience levels, and we make decisions about the right fit on a per-candidate basis.

Your actual level and base salary will be decided based on your specific experience and skill level.

ITAR Requirements

Separate from this I-9 process, as noted above, this position entails access to certain technology and technical data that is restricted under U.S. export control laws and regulations.  Employment or continued employment may be conditioned on your legal authorization to work with or have access to export control materials as necessary to perform your job.

jobs.title: Vice President, Legal Counsel
jobs.description:

We provide officially licensed uniforms, comprehensive resources, and dedicated support, empowering league operators to run the very best youth sports leagues and events in their communities. Our mission is grounded in the transformative power of sports. We’re dedicated to ensuring every child has the opportunity to play the game they love. By empowering league operators to effectively run and maintain their programming season after season, we’re committed to making youth sports accessible and inclusive for all.

The Vice President, Legal Counsel will establish and lead RCX Sports’ in-house legal function, serving as a practical, business-minded advisor to the executive team and cross-functional leaders. This role will bring routine legal work in-house, create scalable legal operations, and manage outside counsel for specialized matters—improving speed, controlling costs, and strengthening legal and regulatory risk management.

As an individual contributor reporting initially to the Chief Customer Officer, and the Chief Operating Officer long-term, this leader will serve as RCX Sports’ senior legal partner, overseeing commercial contracting and contract lifecycle management, compliance, youth protection matters, data privacy, intellectual property, employment-law support, policy governance, legal training, and legal operations. The role will establish and evolve the legal frameworks, policies, agreements, and governance practices that support the business, partnering closely with League Success, League Growth, Marketing, Programs, Events, InfoSec, People Operations, and other teams to define requirements, translate legal obligations into processes, and support effective execution.

Job Responsibilities:

• Serve as a strategic legal advisor to the executive team and business leaders on corporate governance, compliance, risk management, employment matters, contracts, and key business decisions.

• Draft, review, and negotiate sponsorship, supplier, vendor, service, partnership, licensing, media-rights, and other commercial agreements.

• Own the full contract lifecycle, including intake, prioritization, templates and playbooks, approval workflows, execution, a central repository, renewals, obligations tracking.

• Partner with functional owners and department heads to assign accountability, monitor fulfillment, review obligations regularly, and address gaps that could create business risk.

• Build a legal intake and prioritization process with clear service levels and transparent tracking of open legal matters.

• Develop and execute the legal department’s operating plan, annual budget, and reporting cadence.

• Manage outside counsel relationships, including matter scoping, panel selection, rate negotiation, budgets, spend reporting, and decisions about when specialized external support is required.

• Provide legal advisory support to the Foundation on nonprofit governance, program grants, agreements, and owned and operated league activities that expand access to youth sports, in partnership with Foundation and program leaders.

• Create and maintain a company policy library with assigned owners and an annual review cycle, beginning with youth protection, data privacy, and employee policies.

• Lead and document investigations involving alleged violations of youth protection policies and support broader safeguarding compliance, including background-check requirements, participant waivers, and league standards.

• Design and execute a risk-based compliance audit program; track findings through remediation or closure.

• Advise on data collection, processing, privacy, and security matters, including data involving minors, in partnership with InfoSec and operational teams.

• Manage RCX Sports’ trademark and copyright portfolio, including prosecution, maintenance, enforcement, and related calendars.

• Monitor legislative and regulatory developments across the states where RCX Sports operates and provide practical recommendations and regular updates to leadership.

Verkada is transforming how organizations protect their people and places with an integrated, privacy-sensitive AI-powered platform that includes solutions for video security, access control, air quality sensors, alarms, intercoms, and visitor management.

We’ve got serious momentum in the market: more than 30,000 customers (including 100+ of the Fortune 500), a $5.8B valuation, more than $1 billion in annualized bookings, and backing from CapitalG, Sequoia Capital, General Catalyst, Felicis Ventures, Next47 and more. You can look at all kinds of communities to see our platform’s impact in the world. It's the retailer that uses our agentic AI to deter theft before it happens. The warehouse that uses AI-powered alerts to make sure its team is protected on the floor with proper PPE. jobs.description:
At Qualtrics, we create software the world’s best brands use to deliver exceptional frontline experiences, build high-performing teams, and design products people love. But we are more than a platform—we are the creators and stewards of the Experience Management category serving over 18K clients globally. Building a category takes grit, determination, and a disdain for convention—but most of all it requires close-knit, high-functioning teams with an unwavering dedication to serving our customers.

When you join one of our teams, you’ll be part of a nimble group that’s empowered to set aggressive goals and move fast to achieve them. Strategic risks are encouraged and complex problems are solved together, by passing the microphone and iterating until the best solution comes to light. You won’t have to look to find growth opportunities—ready or not, they’ll find you. From retail to government to healthcare, we’re on a mission to bring humanity, connection, and empathy back to business. Join over 5,000 people across the globe who think that’s work worth doing.

Email Marketing Manager

Why We Have This Role

Qualtrics is experiencing incredible growth through the delivery of an exceptional product, and world-class sales and marketing efforts. The Email Marketing Manager will focus on building high-performing email segments, executing rigorous deployment processes, and delivering excellence across assigned email campaigns. This role requires a detail-oriented, proactive email marketer who can manage the end-to-end campaign workflow, work at scale with global partners, and bring forward-thinking innovations and flawless execution to our data-driven email journeys.

How You’ll Find Success

• Partner with Marketing Operations to ensure campaign strategies translate seamlessly into functional database segments.

jobs.title: Lead Platform Engineer
jobs.description:
As Lead Platform Engineer, you will be responsible for architecting and maintaining the foundational infrastructure that supports efficient and scalable software development. This involves creating and enhancing developer tools, APIs, and integrations that automate workflows and streamline processes to improve team agility. You will collaborate closely with engineering teams to ensure the platform meets their needs for delivering high-quality applications, while maintaining scalability, reliability, and performance. A key aspect of this role is empowering development teams to independently provision and manage their own software delivery pipelines, including CI/CD systems, source control, and artifact repositories, enabling them to deliver software continuously and reliably without relying on other teams. You will guide the design and implementation of efficient and secure pipelines tailored to specific software delivery engagements, ensuring fast feedback loops and adherence to risk management, security, and governance requirements.

Job responsibilities

• Design, implement, and maintain scalable and reliable platform infrastructure to support the development and production environments.

• Drive automation and CI/CD pipelines for the platform, improving the speed and efficiency of deployments and operations.

• Ensure the platform's security, scalability, and high availability, meeting the business needs and operational SLAs.

• Troubleshoot and resolve platform-related issues, including performance bottlenecks, incidents, and outages, and ensure root cause analysis is performed and communicated.

• Implement and oversee the use of containerization technologies (Docker, Kubernetes) and manage cloud infrastructure services (e.g., AWS, GCP, Azure).

• Champion the use of Infrastructure as Code (IaC) principles to define and manage platform resources.

• Support the adoption of DevOps and GitOps practices to streamline deployments, enhance collaboration, and reduce manual intervention.

• Actively participate in performance tuning and optimization for cloud-based applications and infrastructure, ensuring long-term sustainability and performance.

Job qualifications

Technical Skills

• Mandatory in-depth expertise in Google Cloud Platform (GCP) services (GKE, Compute, Storage, VPC networking, Serverless), with broad familiarity with multi-cloud environments (AWS or Azure).

• Advanced, hands-on mastery of Infrastructure as Code (IaC) using Terraform, alongside configuration management automation using Ansible or Chef.

• Proven experience driving DevOps, CI/CD, and GitOps practices, including designing and implementing robust infrastructure test automation frameworks (e.g., Terratest, Kitchen, InSpec).

• Comprehensive knowledge of platform observability, designing proactive monitoring and alerting systems using tools such as Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, New Relic, or ELK Stack to troubleshoot complex platform issues.

• Demonstrated track record in securing infrastructure following cloud security best practices (IAM, encryption, network policies) and establishing continuous security monitoring and proactive threat detection.

• Practical experience managing and supporting data infrastructure and operations, including cloud storage solutions, high-throughput pipelines, and NoSQL databases.

• Deep background in containerization (Docker, Helm) and enterprise Kubernetes orchestration platforms, specifically Google Kubernetes Engine.

• Solid programming and scripting skills (Java, Python, Go, Bash, or similar) to automate operational workflows, build developer tooling, and integrate RESTful APIs within microservices architectures.

• Demonstrated ability to conduct platform performance tuning, dynamic auto-scaling, and strategic cloud cost optimization.

Professional Skills

• Excellent communication and presentation skills, both written and verbal, with fluency in English.

• Strong collaboration skills and the ability to work effectively with cross-functional teams, including development, operations, and security teams.

• Ability to troubleshoot complex technical issues and provide clear, actionable solutions.

• Strong problem-solving skills, with a proactive and solution-oriented approach to challenges.

• Ability to make recommendations for platform improvements backed by strong technical reasoning.
