jobs.description:
ABOUT AURELIAN 

Aurelian builds AI tools that help 911 centers handle more with less, so telecommunicators can stay focused on what matters most and communities get the response they need.



AVA https://www.aurelian.com/ava is a conversational AI agent that answers non-emergency calls; the agent routes, triages, and resolves the calls without any human intervention. By handling administrative calls like noise complaints, lost dogs, and parking inquiries, AVA eliminates hold times and lets call-takers focus their energy on actual emergencies.



CORA https://www.aurelian.com/cora supports call-takers on the calls that matter most. CORA is an on-screen assistant that delivers real-time SOP checklists, smart reminders, and contextual guidance as an emergency call unfolds, so dispatchers stay calm, consistent, and confident when every second counts. When AVA detects an emergency mid-call, it transfers the caller to a telecommunicator and passes along the caller details, location, incident type, and key statements directly into CORA. The call-taker never starts from scratch.



The problem we're solving is serious. The average emergency communications center is 30% understaffed nationwide. Staffing shortages drive burnout and attrition, which makes the shortage worse. Meanwhile, 60-80% of the calls coming in aren't even emergencies at all. Aurelian addresses both sides of that equation: AVA reduces unnecessary call volume, and CORA makes every emergency call more manageable for the people handling it.


Aurelian is live in centers across the country, answering thousands of non-emergency calls every day, and is backed by New Enterprise Associates https://www.nea.com/blog/aurelian-ai-agents-powering-the-911-call-centers-of-the-future and Y Combinator https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/aurelian. Aurelian is growing rapidly; we are hiring people who want to help scale this work and make a real difference in public safety infrastructure for communities across the country.




WHY JOIN US:

Aurelian is growing quickly, and this role will be key to building our team across both technical and non-technical roles. The people you bring in will shape what we build and how we work. It's a great fit for someone who's driven, gets excited about finding the candidate everyone else missed, and wants to grow alongside the company.

 


WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING:

 - Source candidates across a wide range of roles to build top-of-funnel - from engineering to sales, marketing, design, product, and operations.

 - Use tools like Noon, Juicebox, etc. and other creative channels to identify strong talent.

 - Build thoughtful and personalized candidate searches and outreach approaches that represent our brand and mission, focusing on quality vs quantity.

 - Partner with the Head of Talent to calibrate profiles, align on pipelines, and iterate based on feedback.

 - Move quickly, stay organized, and adapt as priorities shift.


WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR:

 - 1–4 years of sourcing or recruiting experience, ideally:
   
   - Trained at an agency or search firm, and
   
   - Have since spent some time in-house at a startup.

 - Experience sourcing both technical and non-technical roles.

 - Extreme bias towards action, organized, and able to prioritize in a fast-moving environment.

 - Comfortable working in gray areas with limited structure.

 - Familiarity with Ashby.


PLEASE NOTE:  THIS IS NOT A ROLE SUITED FOR A SENIOR (OR HIGHER) LEVEL RECRUITERS.




 

To learn more about what it's like to work at Aurelian, visit our About Us https://www.aurelian.com/about page and follow us on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/aureliansystem to stay up to date!



We encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every qualification listed above. We believe exceptional people come from many different backgrounds, and we’d rather connect with you than miss the opportunity.




Come do the best work of your life and join us in shaping the future of critical technology that truly matters.

jobs.title: Regional Sales Director, Minnesota
jobs.description:
About Us

Prophet Security builds AI SOC agents designed to outwork modern attackers. Our agentic AI SOC platform works every alert end-to-end, hunts threats early, and tightens detections before gaps turn into incidents. Our founders bring decades of experience from companies including CrowdStrike, Mandiant, Palo Alto Networks, Expel, Red Canary, Abnormal Security and Symantec. Backed by Accel, Bain Capital Ventures, Amex Ventures and Citi Ventures, our mission is to shift cybersecurity power dynamics to favor defenders.

 

What Our Platform Does

Specialized AI agents work together across investigation, threat hunting and detection engineering. They connect to a customer's existing tools through 200+ integrations, with no rip-and-replace.

 - AI SOC Analyst: Triages and investigates every alert at a senior-analyst level and takes scoped response actions, autonomously or with human sign-off.

 - AI Threat Hunter: Lets teams query their environment in plain language and runs hunts on emerging threats, on demand or on a schedule.

 - AI Detection Engineer: Maps real MITRE ATT&CK coverage and builds tuned, backtested detections to close gaps.

 - Prophet AI Watchtower: 24x7x365 human experts validate every malicious determination and escalate in under 30 minutes.

Enterprise-ready with single-tenant deployment, Prophet is trusted by Enterprises, nearly one-third in the F500 and growing by the day.  We deliver massive productivity gains - 5.3 minute median time to investigate, 99.8% accuracy rate, 10X faster median time to respond and 250% ROI.

 

The Impact You'll Have

You'll own new-logo growth in your region. You'll land customers on their most urgent use case, often alert triage and investigation, then expand into threat hunting and detection engineering as they see results. Your work will directly drive Prophet's revenue and help define the AI SOC category.

 

What You'll Do

 - Build and execute a territory plan to win net-new enterprise customers, with a clear land-and-expand strategy across Prophet's platform.

 - Build trusted relationships with CISOs and security leaders, and engage SOC, detection engineering, threat hunting and procurement teams in each deal.

 - Own the full sales cycle, from prospecting and discovery through business case, proof of value (POV), security review, negotiation and close.

 - Run outcome-based POVs with Sales Engineering, using clear success criteria such as accuracy, analyst time saved and detection coverage.

 - Position Prophet against legacy SOAR, MDR/MSSP and emerging AI SOC competitors.

 - Co-sell with channel and technology partners to build pipeline and accelerate deals.

 - Partner with Marketing, Sales Engineering, Customer Success and Product, and maintain accurate forecasting in Salesforce.

 - Achieve and exceed quarterly and annual new-business revenue targets.

 

Qualifications

 - 5+ years of enterprise software sales, including 3+ years closing new logos in cybersecurity.

 - Strong knowledge of security operations buyers and technologies such as SIEM, SOAR, EDR/XDR and MDR/MSSP.

 - Track record of selling platforms or multiple products, and of selling AI, automation or emerging-category solutions.

 - Established network of security leaders and channel partners in your region.

 - Consistent history of exceeding quota, with strong deal discipline (e.g., MEDDPICC) in complex, multi-stakeholder sales.

 - Credibility with both technical practitioners and executives, plus excellent communication and presentation skills.

 - A startup mindset and a passion for helping defenders win.

 

Our Culture

Our employees are recognized as our top asset and we provide great benefits, meaningful equity participation, as well as a fun and inspiring environment to create and collaborate.

 - Customer Centricity: Focus on exceeding customer expectations and placing them at the core of decisions

 - Practicality over Perfection: Emphasis on efficient solutions and agile decision-making

 - Strive for Excellence: Commitment to high standards and continuous improvement

 - Transparent Communication: Encouragement of open, honest dialogue and collaborative trust

 - Unwavering Resilience: Determination to overcome challenges and persist in achieving goals

 - Have Fun: Foster a positive work environment that balances hard work with enjoyment and creativity

jobs.title: Product Management Intern
jobs.description:
Parallel Systems is pioneering autonomous battery-electric rail vehicles designed to transform freight transportation by shifting portions of the $900 billion U.S. trucking industry onto rail. Our innovative technology offers cleaner, safer, and more efficient logistics solutions. Join our dynamic team and help shape a smarter, greener future for global freight.

Product Management Intern

Parallel Systems is seeking a Product Intern to help shape the software platform that our team, operators, and rail partners use to run an autonomous freight network. This is a hands-on role for someone who wants to own a real product problem, not shadow one.

You will sit at the intersection of engineering, operations, and customers. You will talk to users, dig into data, define requirements, and work side by side with software engineers to scope and ship a feature on our platform.

The right person is technical enough to earn engineers' trust, curious enough to understand how rail and logistics actually work, and comfortable bringing structure to ambiguous problems.

What You Will Work On

You will own a specific product problem on our software platform, scoped to team priorities. Example areas include:

• User and customer research: interviewing operators, rail partners, and internal teams to understand workflows and pain points

• Requirements and specs: turning research into clear problem statements, user stories, and requirements engineers can build from

• Feature delivery: working with engineering and design to scope, prioritize, build, and launch a feature on the platform

• Fleet operations workflows: improving how users monitor, dispatch, and manage vehicles and freight through our tools

• Data and metrics: defining success metrics, querying fleet and usage data, and turning findings into product decisions

• Roadmap input: assessing opportunities, competitive landscape, and tradeoffs to inform what the team builds next

You will work through a structured product lifecycle: discovery, problem definition, requirements, delivery with engineering, launch, and measuring results.

What to Expect

• Weeks 1-2: Onboarding, overview of our vehicles, operations, and software platform, shadowing engineers and operators, and tool and data access setup

• Weeks 3-4: Project assignment, user interviews and discovery, and a written problem statement reviewed with your mentor

• Weeks 5-7: Requirements and spec writing, prioritization with engineering, and early design or prototype reviews

• Weeks 8-10: Supporting build and testing with the engineering team, user feedback sessions, and iteration on scope

• Weeks 11-12: Launch or handoff, measurement of early results, documentation of findings and recommended next steps, and a presentation to the broader team

Progress will be tracked through weekly check-ins with your mentor, spec and design reviews, and feedback from engineering, operations, and users.

Basic Requirements

• Currently pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related technical field

• Hands-on product, engineering, or startup experience through internships, student teams, research, or personal projects

• Enough technical fluency to read code, understand system architecture, and discuss tradeoffs with engineers

• Experience working with data, such as writing SQL or analyzing data in Python or spreadsheets

• Strong written communication, including the ability to write clear, concise specs and documents

• Ability to bring structure to ambiguous problems and drive work forward with limited direction

• Excitement about working in a hard-tech environment where software meets physical vehicles and real operations

Preferred Qualifications

• Prior software engineering or product management internship, or experience shipping a software product at a startup or on a student team

• Experience conducting user interviews or usability testing and translating findings into requirements

• Experience building prototypes or simple apps, or comfort with design tools such as Figma

• Familiarity with B2B, enterprise, or operations software

• Interest in logistics, transportation, rail, robotics, or industrial technology

• Experience from hands-on extracurricular engineering teams such as Formula SAE, robotics, autonomous systems teams, or similar

• Strong documentation habits and attention to detail

Final compensation will be commensurate with the candidate’s final level. Also, this range represents base compensation only and does not include equity or benefits, if applicable.

jobs.title: Cybersecurity Support Specialist
jobs.description:
ABOUT NOOKS

Nooks is pioneering Classified-Infrastructure-as-a-Service (CIaaS) — designing, building, and operating Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIFs) and other secured, classified environments for the defense and national security community. We work with the agencies, contractors, and mission-driven organizations that keep the nation safe, delivering the physical infrastructure that makes classified work possible. We’re growing fast, operating across multiple markets, and building a company that takes both the mission and the business seriously.

About the Role

Accredited systems generate a constant stream of security work — scans to run, findings to track, documentation to keep current, users to support. As Cybersecurity Support Specialist, you will keep that work moving at a single Nooks site, supporting the security and compliance of classified and unclassified systems alongside the site's Cybersecurity Lead. You will bring two to five years of hands-on practice to a specialist seat, reporting to the Site IT/Cyber Manager as an individual contributor.

Our procedures are real but still maturing — audits, incidents, and new system standups will reshuffle your week, and you will step in wherever the site's security posture needs attention without waiting to be asked.

Key Responsibilities

Security Monitoring & Vulnerability Management

• Conduct vulnerability scanning, patch verification, and security configuration checks under the direction of the site Cybersecurity Lead.

• Monitor and audit the security posture of classified and unclassified systems, applying Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs).

• Track findings and remediation actions to closure, documented to organizational and Department of Defense (DoD) standards.

Compliance Documentation & Support

• Maintain cybersecurity documentation — System Security Plans (SSPs), Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms), audit logs, and standard operating procedures.

• Record compliance actions and evidence so the site is ready for audits and self-inspections at any time.

• Keep artifacts organized so the Cybersecurity Lead can hand assessors current documentation on demand.

User Support & Access Control

• Provide Tier 1 support for cybersecurity-related user requests, escalating issues that need deeper analysis.

• Manage user accounts, security groups, and permissions in partnership with the site's IT Support Specialist — you both work in this space, so clean records and communication matter.

• Support permissions reviews and the implementation of access control policies, including role-based access control.

Incident Response & Security Awareness

• Participate in incident response and continuous monitoring — log collection, basic analysis, and security control status reporting.

• Reinforce cybersecurity best practices with end users through daily interactions.

• Collaborate with IT, personnel security, and physical security teams to keep site operations compliant with DoW requirements.

What Success Looks Like in This Role

Twelve months in, the site's routine security workload — scans, checks, and documentation upkeep — runs on schedule with little prompting. The SSPs, POA&Ms, and audit artifacts you maintain are current enough to hand straight to an assessor. Tier 1 cybersecurity requests get resolved or escalated cleanly, and account and permissions records stay accurate through every review. Handoffs with the IT Support Specialist are smooth because the shared account work is documented and coordinated. The Cybersecurity Lead trusts your work enough to build audit responses on top of it.

Cross-Functional Expectations

Inside IT/Cyber, you will work most closely with your site's Cybersecurity Lead and IT Support Specialist, coordinating daily on shared account and access work. You will partner with Security on personnel and physical security touchpoints, and support Operations, specifically the Site Lead,  for site activities.

The Skillset

• 2–5 years of experience in cybersecurity, IT support, or system administration.

• DoD 8140.03/8570.01 Information Assurance Technical (IAT) Level II certification (e.g., CompTIA Security+), or the ability to obtain one within six months of hire.

• Hands-on experience with DISA STIGs and tools such as the Security Content Automation Protocol (SCAP) Compliance Checker and STIG Viewer.

• Familiarity with access control, vulnerability management, and system hardening, plus Active Directory — including Group Policy Object (GPO) and Organizational Unit (OU) structure.

• Foundational knowledge of Windows and Linux operating systems, networking, and common IT troubleshooting practices.

• Associate's or Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, or a related field — or equivalent practical experience.

• Strong documentation habits, attention to detail, and clear communication across IT and security functions.

Preferred:

• Familiarity with monitoring and scanning tools such as Tenable Nessus, ManageEngine, Splunk, antivirus platforms (e.g., ESET, Trellix), and other vulnerability and security information and event management (SIEM) tools.

• Prior DoW or cleared-environment exposure.

Compensation & Benefits

Base salary

Benefits: Medical, dental, vision, PTO, and 401(k).

Eligibility & Clearance

Candidates must be eligible to work in the United States and capable of maintaining eligibility up to the Top Secret/Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) level within 45 days of hire.

Salary Range for all departments

Salary Range

$103,000—$114,000 USD

jobs.title: Director, HR Business Partner (Technology)
jobs.description:
Heartflow is a medical technology company advancing the diagnosis and management of coronary artery disease, the #1 cause of death worldwide, using cutting-edge technology. The flagship product—an AI-driven, non-invasive cardiac test supported by the ACC/AHA Chest Pain Guidelines called the Heartflow FFRCT Analysis—provides a color-coded, 3D model of a patient’s coronary arteries indicating the impact blockages have on blood flow to the heart. About the Positions

We’re seeking Office Engineers of various skill levels to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. These positions run the construction office: submittals, RFIs, contract records, pay applications, and change documentation. You’ll keep that record complete and current so decisions on payment, time, and entitlement hold up months later under audit or claim review.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area. We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.

Responsibilities may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Note: We are seeking candidates of various skill levels, and the following responsibilities represent the core of these roles. Scope and complexity increase with experience level.

• May administer the program’s submittal and RFI process, logging, distributing, and tracking each item through technical review to a documented response within the contractual review period.

• Maintain the construction record set, including contract documents, plans, specifications, addenda, and as-built markups, so the current approved version is the one in use.

• Review pay applications and progress payment requests against verified quantities, the approved schedule of values, and contract terms, and route them for approval.

• Compile and track change order documentation, including entitlement records, independent estimate backup, and negotiation history, so the program’s position is documented before anything is executed.

• Monitor contract compliance items, including insurance certificates, bonds, certified payroll, DBE participation, and permit conditions, and escalate lapses before they affect payment.

• Coordinate document flow across active work areas and the contract packages they support.

• Reconcile field records, daily reports, and quantity documentation against contractor submissions so program records support payment decisions and claim review.

• Coordinate with contractors, designers, and agency staff to keep responses moving, and document review cycle delays and their cause when they occur.

• Prepare program progress reports, log summaries, and meeting minutes, and track open action items to closure.

• Organize the project’s document control structure, including naming conventions, version control, and retention, so the record survives audit, claim review, and funding review.

• Support schedule updates by reconciling schedule submissions against program records of submittals, RFIs, and change activity.

Attributes

• Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

• Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

• Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

• Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Minimum Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering, construction engineering, construction management, or engineering technology, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

• 5+ years of office engineering experience for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

• Experience administering submittal, RFI, and construction correspondence logs on an active construction program.

• Working knowledge of contract documents, technical specifications, and construction drawings, and of how pay applications and change orders are documented against them.

• Experience with industry standard document management and project / construction management software (e.g., Procore, e-Builder, Primavera P6, Unifier, Kahua, etc.).

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

• Master’s degree in civil engineering, construction engineering, construction management, or engineering technology.

• Active professional certifications such as CCM (CMAA), PMP (PMI), and/or CDT (CSI).

• Experience running the owner’s construction office records on a package exceeding $100M in construction value.

• Experience administering pay applications and progress payments on a program valued at $1B+.

• Experience assembling change order and claim documentation that was later relied on in negotiation, dispute review board, or audit.

• Understanding of public agency procedures and contract compliance requirements (e.g., FTA, FAA, state DOT, etc.).

• Experience with industry standard labor compliance and document collaboration software (e.g., LCPtracker, B2GNow, Bluebeam Revu, SharePoint, etc.).

• Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Just a couple of things to keep in mind: pay is based on where you're located, and you'll need to keep a home base in the country you're hired in. So while we love the "coffee shop today, mountains tomorrow" life, this isn't a passport-optional, work-from-anywhere-on-Earth kind of remote - think flexible within your country, not borderless.

About the Role:

As a member of the Integrations Team, you’ll manage end-to-end integrations, translate technical requirements into solutions, and ensure a smooth, successful deployment. This is a hands-on role working closely with clients and internal teams, perfect for someone who thrives in fast-paced environments and enjoys solving complex problems with practical, scalable solutions.

 - Lead implementation and integration efforts for fraud and compliance products

 - Own APIs, SDK documentation, integration guides, and overall support documents

jobs.title: Senior Radiopharmaceuticals Production Operator
jobs.description:
Telix Pharmaceuticals is a dynamic, fast-growing radiopharmaceutical company with offices in Australia (HQ), Belgium, Japan, Switzerland, and the United States. Our mission is to deliver on the promise of precision medicine through targeted radiation. At our core, we exist to create products that seek to improve the quality of life for people living with cancer and rare diseases. You will be supporting the international roll-out of our approved prostate cancer imaging agent and helping us to advance our portfolio of late clinical-stage products that address significant unmet need in oncology and rare diseases.

See Yourself at Telix

Performs complex radiochemical synthesis, purification, compounding, and quality control functions supporting PET biomarker production at a cyclotron facility, including set-up, operation, routine checks, and preventive maintenance of manufacturing equipment such as cyclotrons and automated chemistry modules. This non-exempt role performs and documents all quality control testing and plays a crucial part in ensuring that manufacturing and QC activities meet cGMP, radiation safety, and applicable State and Federal requirements.

This role is 5 days a week on-site at our Wilkes-Barre, PA location.

Key Accountabilities:

• Performs complex radiochemical synthesis, purification, and compounding of PET biomarkers, including use of cyclotrons and automated chemistry modules, in accordance with cGMP requirements for PET drug production and applicable radiation safety regulations.

• Partners with cross functional teams in process qualification and process improvement initiatives.

• Leads commissioning and equipment qualification activities, as necessary.

• Lead investigative efforts for manufacturing and process issues to support root-cause analysis and corrective action plan.

• Coordinate daily activities of Radiopharmaceutical Production Technicians while ensuring adherence to production schedules and quality requirements.

• Provides technical leadership and real-time problem resolution.

• Leads the development of manufacturing processes tech transfers and complex projects with communication of timelines to internal and external stakeholders.

• Executes quality control testing using analytical instrumentation (TLC, HPLC, GC); analyzes and interprets results against established specifications and documents outcomes in compliance with GxP requirements.

• Conducts complex inspections, maintenance, and troubleshooting to support manufacturing and testing processes and equipment.

• Implements approved SOP changes to production and quality control processes, helping drive continuous improvement.

• Performs daily, weekly, monthly, and quarterly PM checks of cyclotrons, chemistry modules, and QC equipment per SOPs.

• Oversees routine logistics functions, including preparing products for shipment, coordinating courier schedules, and documenting as necessary.

• Monitor and perform continuous process improvement and waste reduction initiatives.

• Maintains a clean, clutter-free facility and a well-organized production area and workflow.

• Provide technical coaching to Radiopharmaceutical Production Technician I & II

• Provides exemplary customer support.

• Other tasks as assigned by supervisor.

Education and Experience:

• Associates degree or certifications in Chemistry, Radiochemistry, Biochemistry, or a related field required.

• 4+years of experience in a laboratory setting, preferably in radiopharmaceuticals, or a related industry.

• Knowledge of radiochemical synthesis, purification, and safe handling of radioactive materials required.

• Advanced understanding of manufacturing processes and quality systems.

• Experience interpreting complex engineering documentation

• Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and manufacturing work instructions

• Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail.

• Ability to work in a team environment and communicate effectively with diverse groups.

• Familiarity with regulatory requirements such as GMP and radiation safety practices.

• Willingness to work with radioactive materials and follow strict safety protocols.

• Ability to lift up to 50 lbs.

Working Conditions:

• Work is performed in a cGMP radiopharmaceutical production facility containing a cyclotron, hot cells, automated chemistry modules, and quality control laboratory instrumentation.

• Routine handling of radioactive materials is required. The incumbent must qualify and remain in good standing as an authorized radiation worker under the site's radioactive materials license, complete all required radiation safety training, wear assigned dosimetry, and participate in radiation exposure monitoring programs.

• Personal protective equipment, including lab coats, gloves, safety eyewear, and shielding, is required in all production and QC areas. Gowning for classified cleanroom areas is required as applicable.

• Production schedules are driven by the short half-lives of PET radioisotopes. This role requires early morning, overnight, weekend, and holiday shifts, as well as on-call coverage and overtime as needed to meet patient dose delivery schedules. As a non-exempt role, all overtime must be approved in advance in accordance with company policy.

• Work involves exposure to chemical reagents, compressed gases, cryogenic materials, and high-voltage equipment, with controls applied through established SOPs and safety procedures.

• Physical demands include prolonged standing, repetitive manual manipulation of small components behind shielding, and lifting or moving materials and shielded containers with mechanical assistance where provided.

• Occasional travel between production sites may be required.

Key Capabilities:

• Commitment to excellence: Take pride in your work and consistently strive for excellence in everything you do

• Results-oriented: Driven to achieve goals and objectives, with a strong focus on delivering measurable results

• Creativity and innovation: Possess a willingness to think outside the box and come up with unique and creative solutions to challenges

• Strong communication skills: Able to communicate effectively with colleagues and stakeholders at all levels, using clear and concise language

• Collaboration: Work effectively as part of a team, actively sharing knowledge and expertise to achieve common goals

• Resilience: Demonstrate the ability to bounce back from setbacks and persevere in the face of challenges

• Inclusive mindset: Demonstrate an understanding and appreciation for diversity, and actively work to create an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued and respected

• Adaptability: Comfortable working in a dynamic environment, able to adjust to changing priorities, and willing to take on new challenges

• Ethical behavior: Act with integrity and demonstrate a commitment to ethical behavior in all interactions with colleagues and stakeholders

• Continuous learning: Show a commitment to ongoing learning and professional development, continually seeking out opportunities to expand your knowledge and skills

At Telix, we believe everyone counts, we strive to be extraordinary, and we pursue our goals with determination and integrity. You will be part of an engaged and supportive group of colleagues who all have a shared purpose: to help people with cancer and rare diseases live longer, better quality lives. Being a Telix employee means being a part of a unique, global, interdisciplinary team working to deliver what's next in precision medicine. We have hybrid and remote employees located all around the world.  We offer competitive salaries, annual performance-based bonuses, an equity-based incentive program, generous vacation, paid wellness days and support for learning and development.

Telix Pharmaceuticals is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, and other legally protected characteristics.

jobs.title: Software Engineering Intern (Embedded, Backend, Fullstack)
jobs.description:
Parallel Systems is pioneering autonomous battery-electric rail vehicles designed to transform freight transportation by shifting portions of the $900 billion U.S. trucking industry onto rail. Our innovative technology offers cleaner, safer, and more efficient logistics solutions. Join our dynamic team and help shape a smarter, greener future for global freight.

Software Engineering Interns

Parallel Systems is seeking Software Engineering Interns to help build the software that runs our vehicles and the platform behind our fleet. This is a hands-on role for someone who wants to ship real work. Your code will run on prototype vehicles, on test benches, or in the services and tools our team and operators rely on every day.

Interns are placed on a vehicle software or backend/full-stack project based on their background and team priorities. You will own a scoped project from requirements through delivery, work closely with a mentor, and see your work tested on real hardware or used by real users.

The right person is curious beyond their own layer. Whether you are writing firmware, building a service, or shipping an internal tool, you will learn how software, hardware, and vehicle data fit together, and you will be comfortable debugging across those boundaries.

What You Will Work On

You will contribute to a specific project scoped to team priorities. Example areas include:

• Vehicle control software: writing and testing code for braking, drivetrain, actuators, and power systems on microcontrollers or embedded Linux

• Vehicle communications: developing and validating interfaces across CAN, Ethernet, SPI, I2C, or UART, including bench debugging

• Sensor and diagnostics integration: bringing up onboard sensors and devices used for telemetry, health monitoring, and vehicle operation

• Fleet and telemetry services: building services and data pipelines that ingest, store, and serve data from vehicles in the field

• Fleet operations tools: building APIs and web applications used to monitor, dispatch, and manage vehicles

• Developer and test infrastructure: improving CI/CD, simulation, hardware-in-the-loop testing, deployment, and observability for the software team

Regardless of project, you will work through a structured engineering lifecycle: requirements review, design, implementation, testing, and documentation of results.

What to Expect

• Weeks 1-2: Onboarding, vehicle and software platform architecture overview, development environment setup, lab and shop orientation, codebase familiarization, and a first starter task

• Weeks 3-4: Project assignment, review of requirements and interfaces, and initial design and debugging work with your mentor

• Weeks 5-7: Core implementation, testing on the bench or in staging, and iteration through code and design reviews

• Weeks 8-10: Integration onto prototype vehicles or into production systems, test execution, issue investigation, and participation in team design reviews

• Weeks 11-12: Final validation and handoff, documentation of findings and recommended next steps, and a presentation of results to the broader engineering team

Progress will be tracked through weekly check-ins with your mentor, design and code reviews, and feedback from the broader engineering team.

Basic Requirements

• Currently pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, Mechatronics, or a related field

• Hands-on software experience through internships, student teams, research, coursework, or personal projects

• Strong programming skills in at least one language such as Rust, C, C++, Python, Go, or TypeScript

• A track record of building software that works in the real world, not only in class assignments or simulation

• Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to debug issues across system boundaries

• Clear communication, and comfort asking questions and sharing progress early

• Excitement about working in a hands-on, hard-tech environment where software meets physical vehicles

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with Rust, C, or C++ on microcontrollers or embedded Linux

• Familiarity with communication protocols such as CAN, SPI, I2C, UART, or Ethernet

• Experience building APIs, distributed services, data pipelines, or full-stack web applications

• Familiarity with databases, cloud infrastructure, containers, or CI/CD

• Exposure to RTOS environments, simulation, or hardware-in-the-loop testing

• Experience bringing up sensors, actuators, motor controllers, or other real electromechanical systems

• Experience from hands-on extracurricular engineering teams such as Formula SAE, Baja SAE, robotics, rocket club, solar car, autonomous systems teams, or similar

• Strong documentation habits and attention to detail

Please note the hourly range in the job posting reflects the new hire hourly range across levels that would be applicable to the position. Final compensation will be commensurate with the candidate’s final level. Also, this range represents base compensation only and does not include equity or benefits, if applicable.

$50—$50 USD

jobs.title: Site Optimization Manager
jobs.description:
About Life360

Life360’s mission is to keep people close to the ones they love. Our category-leading mobile app, Tile tracking devices, and Pet GPS tracker empower members to protect the people, pets, and things they care about most with a range of services, including location sharing, safe driver reports, and crash detection with emergency dispatch. Life360 serves approximately 102.4 million monthly active users (MAU), as of June 30, 2026, across more than 180 countries.

Life360 delivers peace of mind and enhances everyday family life with seamless coordination for all the moments that matter, big and small. By continuing to innovate and deliver for our customers, we have become a household name and the must-have mobile-based membership for families (and those friends who are basically family).

Life360 has more than 500 (and growing!) remote-first employees. For more information, please visit life360.com.

Life360 is a Remote First company, which means a remote work environment will be the primary experience for all employees. All positions, unless otherwise specified, can be performed remotely (within the US and Canada) regardless of any specified location above.

We are AI Native

We are building an AI native company where AI is an integral part of how we build and operate. AI tool usage during interviews varies by role. You may be asked to demonstrate proficiency with AI tools, discuss how you leverage AI, or complete interview exercises without AI assistance. Your Recruiter will provide clear guidance as you move through the interview process.

Undisclosed use of AI not previously discussed with or approved by your Recruiter may impact your candidacy.

About The Team

As you'd expect from a company obsessed with keeping families connected, the eCommerce team moves fast and takes the member experience seriously – because a clunky flow is its own kind of broken promise. Sitting inside Journey Marketing, we're a mix of merchandisers, marketers, data folks, and designers who all care about the same thing: turning every member touchpoint — from first website or app visit — into long-term loyalty and lasting relationships. From the online store to in-app purchases to wherever commerce shows up next, this team builds the experience that turns interest into purchase. If you like owning outcomes, thinking in systems, and turning "maybe" into "yes" at scale, you'll fit right in.

About the Job

At Life360, our web experience is one of the most important drivers of device sell-through and subscription growth. Making smart decisions about that experience requires performance visibility – always knowing what's happening on the site, where customers are dropping off, and why.

The Site Optimization Manager drives continuous improvement of Life360's digital commerce experience through experimentation, behavioral analysis, and data-driven optimization. You'll manage the day-to-day execution of our web experimentation and personalization programs, translating customer insights and performance data into measurable improvements in conversion, engagement, and revenue.

This is a hands-on role for someone who combines analytical rigor with strong technical execution. You'll identify opportunities, develop hypotheses, build and launch experiments, and translate results into actionable recommendations. Working closely with Web Experience, Analytics, Product, Engineering, and Merchandising, you'll help accelerate our optimization roadmap and build a scalable culture of experimentation.

For candidates based in the US, the salary range for this position is $121,000 to $178,500 USD. For candidates based out of Canada, the salary range for this position is 141,000 to 165,000 CAD. We take into consideration an individual’s background, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience in determining final salary. Base pay may also vary based on geographic location, with US work locations falling into one of three geographic tiers.

Total compensation is inclusive of equity compensation in the form of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), as well as a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, vision, financial, and other benefits.

What You’ll Do

• Monitor site performance continuously, surfacing regressions, anomalies, and emerging trends proactively — bringing a diagnosis with business context and recommended next action alongside every flag, not just the data.

• Identify conversion optimization opportunities by synthesizing quantitative funnel data with qualitative signals — session recordings, heatmaps, and usability findings — to understand where and why customers experience friction and prioritize opportunities for improvement.

• Partner with Analytics to define measurement requirements, ensure visibility into key site performance KPIs, and leverage dashboards tracking CVR, funnel step drop-off, AOV, and session quality across key web surfaces and conversion flows.

• Own the day-to-day operation of Life360's web A/B and multivariate testing program, including test scoping, configuration, builds, QA, traffic allocation, and post-test documentation, ensuring experiments are instrumented correctly and results are interpreted with statistical rigor.

• Maintain and groom the live experiment backlog in partnership with the Director, ensuring tests are scoped clearly, sequenced logically, and launched on time.

• Analyze test results with rigor in partnership with Analytics, evaluating statistical significance, sizing revenue impact, and producing clear readouts that drive confident go/no-go decisions and inform future optimization opportunities.

• Manage personalization campaign operations — maintaining segment-to-experience workflows, coordinating with UX/UI and Merchandising on creative, and tracking lift versus baseline for each active experience.

• Partner with Digital Product, Engineering, Marketing, and Analytics on experimentation platform configuration, feature flag governance, event instrumentation QA, and tagging validation.

• Support hands-on site optimization execution across experimentation, personalization, and content updates, leveraging CMS, commerce platforms, and no-code/low-code tools to implement and QA experiences where appropriate.

• Translate performance insights into actionable recommendations, partnering with Analytics on reporting and contributing optimization findings, experiment outcomes, and prioritized opportunities to weekly and monthly business reviews.

• Contribute to the financial modeling process by sizing expected lift for proposed tests and reconciling actuals to projections post-launch.

• Document experimentation best practices, maintain the team's testing Confluence, and help build institutional knowledge around what works on Life360's web properties.

What We’re Looking For

• 4–6 years of experience in eCommerce or digital analytics, with at least 2 years of hands-on ownership of an experimentation program in a fast-paced commercial environment. Ideally within a hardware + subscription business.

• Proficiency with Statsig preferred or equivalent experimentation platform (Optimizely, VWO, Adobe Target, Dynamic Yield, etc) – you've built and QA'd tests yourself, not just read the reports.

• Familiarity with headless commerce architectures, content management systems (CMS), and modern eCommerce platforms such as BigCommerce and Contentful. Comfortable navigating the technical dependencies of site changes, experimentation, and personalization across commerce and content platforms.

• Strong analytical foundation – you're fluent in GA4, Amplitude, or a comparable analytics platform, can write SQL to pull your own data, and are comfortable building and maintaining dashboards in Looker, Tableau, or similar tools. You understand the statistics behind experimentation well enough to push back when a test is being called too early.

• Experience with personalization tools and segment-based targeting; familiarity with how audience definitions, traffic splits, and experience variants are configured in practice.

• Experience leveraging AI-powered tools to accelerate analysis, identify customer behavior patterns, generate and refine experimentation hypotheses, and improve operational efficiency. Curious about emerging AI capabilities and how they can be applied to digital experience optimization.

• Detail-oriented operator with strong project management instincts — you can run multiple tests simultaneously, keep stakeholders informed, and maintain clean documentation without being asked.

• Collaborative working style with the ability to partner effectively with Product, Engineering, UX/UI, Site Merchandising, and Analytics teams.

• Clear communicator who can translate performance data into plain-language insights for non-technical stakeholders.

• Curiosity-driven: you follow the data wherever it leads, ask good questions, and treat every test as an opportunity to learn something about the customer.

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent.

Our Benefits

• Medical, dental, vision, life and disability insurance plans (100% paid for US employees). We offer life and disability as well as supplemental plans for medical and dental for Canadian employees.

• 401(k) plan with company matching program in the US and RRSP with DPSP plan for Canadian employees.

• Paid parental leave.

• Mental Wellness Program & Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for mental well-being.

• Generous time off: flexible PTO, companywide holidays throughout the year plus summer and winter shutdowns.

• Learning & Development programs.

• Equipment, tools, and reimbursement support for a productive remote environment.

• Free Life360 Platinum Membership and Tile trackers.

Life360 Values

Our company’s mission-driven culture is guided by our shared values to create a trusted work environment where you can bring your authentic self to work and make a positive difference

• Be a Good Person - We have a team of high integrity people you can trust.

• Be Direct With Respect - We communicate directly, even when it’s hard.

• Members Before Metrics - We focus on building an exceptional experience for families.

• High Intensity, High Impact - We do whatever it takes to get the job done.

Our Commitment to Diversity

We believe that different ideas, perspectives and backgrounds create a stronger and more creative work environment that delivers better results. Together, we continue to build an inclusive culture that encourages, supports, and celebrates the diverse voices of our employees. It fuels our innovation and connects us closer to our customers and the communities we serve. We strive to create a workplace that reflects the communities we serve and where everyone feels empowered to bring their authentic best selves to work.

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at Life360. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status or any legally protected status.

We encourage people of all backgrounds to apply. We believe that a diversity of perspectives and experiences create a foundation for the best ideas. Come join us in building something meaningful. Even if you don’t meet 100% of the above qualifications, you should still seriously consider applying!

jobs.title: Clinical Operations Specialist - Licensed Therapist
jobs.description:
CLINICAL OPERATIONS SPECIALIST – LICENSED THERAPIST

Employment Type: Full-time, Salaried
Reports To: Clinical Director
Location: Remote/Hybrid - preference for LA based applicants, may consider others with extraordinary experience.  
Compensation: $83,000–$100,000 per year (commensurate with experience)
Equity: Offered
Benefits: 401(k), full health, dental, and vision insurance, generous unlimited PTO package
Role Type: Licensed Clinician
Caseload: No Caseload Requirement

 


ROLE SUMMARY

The Clinical Operations Specialist is a licensed therapist who provides critical support to clinical operations, leveraging their expertise to address issues involving patients, providers, documentation, quality, and care delivery. This role acts as a bridge between clinicians and the organization’s operational, product, quality, credentialing, and care-coordination teams. Other duties may be assigned as needed.

 


QUALIFICATIONS

 - Independent clinical license required: LCSW, LMFT, LPC, or PhD/PsyD (or state equivalent)

 - Minimum of 4 years post-licensure clinical experience

 - Experience with Electronic Health Record (EHR) systems required

 - No specific EHR or scheduling platform experience necessary; training will be provided

 - Comfortable working in a hybrid clinical/operational role (not traditional caseload-based)

 - Strong cross-functional communication skills to collaborate with Product, Quality, Credentialing, and Operations teams

 - Self-motivated and able to work independently in a remote/hybrid environment

 


RESPONSIBILITIES


1. MEMBER AND CLINICAL SUPPORT

 - Serve as a clinical resource for member issues requiring clinical judgment

 - Support pre-intake clinical review and outreach as needed

 - Review and follow up on member feedback requiring clinical attention

 - Manage rematch escalations and assist with enrollment-related clinical questions

 - Collaborate with the User-Success team to address member needs

 - Handle clinical escalations beyond the scope of non-licensed operations staff

 - Conduct consultation hours as needed

 - Participate in clinical interviews during periods of active hiring

 


2. CLINICAL QUALITY AND DOCUMENTATION

 - Address documentation issues requiring clinical interpretation or provider-to-provider communication

 - Support clinical review of incomplete or missing diagnoses

 - Participate in clinical quality initiatives and audits

 - Support and educate providers on clinical documentation standards

 - Participate in payer and similar clinically-oriented audits

 - Collaborate on quality-improvement initiatives

 - Review caseload and documentation integrity

 


3. THERAPIST DATA AND CLINICAL METRICS

 - Work with Product and Clinical Leadership on workforce and quality metrics

 - Use internal reporting and quality-monitoring tools

 - Interpret metrics for full-time/part-time providers

 - Identify trends in clinical quality and areas needing follow-up

 - Partner with technical teams as reporting and automation tools evolve

 


4. CLINICAL MEETINGS AND CROSS-FUNCTIONAL REPRESENTATION

 - Represent Clinical Operations in cross-functional meetings (Clinical x Product, User-Success x Clinical, team meetings, Credentialing/Quality Committees, organizational meetings)

 - Serve as a clinical liaison to other departments requiring clinical expertise

 


5. MEDICATION MANAGEMENT OPERATIONS

 - Assist with manual rescheduling of medication-management follow-ups when necessary

 - Address exceptions to automated medication-management workflows

 - Support resolution of escalated prior-authorization issues

 - Handle documentation requests (e.g., FMLA, short-term disability) needing clinical review

 - Draft physician-facing documentation for review and signature

 - Coordinate member communication about documentation appointments

 - Support related scheduling changes

 


6. CLINICAL PROCESS IMPROVEMENT AND SPECIAL PROJECTS

 - Identify and propose improvements to clinical workflows

 - Collaborate with Product and Engineering for clinical input

 - Translate clinician and patient needs into operational or product requirements

 - Participate in clinical process redesigns and special projects needing clinical expertise

 - Help develop scalable clinical workflows as the organization grows

 


7. OTHER CLINICAL DUTIES AS REQUIRED

 

Marvin Behavioral Health is committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We encourage applicants from all backgrounds and identities to apply.

Earn up to $95 per session helping California adolescents and adults thrive!

Join our mission to make quality mental healthcare accessible to every person who needs it. At Daybreak Health, you'll be part of a movement dedicated to removing barriers to care and empowering young people to thrive emotionally and mentally.

Every session you lead has the power to change someone's trajectory, and that's just the beginning of the impact you'll make.

jobs.title: Systems Analyst
jobs.description:
Evio Overview

Evio is a highly unique pharmacy solutions company that was founded by and works closely with health plans to implement transformative (to cost, quality, access and experience) initiatives primarily focused on specialty and other high-cost medication solutions.

In 2020, a group of five amazing Blue Cross Blue Shield health plans that in total serve more than 20 million members recognized that the way medications get to patients needs significant reform—rapidly rising costs and massive system complexities are detrimental to patients and the entire industry. In 2025, Wellmark joined as Evio's first non-founding investor and sixth owner health plan. Each company made, and continues to make, significant investments to establish Evio as an independent entity to lead this transformation.

Evio has advanced analytics and contracting capabilities at scale, and a suite of digital tools, to power our high-cost medication solutions. Our solutions act as a self-reinforcing “flywheel” where each element strengthens and feeds into the next, and support an “Only Evio can do that,” mindset and prioritization.

Evio is also a company that has invested heavily in and been highly intentional about people, team and culture. We believe we have created a very special place to work and encourage candidates to observe and ask us about our culture and decide for themselves.

Evio's Values

• Empathy – The people our business serves always come first. We care for our teammates and put ourselves in the shoes of our health plan customers and the patients and clinicians our solutions benefit.

• Diversity – We are committed to fostering a culture where everyone belongs and is valued for their background, experience and insights – one that encourages diversity of ideas, and is a nurturing, trusting, and accepting place for all.

• Adventure – We are flexible, thrive in ambiguity, fail fast, and pivot quickly to get to a better answer. We celebrate wins and pivots with equal intensity.

• Relentless – Guided by evidence and data, we are creative, curious, and unwavering in our pursuit of challenging the status quo and each other.

• Transparency – Just as we seek to bring transparency to the pharmacy supply chain, authenticity and integrity are core to the way we communicate.

• Excellence – We strive to raise the bar in all we do by hiring and developing exceptional talent and holding ourselves and our thinking to the highest standard.

Systems Analyst Role

About the role:

Evio and the six health plans we represent are uniquely positioned in the market and have demonstrated success in creating innovative partnerships with pharmaceutical manufacturers. As the regulatory environment for health plans, PBMs/GPOs, and manufacturers rapidly evolves over the next several years, Evio is expanding our direct manufacturer contracting capabilities and growing the team supporting this work. The Systems Analyst role will translate medication contracting and operational needs into reliable systems, workflows, and data requirements that support this growing business.

You’ll work closely with medication contracting and operations teammates, product leaders, developers, data teams, and external partners to understand business processes and turn them into clear system requirements. You’ll also help test and implement application changes, investigate system and data issues, and ensure solutions work as intended for the teammates using them.

We’re looking for someone who can bring structure to complex operational and data requirements, communicate clearly with both business and technical teammates, and follow details through from requirements to testing and implementation.

What you’ll do:

• Partner with business and technical teams to understand and prioritize operational needs and translate them into functional requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, workflows, data mappings, and system specifications.

• Develop a detailed understanding of the medication contracting processes and the operational workflows supported by assigned applications. Document current- and future-state workflows and identify practical opportunities to improve efficiency, data quality, and user experience.

• Collaborate with developers and vendors to ensure delivered functionality meets approved requirements.

• Help prioritize application enhancements based on business value, operational impact, dependencies, and implementation effort.

• Define data requirements, validation rules, business rules, and source-to-target mappings.

• Use SQL, Excel, and other analytical tools to investigate data issues, validate application behavior, and reconcile system outputs.

• Plan and support application testing, including test cases, expected results, representative test data, user acceptance testing, regression testing, and release validation.

• Document defects clearly, investigate whether issues stem from data, configuration, process, integrations, or application functionality, and work with technical teams through resolution and retesting.

• Create and maintain application guides, process documentation, data definitions, training materials, and release communications.

• Train business users and support teams on new workflows and application functionality, explaining technical changes in clear, practical language.

• Help ensure applications maintain appropriate access controls, approval workflows, auditability, and documentation.

Your skills and experience:

• 5+ years of experience as a Systems Analyst, Business Systems Analyst, Product Analyst, or in a similar role supporting complex business applications.

• Bachelor’s degree in information systems, business, healthcare administration, data analytics, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.

• Demonstrated experience translating operational processes into functional requirements, workflows, data mappings, user stories, and acceptance criteria.

• Experience developing test cases, coordinating user acceptance testing, documenting defects, and validating system releases.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including experience investigating data discrepancies, validating system outputs, and bringing structure to ambiguous or conflicting requirements.

• Advanced Excel skills and working proficiency with SQL.

• Ability to interpret detailed business rules, contracts, pricing terms, or financial requirements.

• Experience working with software developers, data engineers, product managers, business stakeholders, and external vendors.

• Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to document complex requirements and explain processes effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences.

Preferred qualifications:

• Experience in healthcare, pharmacy benefits, pharmaceutical contracting, rebate operations, health plan operations, or a related area.

• Familiarity with healthcare product and drug reference data, including NDC and HCPCS codes.

• Experience supporting contracting, pharmaceutical RFP proposal management, financial, pricing, or operational workflow applications.

• Experience working with APIs, structured data files, secure file transfers, or system integrations.

• Familiarity with Agile product development and tools such as Jira and Confluence.

• Experience supporting applications in a regulated environment with defined privacy, security, access-control, and audit requirements.

Salary Considerations:

Anticipated annual base pay range: $95,000 - $110,000 with additional variable compensation.

At Evio, we’re committed to building a competitive compensation package to honor the value our teammates bring as well as attract and retain top talent that is aligned with our culture, mission and values.  Please note that the base pay information shown is a general guideline for the job responsibilities and qualifications listed. Salary decisions are based on candidate experience, market, and business considerations.

Evio Benefits:

• Great Health Insurance The company pays 100% of medical, dental, and vision premiums for teammates, and 50% for dependents.

• 401K Match Evio matches 100% of teammate contribution up to 5% of salary, subject to IRS limits.

• Time Off We have a flexible vacation policy for teammates to unplug and recharge when you need it. There is no minimum or maximum amount of vacation allowed per year, and there is no payment in consideration for unused vacation. Vacation is to be used at your discretion, with approval of leadership.

• Parental Leave Generous paid leave for new parents (includes birth and non-birth parents).

Fraud Notice

We’ve recently learned of fraudulent job postings and individuals falsely claiming to represent Evio. Protecting our candidates is incredibly important to us, and we want to share a few reminders:

• All official communication will come from an email ending in @evio.com.

• We will never conduct text-only interviews (Teams, SMS, WhatsApp, Telegram, etc.).

• We will never ask for payment, gift cards, fees, or purchases of any kind.

• We will never request sensitive financial information during the recruiting process.

• Our open roles are posted only on our official website, LinkedIn, and Greenhouse job board.

If you believe you’ve encountered a scam, you can also report it to the Federal Trade Commission or the Internet Crime Complaint Center. Thank you for your care and vigilance — we’re grateful to everyone who helps keep our community safe.

Information Disclosure

We value transparency in our hiring process and want applicants to understand how your information is used.

We collect and use personal information you provide during the application process such as your resume, employment history, education, interview responses, and other job-related information, to evaluate your qualifications for employment. This may also include limited technical and interaction data, such as IP address and device or browser information.

We may use automated or AI-assisted tools to help review applications, identify qualified candidates, and detect or investigate potentially fraudulent or deceptive activity. Human reviewers remain involved, and these tools support, not replace, human judgment.

These measures support a fair and secure hiring process for all candidates. If you require a reasonable accommodation, please inform us when invited to interview.

California privacy notice Consistent with California law, we use this information for recruiting, hiring, and related business purposes, including evaluating your candidacy and improving our hiring processes.

jobs.title: GTM Finance Manager
jobs.description:
From Fivetran’s founding until now, our mission has remained the same: to make access to data as simple and reliable as electricity. With Fivetran, customer data arrives in their warehouses, canonical and ready to query, with no engineering or maintenance required. We’re proud that more organizations continue to leverage our technology every day to become truly data-driven.

About Us

Fivetran and dbt Labs are bringing together two industry-leading companies with a shared mission: helping organizations unlock the full value of their data.

Together, we’re delivering the data infrastructure layer that helps organizations move, transform, and trust their data — from the moment data moves, through every transformation, to the context teams and AI systems rely on.

Fivetran helps organizations automate data movement across the systems, clouds, engines, and tools they rely on. dbt Labs pioneered analytics engineering, helping teams transform data into reliable, governed insights. Together, we support thousands of organizations as they build a trusted foundation for analytics, AI, and better business decisions.

As we bring our teams and technology together, we’re building on the strengths of both companies while continuing to deliver the products and experiences our customers know and trust. It’s an exciting time to join us: we’re creating a company with the scale, talent, and technology to help more organizations put their data to work with greater speed, confidence, and impact.

During this transition period, you may see references to both Fivetran and dbt Labs throughout our recruiting process as we integrate our teams, systems, and career sites.

About the Role

Fivetran is building data pipelines to power the modern data stack for thousands of companies.

As the Manager on the GTM Finance and Strategy team, you’ll operate at the center of go-to-market strategy — owning and building critical models to forecast ARR and GAAP Revenue, analyzing and providing perspective around strategic initiatives, and delivering insights that shape executive and Board decisions. You’ll partner closely with Analytics, Revenue Accounting, Revenue Operations, External Reporting, and GTM leadership.

This role reports to the Sr. Manager of GTM Finance and blends strategic finance, data storytelling, technical problem-solving, and operational execution. You’ll drive forward-looking planning, help scale our forecasting infrastructure for a hybrid pricing motion that includes both subscription contracts and usage-based (consumption) revenue, and support high-visibility initiatives across the function.

This is a high-impact role ideal for someone who is passionate about leveraging data and financial insight to guide strategy and operational execution in a high-growth, cross-functional environment.

This is a full-time, hybrid position based out of our Oakland, CA or Denver, CO office. Our hybrid work model offers a blend of remote flexibility and in-person collaboration, including two days in the office each week to connect and build as a team.

Tools/Technologies You’ll Use

Claude / ChatGPT, Looker, SFDC, BigQuery, G-Suite

What You’ll Do

• Revenue Modeling & Forecasting: Own and re-evaluate our rolling GAAP revenue and ARR forecast models, including renewal behavior (NRR), new business, and contract-level revenue recognition across subscription and consumption-based streams. Evolve forecasting frameworks using both deterministic and AI/ML-driven approaches.

• Usage-Based Revenue: Build and maintain forecasting approaches for consumption revenue, including committed vs. overage usage, breakage, and the migration of customers between pricing models

• Business Partnering: Serve as a key advisor and partner to COO, CFO, and collaboration with Analytics, delivering actionable insights to improve efficiency, optimize investments, and accelerate growth.

• Strategic Decision Support: Deliver analysis that informs GTM investment, pricing and packaging, and target setting, and quantify the revenue impact of key business risks and opportunities

• Budgeting & Forecasting: Support annual planning and monthly/quarterly forecast cycles; partner closely with Revenue Accounting on close, variance analysis, and forecast-to-actual (BvA) tracking

• Performance Analysis: Own key revenue and retention metric packages — including NRR, ARPA, new business mix, ROI, and cohort trends — and surface insights to the CFO, executives, and the Board

• Forecast & Reporting Infrastructure: Use AI Tools, or SQL (BigQuery) / Python to automate data pulls, build repeatable and auditable models, and improve the accuracy, speed, and transparency of our topline forecast; partner with Analytics, AI Transformation and Systems on data quality, integrity and self-serve reporting capabilities.

• Executive Reporting: Create compelling, automated, executive-ready reports, dashboards, and narratives that distill complex data, trends, forecasts, and strategic implications into actionable recommendations for Finance leadership and GTM stakeholders.

• Team Leadership: Provide technical guidance, review work, and help raise the modeling standards and work products of the GTM FP&A team

Skills We’re Looking For

• 5-7 years of experience in FP&A, strategic finance, revenue finance, or investment banking, with a strong focus on revenue forecasting

• Expert-level modeling skills (Excel/Sheets) with a commitment to formula-driven, driver based, auditable, well-documented models

• Experience with usage-based or consumption pricing models strongly preferred

• Technical aptitude: working proficiency in SQL, Python, or similar scripting, and hands-on use of AI tools to accelerate and elevate modeling, strategic analysis, and QA; experience with BI tools (e.g., Looker) and data warehouses (e.g., BigQuery, Snowflake) a plus

• Ownership mindset: takes a model or process from ambiguity to a repeatable, documented workflow with minimal oversight, including QA and reconciliation to source data

• Data storytelling: translates complex data into clear insights and recommendations for senior, non-finance audiences, with strong executive presence and attention to detail

• Demonstrated ability to partner cross-functionally and influence without authority

• Excellent communication skills with high attention to detail and executive presence

• Adaptable, resourceful, and excited by the challenge of working in a fast-moving, growth-stage company

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Infrastructure
jobs.description:
ABOUT KEYCARD

At Keycard, we're building identity and access infrastructure for the agent-native era, where software isn't static but a dynamic, constantly changing system of AI agents working on behalf of people and businesses. Keycard gives every agent a verified identity and issues short-lived, task-scoped credentials at runtime, so agents can only do what they were asked to do, and every action is fully auditable. We're backed by a16z, Boldstart, and Acrew, and our founding team built and scaled Snyk, Auth0, HashiCorp, and Heroku.


THE ROLE

We're hiring a staff-level Software Engineer, Infrastructure to build and own how Keycard is deployed and run: in our multi-tenant cloud, in dedicated single-tenant cells, and in our customers' own cloud accounts.

Keycard is a control plane for agents: identity, credential exchange, delegation, policy, and audit. Many of the enterprises adopting it need that control plane inside their own cloud, behind their network controls, with no standing access for us. Bring-your-own-cloud (BYOC) is a product at Keycard, not a services engagement. It's versioned, documented, and held to the same bar as our hosted service.

You'll own BYOC end to end, along with the infrastructure that runs every Keycard cell. You'll work directly with founders, the engineers building our identity and policy services, and the customers running Keycard in their own cloud. Your priority is the platform that makes customer-hosted deployments repeatable. Installs and support shouldn't swallow the job; you'll agree to escalation and on-call with engineering. We build on AWS (and at some point - GCP, and Azure), EKS, Pulumi, and Helm.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - BYOC product. Own what it's like to install, upgrade, and get support for Keycard in a customer's cloud, from what their security team reviews to how each version is documented.

 - Compatibility. Decide what we support, from clouds, regions, and Kubernetes versions to customer guardrails like SCPs and egress proxies. Set the skew limits and deprecation policy that keep our control plane and customer cells compatible.

 - Cells everywhere. Make a new cell, ours or a customer's, a configuration change: infrastructure as code, account bootstrap, and network patterns like PrivateLink and certificates that work through customer proxies. For example: take a new customer's AWS account to a running, upgradeable cell with no standing access from us.

 - Releases. Get releases to many independently versioned cells with staged promotion, approval gates, and rollback. Operate those cells without standing access, with observability, runbooks, and audited break-glass.

 - Agent operations. Build agents for the repetitive work: pre-install checks, installs, failed-upgrade triage, and runbook drafts. They run with scoped credentials, every action is audited, and an engineer approves any change to a customer account.

 - Cost per install. Keep each install cheap in engineering time and cloud spend. Decide what's standard, what's configurable, and what we decline, so one customer's request doesn't become the roadmap.

 - Cell guardrails. Work through reviews with customers' cloud and security teams. With security, set the guardrails for every cell, from credential scope and isolation to workload identity and PKI, then build and run them.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - You build infrastructure as software in Pulumi, Terraform, or CDK, and write the Go or TypeScript tooling around it. You've run Kubernetes and Helm in production.

 - Deep AWS experience, especially IAM and permission boundaries, Organizations and SCPs, and VPC networking.

 - You've run software in accounts you don't control, like customer VPCs, on-prem, or regulated networks, and supported it through upgrades.

 - You've shipped versioned releases that customers upgrade on their own schedule, with a support matrix and deprecations they could plan around.

 - You debug across layers: a hung request that turns out to be a security group rule, a proxy that breaks a TLS handshake, a certificate challenge that can't reach the internet.

 - You've worked directly with customers' platform and security teams, and turned down a one-off when a product change was better.

 - You've made hard trade-offs to ship something now without boxing in the long-term system.

 - You write clear plans and async updates, and know when to jump on a call.

 - Agents at work. You already use coding agents in infrastructure work and have a clear view of where they're reliable and where a human has to review.


STRONG CANDIDATES MAY ALSO HAVE

 - Experience building a BYOC, single-tenant, or self-hosted offering at an infrastructure, data, or security company.

 - GCP or Azure alongside AWS, including private connectivity on those clouds.

 - Workload identity and PKI in production: SPIFFE/SPIRE, cert-manager, private CAs.

 - Experience with OAuth, OIDC, or mTLS, and interest in agent protocols like MCP.


YOUR FIRST 90 DAYS

 - Take our first customer-hosted deployment from pre-production to production with the customer.

 - Install for a second customer without bespoke work, starting from the templates, bootstrap, and pre-install checks the first one produced.

 - Publish the first BYOC support matrix and upgrade policy.

 - Agree a BYOC roadmap with product and engineering, including which operational work moves to agents.


WHO WILL LOVE THIS JOB

 - You want to build a product that runs in someone else's cloud and make it as solid as one you host.

 - You'd rather fix the product than repeat a custom install.


WHAT WE OFFER

 - Build at the Frontier: Work every day at the frontier of agent-native systems — shipping, inventing, and iterating on technology that hasn’t been built before. You’ll be given huge autonomy, the opportunity to gain mastery, and the chance to work in a team that holds each other accountable to succeed.

 - Truly Agent-Native Culture: At Keycard, we don’t just enable others to adopt agents — we use them ourselves to build. You’ll help shape an organization that embeds AI into its foundation as an enduring competitive advantage.

 - Compensation With Upside: Market-competitive salaries and generous equity packages (4-year vest, 1-year cliff) give you the security to focus on building — and the asymmetric upside of ownership in a company chasing a category-defining mission.

 - Comprehensive Benefits & Recharge: Health, dental, vision, and paramedical coverage for you and your family, plus 4 weeks vacation, 11 statutory holidays, and 1 volunteer day annually. We encourage at least 2 weeks off each year to fully recharge.

 - Tools That Keep You Ahead: A new MacBook Pro, a $500 stipend for peripherals, and the best AI tools available so you can work at the forefront of agent-native workflows.

 - Remote-First Flexibility: We are a remote-first team prioritizing asynchronous collaboration, with hiring focused in North and South America. Work where you’re strongest — we just want the best.
