• Experience leading Federal, DefenseTech and Industrial R&D engagements

• Experience tuning quantum algorithms and benchmarking across different quantum modalities, as well as classical SOTA. Expertise in resource estimation and calculating cross-over points.

• Mastery of Python and Qiskit or similar quantum SDK. Working knowledge of C++ or other low-level language

• Evidence of putting customers and mission first, and exceeding expectations

• Excellent collaboration and communication skills

• Must reside in New Mexico

Preferred Qualifications:

• Experience working in the quantum solutions industry e.g. solutions group at quantum computing company or industrial company with a quantum department

• Experience developing software using agentic-AI e.g. Codex, Opus or similar AI assistants including developing rapid prototypes to iterate with customers

The total compensation package includes base, bonus, equity, and a range of benefit options found on our career site.

$160,000—$200,000 USD

jobs.title: Staff Product Designer
jobs.description:
ABOUT NOOKS.AI http://Nooks.ai:

Nooks is an applied AI lab building the Agent Workspace for GTM. We design AI agents that operate across the full sales action set, from account strategy to prospect research and outreach. Building 0→1 has never been easier, but selling at the speed of the market remains the last frontier for AI. Our mission is to 10x every seller by automating the busywork so they can focus on what humans do best: closing deals.

Today, over 2000 customers run on Nooks, including Notion, HubSpot, Cursor, and Rippling. We've raised over 70M USD from top VCs like Kleiner Perkins, and we've at least tripled ARR each year for 3 years running. 




ABOUT THE ROLE

Sales software was built for humans. We believe agents will do most sales work within the next two years. Reps already spend 4+ hours a day in Nooks across AI Dialer, AI Prospecting, AI Sequencing, and Agent Studio — and each of those grew up as its own product.

We're hiring a staff product designer to turn them into one workspace, and to define what it looks like for a person and a team of agents to sell together. Nobody has designed this yet. You'll be the one to do it. This is an IC role, working closely with our head of design.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Set the design direction for the Agent Workspace. Define the interaction model, information architecture, and core patterns that unify our product lines. Make the calls other designers and engineers build against.

 - Design the human-agent loop. When should an agent act on its own, ask first, or hand work back? How does a rep review what agents did across 500 accounts overnight, fix what's wrong, and trust them more tomorrow? Turn model capabilities and failure modes into interfaces reps rely on all day.

 - Ship end to end, in code. Go from a customer problem to production. Prototype and build with real model output, ship front-end changes alongside engineers, sweat the details. Agree on the success metric with your PM and iterate until it moves.

 - Work directly with customers. Our biggest accounts have shared Slack channels with the team. You'll join calls, shadow reps during dial sessions, and watch how teams actually use what you shipped.

 - Raise the design bar across the company. Partner with our head of design to shape how a small team works: evolve the design system, run the hardest crits, raise the craft of the designers around you, and help us hire as the team grows.


YOU MIGHT BE A STRONG FIT IF

 - 8+ years of product design experience, including time leading design for a meaningful product area, as a founding designer, or as the designer others turn to.

 - A portfolio of shipped work on complex, high-frequency tools — products people live in for hours a day, like B2B workflow, productivity, developer, or pro tools.

 - You've shipped AI-powered features. You've designed around non-deterministic output, latency, and errors, and you've worked with engineers on prompts or evals to improve the experience.

 - You're a systems thinker with taste. You can move from platform architecture to a hover state in the same afternoon.

 - You build in code. You prototype and ship front-end work daily with tools like Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex, and you're comfortable in a production React/TypeScript codebase.

 - Strong opinions, held loosely, about what human-agent collaboration should look like.

 - Not afraid to hop on a call with a customer to validate something you just designed. Sales domain experience is a plus, not a requirement.

 - You make the rest of the company faster.

 - Based in San Francisco, excited to be in-office 3+ days per week.

Great designers don't always match every line here. If the problem excites you, apply.



AT NOOKS, YOU'LL ENJOY

 - A world-class team. 3 designers and ~40 engineers, mostly former founders, founding engineers, and veteran builders from places like Applied Intuition, Scale, Uber, Citadel, and Jane Street.

 - A product still being figured out. We don't fully know what sales looks like when agents do most of the work. The people who join now help decide — and in this role, you draw it.

 - Top-of-market compensation. $226,000 - $302,000 + equity.




EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY STATEMENT

Nooks is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workforce. We believe in providing equal employment opportunities to all individuals regardless of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.  

Nooks does not discriminate in hiring, promotion, compensation, or any other employment practices, and we are committed to ensuring a workplace that is free from discrimination, harassment, and retaliation. We encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply and join our team.

KarmaCheck was founded by Eric Ly, a co-founder and the original CTO of LinkedIn. Our customers run screening inside the ATS, VMS, and HRIS platforms they already use, through our integrations and our public API, and KarmaCheck is the only background check integration in Bullhorn's investment portfolio.

Building AI agents is half the work. The other half is making them work inside a customer's world: their Bullhorn, Symplr CTM, or Workday instance, their proprietary systems, and the workflows they actually run. This role is the Product team's technical expert on that second half.
Customer Success runs our standard introductions and scripted pitches. Roadmap and prioritization sit with Product leadership; within the integration lane, you own the scoping, the solution, and delivery. Compensation & Benefits

Work Environment & Culture

Equal Opportunity Employer

Ready to Apply?

If you're passionate about animal health sales, customer education, and launching and growing innovative products, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today to join an employee-owned organization that invests in its people and rewards success through shared ownership.

The pay range for this role considers a wide range of factors including but not limited to: skill sets, experience and training, licensure and certifications, geographical location, and other organizational needs.

The estimated pay range for this role is $53,395 Min to $80,093 Max per year.

Additionally, you will be eligible to participate in a sales incentive program associated with this specific role.

PBI-Gordon Companies and its subsidiaries are proud to offer a comprehensive benefits package to eligible, full-time employees who work 30 hours per week or more. Full-time employees will become eligible to participate in benefits on the first of the month following their start date, unless stated otherwise below. jobs.title: Customer Success Manager
jobs.description:
WHY MINTLIFY?

We're on a mission to empower builders. 

 - Massive reach: Our docs platform serves 100 million+ developers every year and powers documentation for 20,000+ companies, including Anthropic, Microsoft, PayPal, Spotify, Coinbase, X, and over 20% of the last YC batch.

 - Small team, huge impact: We recently passed 65 employees and raised a $45 million Series B led by A16Z and Salesforce Ventures. Each new hire has a huge impact on shaping the company's trajectory. 

 - Culture of slope over y-intercept https://mattrickard.com/hire-slope-not-intercept: We value learning velocity, grit, and unapologetically unique personalities.

We grew in value faster than headcount and we’re looking to align the two quickly.


ABOUT MINTLIFY

Mintlify https://www.mintlify.com/ is the documentation platform for the AI era. More than 20,000 companies, including Anthropic, Microsoft, Coinbase, Perplexity, Replit, Vercel, and Zapier, use Mintlify to publish docs that stay current and work for both developers and AI agents. Our customers' docs reach over 100 million people a year, and nearly half of that traffic now comes from AI agents.

In April 2026 we raised a $45M Series B https://www.mintlify.com/blog/series-b led by Andreessen Horowitz and Salesforce Ventures, with Bain Capital Ventures and Y Combinator also backing us. We're a fast-moving, high-agency team based in San Francisco.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Mintlify is hiring a Customer Success Manager to own the health, retention and growth of a book of Enterprise customers: companies, from fast-growing AI startups to global enterprises, that run their technical docs, help centers and internal knowledge bases on Mintlify.

You'll be the person at Mintlify who knows where each of your accounts stands and has a plan to move it forward. You'll take accounts over from our Solutions Engineers at go-live, get customers enabled quickly, keep a current read on health and strategy for every account, and work alongside Account Managers to land clean renewals and grow expansion. When something looks off, you raise it early.

This is a commercial role as much as a relationship one. You'll be measured on expansion and gross revenue retention across your book, and you'll help customers measure value in the terms they care about: doing more with fewer people, getting accurate answers from their AI assistants and agents, and keeping critical knowledge current and owned.

 - Team: Customer Success, working alongside Account Managers, Solutions Engineers and Support Engineering

 - Reports to: Ben Terrill, Head of Customer Success

 - Location: San Francisco, in office five days a week

 - Travel: Occasional, for on-site visits where you have several accounts in one area

 - Type: Full-time


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own your book from go-live onward. Take a formal handover from the Solutions Engineer, confirm stakeholders and success criteria, and set an initial health score and account strategy for every new account.

 - Get customers enabled fast. Deliver product training and enablement within 30 days of go-live so teams get value from everything they bought.

 - Keep a current, defensible point of view on every account. Maintain the health score, account strategy (Expand, Sustain or Defend), competitive read and success criteria in Salesforce, and update them as soon as something material changes.

 - Stay present and multithreaded. Talk with every account at least once a quarter, run an executive business review with each one at least once a year, and know the economic buyer as well as the day-to-day champion.

 - Catch risk early and lead the save. Escalate at-risk accounts the same week you see the signal, then build and run the save plan with CS leadership and the Account Manager.

 - Generate expansion pipeline. Spot expansion signals in usage and conversations (the next team, the next use case or the next surface, such as a help center or internal knowledge base), source qualified opportunities and work them with the Account Manager.

 - Set up every renewal for success. Kick off renewals at least 90 days out, make the value case with the customer, and lead straightforward renewals when the Account Manager brings you in.

 - Unblock customers technically. Troubleshoot Git, configuration and content questions yourself, and bring in Support or Solutions Engineers for deeper issues.

 - Make the next account easier. Turn what you learn into playbooks, templates and AI-assisted workflows the team can reuse, and bring customer feedback to Product.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 4+ years in customer success, account management or technical account management at a B2B SaaS company, owning a book of mid-market or enterprise accounts.

 - A track record of owning a retention number (GRR, NRR or renewal rate) and growing expansion on your book, with results you can name.

 - Strong commercial instincts: you understand deal structure and discount levers, can forecast renewal risk across a portfolio, and can pitch an expansion to an economic buyer in business terms.

 - Executive presence: you've turned a cold executive sponsor into an internal advocate and run business reviews that tell a value story, not a status update.

 - Technical fluency: you're comfortable with Git workflows, Markdown or MDX, web basics (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) and APIs, enough to debug why a customer's docs didn't update after a merged PR.

 - Comfort working with data: you can read product usage data, reconcile numbers that don't agree and turn signals into action.

 - Real examples of using AI to build parts of your own customer success workflow.

 - Strong ownership and candor: you escalate early, push back constructively with internal teams and own outcomes, including the ones that didn't go your way.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience at a developer-tools, documentation or AI company.

 - Hands-on Salesforce experience (reports, dashboards, keeping a book's data clean).

 - SQL or Python for your own analysis.

 - Experience building health scores, playbooks or automations from scratch.

 - Experience creating customer advocacy assets, such as case studies and reference calls.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - 30 days: You know the product, how we run customer success and every account on your book. You've met your Account Managers, Solutions Engineers and largest customers, and every account has a health score, strategy and competitive read.

 - 60 days: You've talked with every account, success criteria are captured wherever they were missing, and every renewal in the next 120 days has a kickoff plan.

 - 90 days: Health scores, strategies and Salesforce data are current across your book, every at-risk account has a written save plan, and your first expansion opportunities are in the pipeline.

 - First year: GRR on your book is at or above target, you've driven meaningful expansion ARR, every account has had an executive business review, and at least one playbook or workflow you built is used across the team.


COMPANY BENEFITS:

 - Competitive compensation and equity

 - 20 days paid time off every year

 - 401k with Employer Match

 - monthly wellness stipend

 - 100% employee coverage for Health, Dental, Vision

 - Commute stipend to help get you to and from work

 - Free lunch and dinners

 - Annual team offsite (previously went to Alaska, Hawaii, Jackson Hole)

jobs.title: Director, US GI Market Research
jobs.description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

The Opportunity:

Reporting to the Senior Director, US GI Analytics & Insights, the Director, US GI Market Research will serve as the US Market Research lead for Revolution Medicines’ GI cancer portfolio.

This role will partner closely with US Commercial, , US Market Access, Global Market Research, Medical Affairs, Clinical Development, and Business Operations to generate actionable insights that inform portfolio strategy, launch readiness, commercialization planning, and business performance.

The role requires a strong understanding of the PDAC and CRC cancer treatment landscape, patient journey, biomarker-driven markets, and oncology data assets.

This position is based at our Redwood City, CA headquarters, with flexibility for remote candidates willing to travel regularly to the office.

Responsibilities include:

• Leads, designs, and executes US primary market research projects with HCPs, patients, and payors.

• Initiates and facilitates activities that enhance partners’ knowledge regarding the relevant US market and potential product attitudes, usage, market dynamics, and competition (for example, development of treatment flows, target product profiles, opportunity assessments, and market landscape research).

• Shares the voice of the US community (e.g., physicians, patients, payors) to the organization by maintaining and communicating a holistic understanding of the marketplace synthesized from primary and secondary sources.

• Reinforces market research best practices, identify market research and data sources, vendor options, and methodologies that are best suited to address a business need. Manages third parties associated with this function.

• Communicates and aligns key internal stakeholders around market research objectives and outputs including qualifying the results based on the strength of the data and identifying limitations.

• Develops and presents timely final reports and actionable recommendations to key stakeholders, focusing on key findings and relevant implications to each stakeholder group, and senior leadership.

• Communicate insights and strategic implications to senior leadership through clear, concise, and compelling recommendations.

• Shapes situation analysis as a part of launch planning to provide a comprehensive understanding of the market. Partner with cross-functional teams like marketing, sales (when appropriate), access, and medical to provide a clear view of the market.

• Demonstrates the ability to quickly understand complex markets, disease states, competitive landscapes, and relevant market and managed care dynamics.

• Exhibits analytical rigor in the valuation of business opportunities and the quantification of risk.

• Partner with US Forecasting, US Data Analytics, and Competitive Intelligence colleagues to develop an integrated view of market performance and future growth opportunities.

• Travels as needed.

Required Skills, Experience and Education:

• Bachelor's degree required (advanced degree preferred) with 10+ years of progressive experience in a pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or strategic consulting role with 6+ years of experience in a strategic analytics role.

• Oncology market research experience required; GI cancer (PDAC and/or CRC) experience strongly preferred.

• Experience in market development and new product launches.

• Extensive primary research and secondary analytical skills required; ability to translate the data and learning into actionable recommendations for business growth.

• Track record of being a collaborative team player, and adaptive to meet the needs of a growing business

• Strong problem solver with experience leveraging a variety of research and analytical vendors, study designs, and building quality research vendor partnerships

• Demonstrated ability to influence senior management and key business partners.

• Proven experience in a smaller, rapidly growing, company.

• Excellent organizational skills and an ability to prioritize effectively to deliver results within reasonably established timelines.

• Ability to represent Revolution Medicines well with internal and external stakeholders, including strong interpersonal skills including verbal and written communication.

• Entrepreneurial mindset, with a tolerance for ambiguity, and a passion for helping cancer patients.

Preferred Skills:

• MBA, MPH, MS, or PhD.

• Deep understanding of PDAC and/or CRC and biomarker-driven oncology markets.

• Experience supporting targeted oncology therapies.

• Prior experience in a growth-stage biotechnology company.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, SDK
jobs.description:
ABOUT KEYCARD

At Keycard, we're building identity and access infrastructure for the agent-native era, where software isn't static but a dynamic, constantly changing system of AI agents working on behalf of people and businesses. Keycard gives every agent a verified identity and issues short-lived, task-scoped credentials at runtime, so agents can only do what they were asked to do, and every action is fully auditable. We're backed by a16z, Boldstart, and Acrew, and our founding team built and scaled Snyk, Auth0, HashiCorp, and Heroku.


THE ROLE

We're hiring a staff-level Software Engineer, SDK to own the libraries developers use to put Keycard in front of their agents and MCP servers. For most teams, the SDK is the first Keycard code they touch: a few lines that add OAuth to an MCP server, then token exchange so a tool can call GitHub or Google as the user.

Keycard is a control plane for agents: identity, credential exchange, delegation, policy, and audit. Our SDKs come in two kinds. The REST API clients for Python, TypeScript, and Go are generated with Stainless from our OpenAPI spec. The agent SDKs are handwritten: OAuth primitives, MCP server and client auth, agent-to-agent (A2A) delegation (in preview), and integrations for frameworks like FastMCP, LangChain, Temporal, and Cloudflare Workers. The hard design work is on the handwritten side.

Python is the most complete today. TypeScript is in preview and working toward parity, and Go and Ruby are earlier. Keeping four languages consistent, without treating any of them as second-class, is the core of the job. You'll work with founders, product, and the engineers building the services underneath.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - API design. Decide what each package exposes and keep it consistent across languages. An AuthProvider in Python should feel like the one in TypeScript, Go, and Ruby, down to errors and credential types.

 - Safe defaults. The SDK verifies tokens, refreshes them, and handles signing-key outages, so the safe path has to be the easy one. A verifier built without an audience should warn. An expired token should refresh, not force a new sign-in.

 - Track upstream. Our MCP package follows the upstream MCP SDK's major versions, and framework integrations are tested nightly against each upstream's latest release. Ship support for new versions quickly, and decide when an old line moves to security fixes only.

 - Releases. Each package versions and publishes on its own, to PyPI, npm, pkg.go.dev http://pkg.go.dev, and RubyGems. Own semver, changelogs, deprecations, and the CI that bumps and publishes on merge.

 - Generated clients. Own the path from our OpenAPI spec to the Stainless-generated clients. Fix problems in the spec, not in generated code.

 - Developer experience. Quick starts, examples, and docs that take someone from install to a protected MCP server, and a loop that turns developer feedback into API changes.

 - Agents at work. Coding agents already open a good share of our SDK pull requests. Decide what they're trusted to do, and keep tests and review strong enough to catch what they get wrong.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - You've shipped libraries or SDKs that other developers depend on, and supported them through breaking changes.

 - You've kept one API consistent across at least two languages. You write idiomatic Python and TypeScript; Go or Ruby is a plus.

 - You know OAuth 2.0 and OIDC at the library level: token verification, refresh, PKCE, and token exchange (RFC 8693).

 - You've managed versioning in the real world: peer dependency ranges, maintenance branches, and deprecations users could plan around.

 - You build with MCP and agent frameworks, and have opinions about what works and what doesn't.

 - Agents in your work. You use coding agents daily and know where their output needs a closer look.


STRONG CANDIDATES MAY ALSO HAVE

 - Code generation for multi-language SDKs: Stainless, Speakeasy, Fern, OpenAPI, or protobuf.

 - Plugin or integration ecosystems, like Terraform providers, framework adapters, or editor extensions.

 - Contributions to MCP, the A2A protocol (which we support in preview), or open source agent frameworks.

 - Edge runtimes like Cloudflare Workers, or durable execution like Temporal.


YOUR FIRST 90 DAYS

 - Close the biggest gaps between the TypeScript and Python SDKs, toward dropping TypeScript's preview label.

 - Publish a cross-language API guide: names, errors, and credential types, mapped across Python, TypeScript, Go, and Ruby.

 - Take one upstream breaking change, like a new MCP SDK major or framework release, from nightly failure to released support.

 - Agree an SDK roadmap with product and engineering, including where generated clients end and handwritten SDKs begin.


WHO WILL LOVE THIS JOB

 - You care about the first ten lines a developer writes with your library.

 - You'd rather design an API once than explain it four different ways.


WHAT WE OFFER

 - Build at the Frontier: Work every day at the frontier of agent-native systems — shipping, inventing, and iterating on technology that hasn’t been built before. You’ll be given huge autonomy, the opportunity to gain mastery, and the chance to work in a team that holds each other accountable to succeed.

 - Truly Agent-Native Culture: At Keycard, we don’t just enable others to adopt agents — we use them ourselves to build. You’ll help shape an organization that embeds AI into its foundation as an enduring competitive advantage.

 - Compensation With Upside: Market-competitive salaries and generous equity packages (4-year vest, 1-year cliff) give you the security to focus on building — and the asymmetric upside of ownership in a company chasing a category-defining mission.

 - Comprehensive Benefits & Recharge: Health, dental, vision, and paramedical coverage for you and your family, plus 4 weeks vacation, 11 statutory holidays, and 1 volunteer day annually. We encourage at least 2 weeks off each year to fully recharge.

 - Tools That Keep You Ahead: A new MacBook Pro, a $500 stipend for peripherals, and the best AI tools available so you can work at the forefront of agent-native workflows.

 - Remote-First Flexibility: We are a remote-first team prioritizing asynchronous collaboration, with hiring focused in North and South America. Work where you’re strongest — we just want the best.

PRIVACY PROGRAM MANAGER @ CLAY

Personal data is at the center of how Clay works.  It comes from our data provider marketplace, our own proprietary B2B dataset, the web research our agents run, and the records our customers bring to Clay. Every person in that data, and every customer who relies on it, needs to trust how Clay handles it. As we build agents that research and act for our customers, that trust also depends on how we build and use AI.

We're looking for a Privacy Program Manager to help build and run Clay's privacy program, including the operational side of AI governance. You'll report to our Head of Product, Privacy & AI Legal and work closely with Product, Engineering, Data Platform, Data Partnerships, Security, Marketing, and Sales. Our Legal team sets the standards and makes the legal calls. As part of that team, you'll turn them into processes, records, and tooling that work at Clay's pace.

This role is for someone who wants to build and own a privacy program that differentiates Clay. You'll connect the privacy work already happening across Clay into one program with clear owners, reliable operations, and evidence we can stand behind. You'll also automate as much as possible, so Product and Engineering can spend more time building.

What You'll Do

 - Own the program plan. Turn Legal's privacy strategy into a prioritized plan with owners, dependencies, and six- and twelve-month outcomes. Flag early when work lacks an owner or capacity.

 - Own our records of processing:  Maintain Clay’s records of processing for the product and our own operations, and set the privacy requirements for the data inventory our GRC team maintains: sources, uses, recipients, storage, retention, and restrictions.

 - Run privacy and AI assessments. Run PIAs, DPIAs, transfer and legitimate interests assessments, and AI assessments from fact gathering through follow-up. Legal makes the legal determinations.

 - Build privacy into how Clay ships. Help run privacy and AI review inside EPD’s product development process, so teams get fast, consistent answers and the right questions reach Legal early.

 - Run the operational side of AI governance. Keep records of how Clay's products and internal tools use AI. Gather evidence on how agent features are controlled, and keep review conditions and customer guidance current as models and permissions change.

 - Run provider and vendor privacy diligence. Review data providers, marketplace partners, and vendors at onboarding, change, renewal, and exit. Maintain our subprocessor list and customer notices.

 - Operate privacy rights requests. Own access, deletion, correction, and opt-out requests end to end, including California Delete Act (DROP) requests, across the systems that hold a person's data, using our privacy platform (Transcend). Close every request with evidence.

 - Make retention and deletion work. Turn approved retention rules into a system-by-system map with technical owners, and coordinate fixes with Engineering and Data Platform.

 - Keep our commitments accurate. Keep privacy notices, our subprocessor list, and other public commitments to customers and regulators aligned with how Clay actually processes data. Support incident response with Legal and Security.

 - Automate, train, and measure. Automate routine work with Clay and AI tools, build short role-specific training, and report program metrics to Legal and EPD leadership.

How You'll Work with Others

 - Your team, Legal, sets privacy and AI standards and makes the legal calls. You put them into practice and flag early when something needs one.

 - Product, Engineering, and business teams own what we build and why, including model choices, evaluations, and agent safety. You make review fast and predictable, gather the evidence, and follow through.

 - Our GRC team owns security certifications such as SOC 2, the vendor and product review process, Clay’s data inventory, and security questionnaire.  You own the privacy side of each and keep handoffs clean.

What You'll Bring

 - 6 to 8+ years building and running privacy programs or privacy operations at a technology company, ideally high-growth B2B SaaS, data, or AI

 - Hands-on experience with privacy requests, data mapping, PIAs and DPIAs, vendor diligence, and consent management

 - Working knowledge of GDPR, UK GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, and other US state privacy laws, and good judgment about when to bring in Legal

 - AI fluency: you understand how LLM features and agents use data, and you can put frameworks like the EU AI Act into practice

 - Technical fluency: you can follow data across systems and APIs and ask engineers precise questions

 - A track record of building a program from scratch and making it stick with teams that didn't report to you

 - Clear, plain writing, and a habit of using AI and automation to remove routine work

 - CIPM or equivalent certification

 - A law degree is not required

Nice to Haves

 - CIPP/E, CIPP/US, CIPT, or AIGP

 - Hands-on AI governance experience, such as AI inventories, AI impact assessments, ISO/IEC 42001, or the NIST AI RMF

 - Experience at a B2B data or enrichment company, or with data partnerships and licensing

 - Experience with Transcend, OneTrust, DataGrail, or similar

 - Experience with Clay or building GTM workflows

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Card Growth
jobs.description:
JOIN THE TILT TEAM

At Tilt, we see a side of people that traditional lenders miss. Our mobile-first products and machine learning-powered credit models look beyond credit scores, using over 250 real-time financial signals to recognize real potential. With millions of customers worldwide, we're not just changing how people access financial products — we're creating a new credit system that backs the working, whatever they're working toward.




ABOUT THE ROLE

This role sits at the heart of Tilt’s card growth engine. You’ll build and scale the credit card acquisition channels we haven’t fully tapped yet: new affiliate partnerships, paid search, and paid social.

As the Senior Manager, Card Growth, you’ll own strategy, execution, and performance across these channels. You’ll source and launch new long-tail affiliate partners. You’ll build highly targeted search and social programs. You’ll turn new distribution into meaningful card volume and strong returns

Card Growth at Tilt is different from most consumer marketing. You’ll work closely with credit, product, data science, and marketing to turn acquisition complexity into profitable growth at scale.




HOW YOU’LL MAKE AN IMPACT

 - Scale the affiliates channel:
   
   - Source, pitch, and launch affiliate partners that extend Tilt’s reach beyond our largest marketplaces. Own each partnership from first conversation through launch and ongoing optimization.

 - Build paid search and social:
   
   - Design and run targeted search and social programs built around who is likely to qualify, not just who will click.

 - Shape policy with credit:
   
   - Partner with credit to adapt prequalification policies so new channels and partners can launch and grow.

 - Drive profitable acquisition:
   
   - Work with credit and data science to apply models and targeting strategies that lift approved volume and return on spend.

 - Build the test-and-learn engine:
   
   - Design and run structured tests across partners, audiences, offers, creative, and bidding to improve performance over time.

 - Influence product success:
   
   - Work with product and engineering to shape the offers and application experiences that partners and digital channels depend on.

 - See the full picture:
   
   - Use data to connect channel performance to downstream outcomes like approval, activation, spend, and credit performance.




WHY YOU’RE A GREAT FIT

 - You have hands-on experience running growth programs for lending products, ideally credit cards.

 - You’re deeply analytical and comfortable working with SQL and Python day-to-day to evaluate funnel performance and segment level unit economics.

 - You understand prescreened/non prescreened acquisition strategies, and how marketing and credit policy intersect.

 - You’re highly autonomous and organized, comfortable owning execution of an end-to-end channel.

 - You’re a clear, confident communicator who can influence across marketing, credit, product, and operations.

 - You’re relentlessly results-focused, with a strong bias toward experimentation and measurable outcomes.





Don’t meet every qualification? We care about potential over your past. If you're bringing ambition and drive to what we're building, we want to hear from you.





WHAT YOU'LL GET AT TILT

 - Virtual-first teamwork: The Tilt team is collaborating across 14 countries, 12 time zones, and counting. You’ll get started with a WFH office reimbursement.

 - Competitive pay: We're big on potential, and it's reflected in our competitive compensation packages and generous equity.

 - Complete support: Find flexible health plans at every premium level, and substantial subsidies that stand up to global standards.

 - Visibility is yours: You can count on direct exposure to our leadership team — we’re a team where good ideas travel quickly.

 - Paid global onsites: Magic happens IRL: we gather twice yearly to reconnect over shared meals or kayaking adventures. (We’ve visited Vail, San Diego, and Mexico City, to name a few.)

 - Impact is recognized: Growth opportunities follow your contributions, not rigid promotion timelines.


THE TILT WAY

We're looking for people who chase excellence and impact. Those who stand behind their work, celebrating the wins and learning from the missteps equally. We foster an environment where every voice is valued and mutual respect is non-negotiable — brilliant jerks need not apply. We're in this together, working to expand access to fair credit and prove that people are incredible. When you join us, it's not just another day at the [virtual] office, you're helping millions of hardworking people reach better financial futures.



You’re pushing ahead in your career? We can get behind that. Join us in building the credit system that people deserve.

jobs.title: Manager, Operation & Maintenance (Power Plant) - Memphis
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

We are seeking a Manager of Operation & Maintenance to lead the people who keep SpaceXSI’s on-site power plant running. You will oversee supervisors, leads, and technicians supporting operations and maintenance of gas turbine generation, balance-of-plant, process and fluid systems, and plant electrical systems. This plant supplies power for high-density AI supercomputing facilities in the Memphis and Southaven area, and it has to stay online.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You will set the operating and maintenance standard, run the organization through trips, outages, and day-to-day work, and build supervisors and technicians who can execute safely without waiting on you for every decision. You will work with engineering, construction, operations leadership, OEMs, and contractors as the plant grows. This is a full-time, onsite role based in the Memphis region.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Own operation and maintenance of the power plant, including gas turbines and generators, balance-of-plant, fuel gas and process/fluid systems, water, compressed/instrument air, plant HVAC and cooling, and electrical systems through, including protection, e-houses, blackstart, and switching.

• Lead supervisors, leads, and technicians across plant, process, and electrical crafts as one O&M organization.

• Set daily and weekly priorities so planned maintenance, emergent work, alarms, trips, and outages are balanced without losing generation.

• Own the maintenance program: work planning, scheduling, procedures, CMMS discipline, spare parts readiness, and as-found/as-left documentation.

• Direct start-up, shutdown, switching, isolation, LOTO, and restoration so mechanical, process, and electrical work is coordinated and safe.

• Enforce SpaceXSI safety standards, including LOTO, NFPA 70E / arc-flash, confined space, and hot work. Stop work when conditions are unsafe and hold the organization to that standard.

• Lead outage planning and execution with engineering, OEMs, and contractors, and support commissioning and turnover of new generation and BOP systems into operations.

• Own O&M vendor and contractor performance, cost, and schedule. Work with buyers and accounts payable so accounts and contracts stay in order.

• Drive reliability: bad-actor elimination, root-cause investigations, and standards that raise uptime as capacity grows.

• Coach and develop supervisors and leads. Set expectations, manage performance, and scale the team with the plant.

• Communicate plant status, risks, team performance, and resource needs to site leadership.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• High school diploma or equivalency certificate.

• 6+ years of experience in power plant or other high-reliability industrial operations and maintenance.

• 2+ years directly managing supervisors, leads, or a multi-discipline technician organization.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Bachelor’s degree in a technical, engineering, or related field, or equivalent experience.

• Experience operating or maintaining gas turbine generation and balance-of-plant, including fuel gas, water, compressed air, and plant electrical systems.

• Experience leading a mixed-discipline O&M team (plant, process, and electrical) in a generating station or similar facility.

• Working knowledge of P&IDs, single-line diagrams, electrical schematics, switching, LOTO, and NFPA 70E / arc-flash practices.

• Experience running a CMMS-based maintenance program, including planning, scheduling, and outage execution.

• Experience managing O&M budgets, OEM service agreements, and third-party contractors.

• Track record of reliability improvement, root-cause investigations, and high-uptime operation of mission-critical plant equipment.

• Ability to develop supervisors and leads while staying close enough to the work to catch problems early.

• Strong written and verbal communication with technicians, engineers, contractors, and site leadership.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Willingness to be in the plant and to perform hands-on work in all environments (heat, cold, rain), in tight quarters or at heights.

• Ability to work extended hours, nights, weekends, and on-call coverage to support plant operations.

• Remain focused while working in hazardous environments, while wearing appropriate PPE.

• Must be able to lift up to 25 lbs unassisted.

• Lifting, standing, climbing, bending, grasping, sitting, pulling, pushing, stooping, stretching, and carrying are generally required to perform the functions of this position.

• Must be able to work on-site at the power generation facility, with potential travel to other SpaceXSI sites.

SpaceXSI is an equal opportunity employer. For details on data processing, view our Recruitment Privacy Notice.

jobs.description:

As Cresco grows, we will operate with the same level of professionalism and precision in each new market we move in to.

JOB SUMMARY

The Regional Director of Sunnyside* reports to the Vice President of Retail Sales & Operations and is responsible for profitability of the multi-state retail operation and building high performing management teams within Ohio, Massachusetts, and New York. The Regional Director will oversee and lead Sunnyside* dispensaries, ensuring the region achieves or exceeds all key metrics and goals, including meeting revenue targets and increased market share.  As a strategic leader, you will work closely with senior leadership to implement national Sunnyside initiatives, build & execute plans, create a best-in-class customer experience, and drive operational consistency across all Sunnyside dispensaries. This role will work cross functionally with key partners including but not limited to Human Resources, Compliance, Security, Marketing, New Store Development, Construction, Learning & Development and Talent Acquisition to ensure regional business needs are met.

At Sunnyside, we believe the employee experience is paramount to all. With a strong focus on training, development, diversity and authenticity, our employees experience both personal and professional growth.  As a Regional Director, you will have:

• Experience leading and motivating a team of District Managers & Dispensary Managers; skills include recruiting, onboarding, training, managing employee relations and coaching.

• P&L responsible for a region to include payroll, financial management, and achieving monthly sales goals.

• Skills in conflict resolution, strategic thinking, decision making and complex problem solving.

• Skills in talent selection, performance management and succession planning of regional retail leadership.

WHO YOU ARE

• You are energetic, possess strong interpersonal skills and work well with others. Collaboration is key to our team’s success!

• You enjoy people! Consulting our customers, listening to their needs and providing an exceptional experience is vital to achieving customer loyalty.

• You inspire others! You are a leader who has a passion for coaching, developing, and influencing your teams while driving a profitable multi-unit business. You have proven success building a high-performance team!

• You hold yourself to an elevated level of integrity. In an industry that is highly regulated, we trust in our employee’s commitment to always do the right thing.

CORE JOB DUTIES

• Build a high-performing retail leadership team by pairing critical talent selection with nuanced region and district needs.

• Assess management performance, skill gaps, and career aspirations to develop a leadership pipeline that provides for projected new store openings and revenue growth.

• Develop, coach, and inspire leaders to achieve individual and team goals through regular feedback inclusive of recurring performance discussions and career development planning. Sustain coaching, training and development initiatives specific to succession planning needs.

• Uphold a culture of accountability, people-centeredness and forward-thinking in the performance management of regional leadership.

• Drive the direction of district level resource planning and operational needs aligning with regional strategy.

• Contribute to the development of key Sunnyside initiatives and own the successful deployment within the region.

• Regularly assess and develop regional structure and organizational design reacting to forecasts, new store openings, and an ever-changing landscape.

• Maintain and influence key business partner relationships across Human Resources, Outreach, Compliance, Security, Employees Health & Safety, Marketing, Construction, and IT.

• Ensure regional strategic priorities, budgets and people needs are incorporated into new store opening project initiatives.

• Achieve sales objectives by influencing regional sales targets, driving accountability to meet or exceed sales goals and solving operational challenges to increase productivity.

• Partner with Regional Buyer to select product line enhancements (cultivators/vendors/products) given regional trends and customer demographics; ensure dispensary management is prepared and resourced to launch enhancements.

• Gather data and insights from districts and develop strategic plans for the region that address business and competitor risk.

• Partner with Human Resources to investigate and resolve employee relations and employee engagement concerns in a timely manner

• Manage any inspection or audit escalations.

• Establish short term and long-term strategic goals and work with business partners and stakeholders to monitor and drive the achievement of company and individual performance through KPI’s and other metrics.

REQUIRED EXPERIENCE, EDUCATION AND SKILLS

• 10 plus years of Retail Management Experience, preferably in a high-growth or fast-paced environment with multiple site responsibility.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite with strong Excel skills.

• Demonstrated ability to learn, apply and teach others technical and product-related information in a professional consultative manner.

• Strong business acumen including data management, attention to detail, and excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

• A high level of integrity, personal motivation, adaptability, and sense of urgency.

• Available to work all hours of operation inclusive of nights, weekends, and holidays

• Regular travel within the state to visit all assigned dispensaries as well periodic travel to other states for business meetings and events

In accordance with any local and state compensation laws, the compensation listed is the current estimated range for the position. Final offer details and future compensation may be determined by multiple factors including but not limited to, geographic location, market compensation data, skills, experience, and other relevant factors. For questions about this please discuss with your recruiter during the interview process.

$130,000—$130,000 USD

BENEFITS

Cresco Labs is proud to offer eligible employees a robust offering of benefits including, major medical, dental and vision insurance, a 401(K)-match program, FSA/HSA programs, LTD/STD options, life insurance and AD&D.  We also offer eligible employees paid holidays and paid time off.  Other rewards may include annual discretionary bonuses, stock options as well as participation in our employee discount program. Benefits eligibility for permanent positions may vary by full-time or part-time roles, location, or position.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

jobs.title: Gardener
jobs.description:
Position Title:  Gardener

Department: Horticulture

Supervisor: Area Manager- Horticulture

Nashville Zoo Mission:

Nashville Zoo is dedicated to inspiring a culture of understanding and discovery of our natural world through conservation, innovation, and leadership. With a diverse collection of animals and a commitment to wildlife preservation, we provide engaging experiences for visitors of all ages.

Why Work with Us:

At the Nashville Zoo, we believe in taking care of our team just as well as we care for our animals. Full-time employees enjoy a robust benefits package designed to support your health, well-being, and future:

• Comprehensive healthcare coverage – including medical, dental, and vision plans to keep you and your family healthy.

• Employee Assistance Program (EAP) – confidential support services for mental, emotional, and financial well-being.

• 401(k) retirement plan with company matching – helping you build a secure future while you make a meaningful impact today.

• Generous paid time off and sick leave – because rest and recovery are vital.

• Exclusive zoo perks – enjoy discounts on park experiences, retail, and food services, plus complimentary membership benefits.

• A collaborative and inclusive culture – be part of a diverse team where your voice matters, your growth is nurtured, and collaboration thrives across all departments.

• AZA-accredited facility – Nashville Zoo is committed to top-tier animal care, ethics and global conservation efforts.

Position Description:

Gardener responsibilities include monitoring the health of all plants and greenscapes, watering and feeding plants, trimming trees and shrubs, fertilizing and mowing lawns, weeding gardens, and keeping green spaces and walkways clear of debris and litter within their assigned area. The Gardener should know how to use and maintain landscaping equipment, including mowers, trimmers, and fertilizers while following health and safety regulations while making sure the gardens and green spaces are always healthy and beautiful. The ideal candidate possesses a strong appreciation for horticulture, an eye for detail, and a commitment to maintaining vibrant, attractive, and healthy landscapes year-round.

Duties and Responsibilities:

• Prune and weed-landscaped areas.

• Maintain regular and reliable attendance.

• Maintain professional conduct at all times and consistently model the organization’s values in all interactions with colleagues, guests, and stakeholders.

• Monitor irrigation systems and ensure they are working properly.

• Hand water all plantings that are not established.

• Install plants when necessary.

• Responsible for assisting other departments and staff when requested.

• Responsible for completing assigned tasks in an orderly efficient manner.

• Responsible for furthering horticulture knowledge during tenure at the Zoo.

Qualifications

Skills:

• Ability to self-direct work tasks while ensuring safety and productivity.

• Ability and motivation to learn the plants on grounds and their proper care.

• Ability to interact professionally with both staff and visitors.

• Ability to perform assigned tasks in an organized and efficient manner.

• Ability to professionally and safely use small, medium and heavy equipment and tools required for the execution of assigned tasks.

Education/ Experience:

• Minimum High School diploma or GED equivalent is required.

• A background in landscaping or grounds maintenance is preferred.

• A valid driver’s license is required.

Physical Responsibilities:

Staff must frequently stand and walk for most of an 8–10‑hour shift and regularly bend, kneel, reach, climb, and perform repetitive motions while cleaning, maintaining grounds, or performing facilities repairs. These roles require frequently lifting, carrying, pushing, and pulling up to 50 lbs and occasionally heavier items with assistance, as well as safely navigating ladders, stairs, uneven surfaces, and wet or slippery areas. Adequate vision, hearing, hand dexterity, and clear communication are necessary to operate tools, equipment, vehicles, and radios safely. Work occurs both indoors and outdoors year‑round in all weather conditions, with routine exposure to dust, dirt, chemicals, cleaning agents, noise, and equipment vibration. Positions may involve using power tools, machinery, or motorized vehicles and require adherence to established safety procedures. PPE such as gloves, protective footwear, eye and hearing protection, or respirators may be required depending on the task. Schedules may include early mornings, evenings, weekends, holidays, and occasional overtime based on operational needs. The role must learn new tasks, remember processes, maintain focus, complete task independently, and make timely decisions in the context of a workflow.

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform essential job functions.

Work Schedule:

Full-Time position

Flexibility: Position may require flexibility in working hours to accommodate special events, emergencies, or animal care needs.

Pre-employment requirements:

Nashville Zoo is an Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) employer and maintains a drug-free work environment. All employment is at-will.

• All candidates are required to successfully complete a criminal background check and drug screening prior to hire.

• Pre-employment and annual tuberculosis (TB) screenings are a condition of continued employment.

Pay Range

$17.39—$18.50 USD

jobs.title: Value Engineer - NYC
jobs.description:
About the Team

The Value Engineer team helps customers turn frontier AI into real business value. We accelerate adoption of OpenAI technology at scale and guide organizations from initial activation to measurable, organization-wide impact. We partner closely with Sales, Product, Solutions Architecture, and Security to deliver safe and responsible AI transformation. Our work shapes how customers generate and measure tangible outcomes from OpenAI products and creates a repeatable blueprint for successful enterprise launches and expansions.



About the Role

We are hiring a Value Engineer to help articulate and quantify the business value of OpenAI’s technology across Enterprise, Education, and Government customers. In this role, you will help customers and internal teams translate AI adoption into measurable financial and operational impact.



As an early member of the Value Engineering team, you will help define how OpenAI measures and communicates the real-world impact of AI across its customers. You will partner closely with Sales, AI Success Engineers, AI Deployment Engineering, and Product teams to identify high-impact AI use cases and build financial and operational business cases. Your work will directly influence executive alignment, investment decisions, renewals, and long-term expansion.



You will play a key role in helping build and shape the value engineering function from the ground up — developing repeatable frameworks, ROI models, value narratives, dashboards, and collateral that help internal teams and customers understand and measure the impact of AI adoption.



Success in this role is measured by how clearly customers and internal teams can quantify the value of AI, how effectively business cases support adoption and expansion, and how scalable value frameworks become across the GTM organization.



This role is based in San Francisco or New York City and we offer relocation benefits to new employees.



In This Role, You Will

 - Lead business value assessments for our largest deals, working closely with customers to identify key business drivers and quantify the value of OpenAI’s products to support investment decisions

 - Build and maintain standardized ROI, TCO, and value modeling tools for internal and customer use.

 - Lead structured value discovery to identify high-impact use cases and define measurable outcomes.

 - Publish executive-ready business cases that quantify results and strengthen relationships with C-level stakeholders.

 - Codify value frameworks, methodologies, and reusable assets that scale value-based selling across the global GTM organization.

 - Establish baselines, KPIs, and dashboards to track and communicate value delivery.

 - Partner closely with Account Directors and post-sale teams to influence deal strategy, renewals, and expansion opportunities.

 - Contribute to thought leadership on AI-driven business transformation by identifying emerging patterns in how organizations realize value from AI.
   

You Will Thrive in This Role If You

 - Bring 6–10 years of experience in value engineering, management consulting, or adjacent roles.

 - Have strong financial and analytical skills, with experience quantifying and presenting value to executive stakeholders.

 - Demonstrate exceptional executive presence with strong written, verbal, and presentation skills.

 - Have experience working on large-scale AI, cloud, or digital transformation initiatives.

 - Communicate with clarity and confidence across technical and business audiences.

 - Can translate AI capabilities into compelling financial, productivity, and workforce transformation narratives.

 - Enjoy managing multiple complex customers and driving toward concrete, measurable outcomes.

 - Demonstrate humility, curiosity, and a customer-first mindset.

 - Operate with high ownership, urgency, and comfort navigating ambiguity.

 - Are a creative builder who thrives in 0→1 environments and enjoys rolling up your sleeves to balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution.



About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. 

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. 

For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement https://cdn.openai.com/policies/eeo-policy-statement.pdf.

Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. For unincorporated Los Angeles County workers: we reasonably believe that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship with the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment: protect computer hardware entrusted to you from theft, loss or damage; return all computer hardware in your possession (including the data contained therein) upon termination of employment or end of assignment; and maintain the confidentiality of proprietary, confidential, and non-public information. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations.

jobs.location: Atlanta, Georgia, United States; Franklin, TN
jobs.description:
Title: Preconstruction Manager – Water Solutions

Location: Atlanta and Franklin

Region: Southeast

About Loenbro

Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our market spans all industries and our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication. Our expertise lies in simplifying the complex and establishing long-standing relationships with our partners. We have a national presence but a local approach—every customer benefits from our capabilities and our care.

At Loenbro, we don’t just offer jobs—we build careers grounded in integrity, teamwork, excellence, and purpose. Join a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work helps maintain and enhance the critical infrastructure that powers communities across the nation.

Job Summary

The Preconstruction Manager is responsible for managing strategic client relationships and overseeing project opportunities from initial identification through award or closeout. Operating under the seller/doer model, this role serves as the primary point of contact for clients within their assigned region and industry sectors. The Preconstruction Manager will collaborate closely with estimating, operations, business development, and marketing teams to deliver client-focused proposals and achieve regional and corporate sales goals.

This position requires strong communication, organizational, and leadership skills to ensure that client needs are met through proactive engagement and seamless coordination throughout the project lifecycle.

Essential Job Responsibilities

• Serve as the lead client contact for assigned key accounts and project opportunities.

• Develop and maintain long-term relationships with clients, general contractors, engineers, and industry partners.

• Identify project opportunities through research, networking, and collaboration with business development and marketing teams.

• Lead preconstruction efforts including scope alignment, risk identification, value engineering, and constructability input.

• Own and manage the opportunity lifecycle from project identification through bid, award, and closeout using Salesforce CRM.

• Responsible for developing and implementing win strategies and Go-No-Go process to determine which projects and clients to target.

• Lead the RFP/RFQ process and deliver to the client while meeting company standards and processes.

• Coordinate with estimating and operations teams to develop comprehensive proposals and ensure accurate project pricing.

• Lead constructability and schedule reviews and develop staffing/labor forecast plans in coordination with the clients project schedule.

• Gain a solid understanding of the services to be sold and represent that well to the client, bringing in subject matter experts when appropriate.

• Lead preconstruction efforts including scope alignment, risk identification, value engineering, and constructability input.

• Participate in pre-bid meetings, client presentations, and interviews to support pursuit strategies.

• Work with the Regional Sales Director to execute regional business plans and achieve annual sales targets.

• Monitor client satisfaction and provide feedback to internal teams for continuous improvement.

• Maintain accurate and timely records of opportunities, client interactions, and project outcomes in Salesforce.

• Represent Loenbro at regional trade shows, association events, and client meetings to strengthen industry presence.

• Uphold Loenbro’s safety culture and actively support company initiatives and values.

Minimum Qualifications

Required:

• 8+ years of experience in industrial or commercial construction through preconstruction, estimating, project management, or business development areas, including at least [5] years in municipal or industrial water/wastewater.

• Proven ability to manage client relationships and coordinate cross-functional teams to deliver successful outcomes.

• Hands-on experience estimating or leading pursuits for water or wastewater treatment plants, pump stations, or lift stations.

• Working knowledge of the electrical and controls scope on water projects: MCCs, medium-voltage gear, PLC/SCADA, duct bank, and standby power.

• Experience with public-sector procurement: prequalification, public bid, design-build, and CMAR (construction manager at risk)

• Knowledge of estimating, bid development, and preconstruction processes.

• Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to influence decisions and build trust.

• Highly organized, self-motivated, results-oriented, and capable of managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

• Willingness to travel within the assigned region to meet with clients and internal teams.

Preferred:

• Experience using Salesforce CRM and familiarity with Industrial Info Resources (IIR) preferred.

• Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Business, or related field (or equivalent experience).

Physical Demands and Work Environment

The physical demands and work environment described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Work Environment:

• Indoor office setting with controlled temperature.

• Potential visits to outdoor industrial sites with exposure to weather extremes.

• Potential exposure to noise, dust, chemicals, or other environmental factors.

• Travel requirements: varies.

This role requires compliance with all applicable safety regulations, personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements, and Loenbro's Environmental Health and Safety (EH&S) policies.

Benefits

Loenbro offers a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits package, and rewards to those who join our team:

• Medical, dental, and vision insurance

• 401(k) retirement plan with company match

• Paid time off (PTO) and holiday pay

• Life and disability insurance

• Professional development and training opportunities

• Employee assistance program (EAP)

Benefits eligibility may vary based on employment classification and hours worked.

Guided by Core Values (LEAD), grounded in grit and a commitment to excellence, Loenbro betters our families, customers, and local communities.  If you’re ready to be part of a company that LEADS by:

• Living with Integrity

• Exceeding Expectations

• Acting with Urgency

• Delivering Excellence

…we want to hear from you.

Loenbro is an Equal Opportunity Employer

The Senior Product Training Lead combines advanced HVAC technical instruction with leadership of product-focused training development. This role serves as the technical training lead for assigned LG HVAC products, ensuring that new and existing product training is accurate, effective, and ready to support product introductions. The position partners with Product Management, Engineering, and the Training Content Development Team to develop instructor-led courses, hands-on activities, assessments, e-learning, and digital training resources.

The role also conducts classroom, virtual, and hands-on technical training; performs new product testing and technical evaluations; provides product guidance to fellow instructors; and supports the operation and readiness of the assigned LG Training Academy. This is a technical leadership role and does not inherently include direct people management.

The Opportunity

Product Training Leadership & Content Development

• Serve as technical training lead and subject matter expert for assigned LG HVAC product lines, including new releases and existing product enhancements.

• Lead the technical planning, development, review, and updates of training curricula, presentations, instructor guides, student materials, hands-on exercises, and knowledge assessments.

• Partner with the Content Development Team to create e-learning modules, instructional videos, product demonstrations, and other digital learning resources; validate content for technical accuracy.

• Coordinate with Product Management, Engineering, and Field Teams to identify product training needs, secure technical information, and establish training readiness for product launches.

• Develop and support Train-the-Trainer activities; communicate product updates and provide technical direction to instructors across LG and Associate Academies.

Product Testing & Technical Evaluation

• Perform hands-on testing of new HVAC products, equipment, and controls to evaluate installation, commissioning, operation, service, and troubleshooting procedures.

• Document testing results, technical findings, and training recommendations; communicate product concerns and improvement opportunities to the appropriate teams.

• Validate service procedures, product documentation, laboratory exercises, and technical training materials through practical testing and equipment evaluation.

Technical Instruction & Customer Support

• Deliver instructor-led, hands-on, and virtual technical training covering LG product applications, safety, installation, commissioning, maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair.

• Conduct training at LG Academies, Associate Academies, and designated field locations; administer practical and written assessments as needed.

• Provide technical guidance to instructors, internal teams, and customers; support field evaluations and commissioning when needed to reinforce practical training.

• Collaborate with regional LG Field Teams to align training content and delivery with contractor and market needs.

Academy Operations & Readiness

• Support operations of the assigned academy, including training schedules, instructional materials, laboratory readiness, equipment, software, controls, and learner amenities.

• Coordinate equipment installation, upgrades, maintenance, contractor work, and approved work orders, including applicable EP portal submissions.

• Support assigned Associate Academies with training equipment and laboratory needs; publish training schedules at least eight weeks before each quarter.

The Qualifications

• Vocational diploma or Associate's/Bachelor's degree in HVAC or a related field preferred; equivalent relevant experience considered.

• 10+ years of HVAC industry experience with substantial technical training, service, product support, or technical content development experience.

• 3–5 years of hands-on experience with VRF, ductless, and/or residential and light commercial HVAC systems.

• Proven ability to deliver technical training and develop clear, practical instructional materials and hands-on exercises.

• Experience with product testing, technical evaluations, or new product introductions; ability to interpret installation/service manuals, electrical schematics, piping diagrams, and controls sequences.

• Experience collaborating with Product Management, Engineering, technical support, and/or learning content development teams.

• Understanding of HVAC installation, commissioning, system operation, troubleshooting, and industry best practices; LG product knowledge preferred.

• Familiarity with e-learning development, learning management systems, and instructional video or digital learning content preferred.

• Strong communication, technical writing, presentation, project coordination, analytical, and organizational skills; proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite.

• Ability to independently prioritize multiple projects, support academy operations, and travel up to 50%.

jobs.title: Senior Product Marketing Manager, Core Product
jobs.description:
ABOUT MESHY

Meshy is a leading generative AI platform for 3D creation. Millions of game developers, 3D artists, makers, and studios use Meshy to turn text and images into production-ready 3D assets—textured, rigged, and ready to drop into a game engine or a print queue. Headquartered in Silicon Valley, we are one of the fastest-growing AI companies in the world.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Meshy’s core product moves fast, with new generation models, better texturing, rigging and animation, and expanding API capabilities. We’re looking for a Senior Product Marketing Manager to translate that innovation into clear positioning, compelling stories, and launches that drive adoption.

You will own product marketing for Meshy’s core product: how each release is positioned, who it serves, why it matters, and how the market learns about it. You will also help decide which releases deserve a major launch and which are better supported through focused, ongoing communications.

This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who brings a clear point of view, studies the product and market, identifies the strongest story, and turns that story into action.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own product positioning and messaging. Define who each capability serves, the problems it solves, and the language we use across our website, product, documentation, and campaigns.

 - Set launch priorities. Build and apply a launch tiering framework. Bring related features together into compelling narratives and keep smaller releases efficient.

 - Lead launches from planning through measurement. Own messaging, launch assets, channel plans, and cross-functional coordination, from pre-launch preparation to post-launch analysis.

 - Partner closely with Product and Engineering. Understand upcoming capabilities early, build realistic launch plans, and bring market and customer insights into product decisions.

 - Develop deep customer understanding. Learn how game developers, 3D artists, and makers work—their workflows, tools, and frustrations—and create content that reflects that understanding.

 - Measure impact. Define success for each launch, including adoption, activation, coverage, and pipeline, and report clearly on results and lessons learned.

 - Equip the go-to-market team. Give Growth, Sales, and Social teams the messaging, proof points, and assets they need to tell a consistent product story.


WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - 6+ years of product marketing experience, ideally with a technical or creative product serving both self-serve and enterprise users.

 - A track record of owning launches, with the ability to explain your strategy, key decisions, and results.

 - Strong prioritization skills and examples of when you advocated for a larger launch, a smaller release, or a different approach.

 - Excellent writing skills. A writing exercise will be part of the interview process.

 - Familiarity with at least one of our core markets: game development, 3D content creation, or 3D printing and digital manufacturing. You understand what a 3D pipeline involves and the challenges users face.

 - Experience working closely with Product and Engineering teams, including collaboration across time zones.

 - Based in the San Francisco Bay Area or willing to relocate. This role works in-office with the GTM team.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Hands-on experience with 3D tools, game engines, or generative AI products.

 - A background in developer tools, creative software, or gaming.

 - Experience at a company scaling through hypergrowth.


SALARY:

The base salary range for this position is $120,000 – $250,000 per year. Actual compensation will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and skills. This role may also be eligible for additional compensation and a comprehensive benefits package.

As a member of the interdisciplinary team, the RN Case Manager works under the general direction of the Director of Nursing, the attending physician and the interdisciplinary group in providing skilled nursing assessments, planning, and care in order to maximize the comfort and health of both patients and their loved ones/caregivers.

Responsible for identifying patient and loved ones/caregiver needs and for providing supportive care in accordance with the attending physician’s orders and plan of care and the policies and procedures. The functions of this position will include the following:

jobs.title: Chief of Staff
jobs.description:
CHIEF OF STAFF TO THE CEO — MAVEN AGI




COMPANY OVERVIEW

Maven AGI sits at the center of the hottest intersection in tech right now: AI and customer experience. While most "AI support" tools still focus on FAQs and deflection, Maven's agents actually do the work — autonomously interacting with customers, personalizing the conversation, and resolving complex issues, not just providing information.

That's not a soft ROI story. It's the most direct cost-displacement case in enterprise software today: real human work, replaced, at a fraction of the cost — not "savings if you use it well," but savings because the agent did the ticket instead of a person. 

Founded in 2023 by executives from HubSpot, Google, and Stripe, Maven builds conversational AI agents that don't just answer customers — they act: going into a customer's account, finding the actual problem, and fixing it, with no human required. Customers like Dell, ServPro, HardRock, Tripadvisor, Clio, and Thumbtack rely on Maven, with independently verified results — customers report resolving 70–93% of interactions autonomously — and G2 has named Maven a High Performer and Best Meets Requirements across multiple categories this spring




POSITION OVERVIEW

We're hiring a Chief of Staff to the CEO to be a strategic partner to our CEO and leadership team as we scale. This role is for an analytical, execution-oriented leader who thrives where strategy, operations, and communication meet.

You'll be a force multiplier for the CEO. You'll drive alignment across the company, own critical initiatives, and make sure Maven executes with speed, clarity, and rigor. You'll work across product, go-to-market, engineering, and operations, turning company priorities into concrete plans and measurable outcomes. It's a high-impact seat with direct exposure to company strategy, executive decision-making, and what it takes to scale an AI-first enterprise business.




WHAT YOU'LL DO
