• Lead the specification, selection, and integration of process instrumentation including pressure, temperature, flow, level, position, vibration, and gas analysis.

• Lead instrument calibration, loop checks, FAT, SAT, startup, and commissioning activities.

Basic Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Engineering or related discipline.

• 10+ years of experience with industrial process instrumentation.

• Experience with complex thermal-fluid systems, power generation, chemical processing, nuclear, aerospace test facilities, or similar industries.

• Strong understanding of instrumentation selection, calibration, and commissioning.

Preferred Skills and Experience

• Experience with high-temperature gas systems, helium systems, or advanced reactor technologies.

• Experience with Allen-Bradley ControlLogix/GuardLogix.

• Experience commissioning first-of-a-kind process facilities.

jobs.title: Court Security Officer, Roswell, NM
jobs.description:
Walden Security is currently recruiting experienced Court Security Officers. CSOs will provide armed security to courthouses under the USMS contract.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Includes the following and other duties may be assigned:

Perform entrance control: Enforce the District’s entry and identification system which includes operating security screening equipment to detect weapons, contraband, and prohibited items, checking items such as handbags, briefcases, computers, packages, baby carriages, wheelchairs, etc.

Perform roving patrol: Patrol court facilities and grounds of the facility in accordance with applicable post orders.

Perform stationary post assignments: Stand guard at stationary posts which include (but not limited to) monitoring closed-circuit television, duress alarm systems and other security equipment, courtrooms, judge chambers, and jury rooms.

Perform escort duties: When directed, provide armed escort services for judges, court personnel, jurors, and other designated individuals.

Perform garage parking and pedestrian control: Where applicable, direct traffic and control lights on court facility properties, as described in the post orders and/or standard operating procedures.

Enforce law and order: Enforce federal law while in the performance of assigned duties. This includes (but not limited to) detaining any person attempting to gain unauthorized access to Government property, or a court proceeding(s), or attempting to commit acts that imperil the safety and security of Government employees, property, and the public.

Prepare reports and records: Prepare various reports and records regarding contract performance issues, such as labor hours worked, accidents, fire, bomb threats, unusual incidents, or unlawful acts that occurred within the court facility area.

Court attendance: Responsible for securing unattended courtrooms, an inspection of courtrooms prior to a proceeding, testing of security devices, and other duties concerning security of the court area.

Preserve order: Responsible for providing security presence in the courtroom, enforcing federal law and judicial orders within the courtroom, enforcing local court rules regarding prohibited items, and providing protection to court proceedings as circumstances dictate.

jobs.title: NPI Buyer/Planner
jobs.description:
Figure is an AI robotics company developing autonomous general-purpose humanoid robots. The goal of the company is to ship humanoid robots with human level intelligence. Its robots are engineered to perform a variety of tasks in the home and commercial markets. Figure is headquartered in San Jose, CA.

As the NPI Buyer/Planner, you own material readiness for new product introduction PCBAs and components. From early prototypes through mass production, EVT/DVT, as well as the handoff to mass production stakeholders. You sit between Engineering and the Supply Chain teams, converting and assessing immature BOMs and shifting build schedules into placed POs, committed dates, and kitted builds that land on time.

This role is equal parts tactical buying, prototype planning, and cross-functional firefighting. You will work daily with Design Engineering, NPI, Manufacturing, Global Supply Chain, Quality, and Logistics teams to ensure pilot builds are clear-to-build in an environment where the design changes rapidly without notice.

Responsibilities:

• NPI Material Planning

• Convert engineering build plans and prototype schedules into time-phased material requirements for EVT/DVT/PVT and pilot builds.

• Plan against incomplete and rapidly changing BOMs; run BOM scrubs with Engineering to close gaps on part numbers, revisions, quantities, and reference designators before they become shortages.

• Identify long-lead and single-source parts early and drive risk-buy or bridge-buy decisions with Global Supply Managers.

• Build and maintain the NPI shortage list; publish clear-to-build status and recovery dates for each build event.

• Plan for build-specific overages using historical program data including attrition, engineering consumption, test consumption, and reliability samples.

• Tactical Purchasing

• Own the RFQ-to-PO cycle for prototype and pilot material: request quotes, place POs, confirm acknowledgments, and track ETAs to dock.

• Expedite and de-expedite based on schedule movement; escalate supplier commit risk with clear impact statements.

• Manage buys against unreleased or non-standard parts, including drop-in samples, distributor spot buys, and broker sourcing when authorized.

• Reconcile pricing, MOQs, NRE, and tooling charges; flag cost drivers ahead of production quoting.

• Change and Configuration Management

• Own material disposition for NPI Program(s) ECOs and deviations: scrap, rework, use-as-is, or run-out.

• Maintain accurate item master for BOMs, CTB/planning trackers, and lead times as well as cost in defined tools for transition into ERP as parts mature from prototype to production status.

• Build Execution Support

• Partner with GSMs on consignment materials required for each build.

• Maintain inventory accuracy for NPI stock at quick turn suppliers, including reconciliation of Figure-consigned material.

• Transition to Production

• Hand off part-level history, supplier commitments, lead times, and planning parameters to the production planning team at ramp.

• Feed EAU forecasts and demand signals to Global Supply Management to support supplier capacity and long-term agreements.

• Process Improvement

• Identify recurring failure points in the NPI material flow and implement fixes to reporting, planning, and cross-functional handoffs.

• Improve the fidelity of build-readiness reporting so risks are mitigated early.

Requirements:

• Education

• Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Engineering, or a related field or applicable industry experience for the role.

• Experience

• 3–5 years in buying, planning, or materials management, with at least 2 years supporting NPI or prototype builds.

• Background in complex electromechanical hardware — robotics, aerospace, medical devices, automotive, or consumer electronics.

• Direct experience buying against immature BOMs and managing engineering change in a live build.

• Technical Skills

• Proficiency with ERP/MRP systems (SAP, Oracle, or NetSuite) and PLM tools (Arena, Enovia, etc)

• Advanced Excel (XLOOKUP, pivot tables, shortage and coverage modeling); SQL or BI tooling a plus.

• Working fluency in reading BOMs; comfortable discussing tolerances, finishes, and component specs with engineers.

• Core Competencies

• High urgency and strong follow-through: you have the ability close loops without being asked twice.

• Comfort operating with incomplete information and changing priorities.

• Clear, direct communication with engineers and suppliers alike; able to translate a slipped ETA into schedule impact leadership can act on.

• Strong attention to detail on revisions, dates, and quantities – this is a role where a single missed line item stops a build.

The US base salary range for this full-time position is $120,000 to $180,000 per year.

The pay offered for this position may vary based on several individual factors, including job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The total compensation package may also include additional components/benefits depending on the specific role. This information will be shared if an employment offer is extended.

jobs.description:
Project Lead, Maritime Consortium

Bring a new consortium model to the undersea and littoral fight

This year, USSOCOM launched SOF RACER, a consortium that is free for companies and exists to rapidly prototype commercial technology. BMNT runs the human engine, framing the right problems, recruiting and preparing companies, and accelerating the impact. Soon, we may be managing a second consortium built on the same model for the maritime domain: undersea and seabed systems, littoral and expeditionary operations, mine countermeasures, and the autonomous and robotic systems. We need someone to run the day to day work.

You will be the person that a Navy program office calls when they have a problem and the reason a maritime robotics founder decides consortium membership was the best decision they made all year. You will be BMNT's first maritime domain lead.

What you will actually do

• Own the demand engine. Build and keep the relationships with the Navy program offices, labs, and operating units where maritime problems are born. Take them from "we have this problem," to a problem statement the whole consortium competes on.

• Own member value. Companies stay in the consortium because it's worth their time through rapid onboarding and member resources that you will help execute.

• Translate in both directions. Turn operator and engineer language into problem statements that an entrepreneur can act on, and keep the government side confident that what they said was not lost in translation.

• Filter honestly. You will hear lots of problems. The job is finding the right ones: real users, real pain, someone with authority who cares, and the funding for prototyping.

• Run point on the moments that matter. Industry days, curation sessions, white paper workshops, demo events, and the follow-through afterward.

Who thrives in this seat

• You have lived in the maritime domain: undersea or surface unmanned systems, mine warfare, EOD or diving, expeditionary operations, naval test and evaluation, or industry. When you walk into a Navy warfare center, people assume you belong there.

• You have worked government acquisition in the form of OTAs, consortia, SBIR, accelerators, or federal business development where your job was earning a program manager's trust.

• You can brief a Navy leader in the morning and coach a seed-stage founder in the afternoon, and you genuinely like both conversations.

• You do only 25 to 40 percent of the talking in a discovery conversation and treat what you learn as the product of your effort.

• You are comfortable with autonomy and ambiguity, and you ask for help early and loudly when it affects the mission.

• Clearance: active Secret preferred; you must be eligible for TS/SCI. U.S. citizenship required.

Why BMNT

We are the 40-person Silicon Valley company that has spent a decade proving commercial innovation methods work in national security. Our methods trace to the Army's Rapid Equipping Force, which our founder led; we run the Hacking for Defense program across 67 universities; and our pipelines have moved real technology, including ocean sensors, photonic navigation, and edge AI, into operational hands. We just helped end the consortium-fee model that taxed the defense industrial base for two decades, and we hope to bring that model to the water. We’re a small company with no layers, a national mission, and your fingerprints can be on all of it.

The details

In office or hybrid with monthly travel, especially wherever the government problem owners are. Compensation is between $105,000 to $165,000 and determined by location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

BMNT is a certified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business and an equal opportunity employer.

If you are a self-starter with an obsession for outcomes, not activities and a history of achievements, and enjoy working on projects with collaborative and creative teams, this could be the right role for you!

jobs.title: Senior Recruiter, GTM & Sales

More than half of all working Americans are not saving enough for their future. Too often, it’s because they are employed by a company that doesn’t offer a retirement plan. Human Interest is changing that by making it affordable and accessible for small and medium-sized businesses to offer employees a path to financial independence through retirement savings.

We’re a high-growth fintech company changing the retirement industry. We are backed by a number of investors. This includes funding from Marshall Wace and Baillie Gifford, as well as top investors such as BlackRock, TPG (The Rise Fund), SoftBank, Glynn Capital, NewView Capital, USVP, Wing, Uncork, and more.

We’re a high-growth fintech company backed by top investors including BlackRock, SoftBank, and TPG. We are looking for a Senior GTM Recruiter to help us scale our most critical revenue-generating and support functions.

About the role

As a Senior GTM Recruiter, you will be a full-cycle owner responsible for the entire hiring lifecycle for our Sales and Go-To-Market organizations. This is a high-impact role that requires the speed of a Sales Recruiter and the strategic mindset of a Business Partner. You will attract top-tier talent for roles ranging from SDRs and Account Executives to Sales Leadership, Marketing, and Operations.

What you get to do every day

• Drive Full-Cycle Recruitment: Manage the end-to-end process for a portfolio of diverse roles (Sales, Marketing, CS&O, and Leadership), from strategic sourcing and interviewing to complex offer negotiations and closing.

• Lead Hiring Partner Consultation: Act as a strategic advisor to Revenue leadership. Facilitate weekly hiring meetings, provide expert guidance on market trends, and lead talent assessment recalibrations.

• Strategic Sourcing: Build and maintain a robust pipeline of passive talent using LinkedIn Recruiter and other innovative sourcing channels, ensuring we always have a "warm" bench for high-attrition or high-growth areas.

• Champion Candidate Experience: Embody Human Interest’s values, ensuring every candidate—regardless of the outcome—has an exceptional and transparent experience.

• Maintain Operational Excellence: Use Greenhouse and interview intelligence tools (like BrightHire) to track metrics, identify bottlenecks, and drive data-driven improvements in our hiring velocity.

• Contribute to Strategic Projects: Lead or participate in TA initiatives such as employer branding, DEI sourcing strategies, and process optimization to "raise the bar" for talent across the org.

What you bring to the role

• 5+ years of in-house full-cycle recruiting experience in a fast-paced, high-growth environment (Fintech or SaaS preferred).

• Dual Expertise: A proven track record of successfully hiring for high-volume sales roles and complex GTM/Corporate functions.

• Expert Sourcing: Advanced proficiency with LinkedIn Recruiter and a proactive "headhunter" mindset for passive talent.

• Consultative Approach: Exceptional communication and negotiation skills with the ability to influence senior stakeholders and business leaders.

• Analytical Mindset: Ability to use data to tell a story, identify hiring trends, and solve recruiting challenges.

• Adaptability: A proactive, problem-solving mindset with the ability to navigate the ambiguity of a scaling startup.

• Remote Fluency: Self-motivated and highly effective working independently in a remote environment.

Nice to have

• Expertise with Greenhouse ATS.

• Familiarity with BrightHire or other interview intelligence platforms.

• Ability to work in all US time zones.

Why you will love working at Human Interest

Human Interest is tackling one of our country's biggest challenges - closing the retirement gap. You'll be instrumental in architecting and scaling solutions that bring financial security to employees at small and medium-sized businesses nationwide. We’ve made significant progress, but there is still growth ahead, offering you a unique opportunity to solve complex problems, drive innovation, and advance your career alongside a dedicated, mission-driven team. We value hard work and recognize that our team's contributions are key to our continued success.

Join Human Interest and make a lasting impact by shaping the future of retirement.

Our operating principles define how we work together as a team. They reflect Human Interest’s unique view on what’s important and what’s right. Documenting this core aspect of our culture helps employees make good decisions on their own. It also helps candidates considering career opportunities critically evaluate whether they will thrive at Human Interest.

• Customer obsession: We're all about creating amazing experiences for our customers. We put their needs first and go the extra mile to make them smile.

• Long-Term Orientation: We're not just playing for today; we're building a legacy. We think big, plan strategically, and invest in our future.

• Autonomous and Accountable Teams: We trust our team members to take ownership and make smart decisions. We empower you to be your best self!

• An Escalating Bar for Talent and Performance: We're constantly raising the bar and challenging ourselves to be better. We believe in growth and continuous improvement.

• Fundamental Optimism: We see the glass as half full (and then we fill it up with more amazing ideas!). We believe in the power of positivity and the potential for greatness.

jobs.title: Robotics Intern, Post-Training and Continual Learning
jobs.description:
At Toyota Research Institute (TRI), we’re on a mission to improve the quality of human life. We’re developing new tools and capabilities to amplify the human experience. To lead this transformative shift in mobility, we’ve built a world-class team advancing the state of the art in AI, robotics, driving, and material sciences.
This is a paid 12-week internship opportunity and is a hybrid, in-office role.
Here’s a glimpse into the Internship experience from some of our TRI interns!


The Team

Our team in the Robotics division is developing pretrained generalist policies that can support a broad range of tasks, environments, and robotic systems. A central scientific challenge is determining how these broadly pretrained policies can be efficiently adapted to new target tasks while achieving the reliability, precision, and robustness required for real-world use.

Pretraining can provide a policy with broad behavioral capabilities, but those capabilities may not immediately translate into dependable performance in a specific deployment setting. Effective post-training methods are therefore essential for converting general capabilities into policies that can adapt quickly, learn from limited additional data or interaction, and perform consistently on demanding downstream tasks.

The Opportunity 

Our research interests include reinforcement learning, imitation learning, human-in-the-loop learning, simulation, world models, policy distillation, and large-scale robot learning. We aim to advance the scientific foundations of policy adaptation while developing methods that may ultimately be evaluated or deployed within internal research projects involving real-world industrial tasks.

Potential research directions include, but are not limited to: 
Offline-to-online reinforcement learning
DAgger, imitation learning, and human-in-the-loop policy improvement
Sim-to-real policy distillation and adaptation
Policy improvement, planning, or data generation using world models
Data-efficient adaptation to new tasks and environments

jobs.description:
Job Title/Position: Director Revenue Cycle

Location: Nashville, TN preferred or in market (remote with light travel)

Reports To: Vice President of Finance

About Luminary Hospice:

At Luminary Hospice, we are a mission-driven organization that empowers our team members to shape our culture in order to allow them to provide the highest quality support to patients and families throughout their entire end-of-life journey.

Our mission is to deliver personalized care that radiates compassion and preserves dignity for all that we are honored to serve on their end-of-life journey. We are centered on caring for the whole person – with expert medical care, pain management as well as emotional and spiritual support along with resources, information, and emotional support for families and caregivers.

About the role:

Luminary Hospice is seeking a Director of Revenue Cycle to own the entire revenue cycle for our growing, multi-state, multi-site hospice organization. That covers everything from eligibility verification through final account resolution. This leader is the single accountable executive for how we get paid: accurately, compliantly, and on time. The role manages our third-party RCM billing vendor, partners with local agencies to drive best practices, and builds a revenue cycle operation that scales as we add locations, states, and payers.

This is a hands-on role. The ideal candidate knows hospice reimbursement in detail, including NOEs, benefit periods, CTI and face-to-face requirements, levels of care, SIA, RTPs, ADRs, and room and board. They should be comfortable digging into individual accounts to find root causes.

Job Responsibilities:

Revenue Cycle Ownership

• Own the full hospice revenue cycle across all sites and states, along with every revenue cycle KPI: cash, DSO, unbilled days, NOE timeliness, claim holds, denials, aging, and write-offs

• Set revenue cycle strategy, policies, staffing, and goals, and report performance and risks to executive leadership

• Lead front-end functions: eligibility and benefit verification, authorizations, and financial clearance for room and board and Medicaid pending patients

• Own pre-billing audit and revenue integrity across levels of care, SIA, and rate maintenance

• Oversee NOE/NOTR filing, monthly claim submission, RTP correction, timely filing, payer follow-up, denials, and appeals for ADR, TPE, and other medical reviews

• Drive timely resolution of claim holds, such as unsigned orders, missing CTIs or face-to-face encounters, NOE issues, and eligibility gaps, so claims go out on schedule every billing cycle

• Oversee payment posting, adjustments, recoupments, credit balances, refunds, and reconciliation of cash to bank deposits, remittances, and the general ledger

• Own Medicare and Medicaid enrollment for all provider numbers, Hospice Cap monitoring and reporting, and revenue cycle readiness for new sites and acquisitions

Third-Party RCM Vendor Management

• Manage our third-party RCM billing vendor, including scope of work, SLAs, performance scorecards, and regular operating reviews

• Hold the vendor accountable for submission timeliness, follow-up, posting accuracy, backlog, and cash results, and escalate and correct gaps quickly

• Keep independent oversight through account-level audits and validation of vendor-reported metrics, and advise on contract terms and renewal

Local Agency Partnership

• Collaborate with local agency leaders to make sure revenue cycle best practices are followed consistently at every location

• Train agency teams on admission paperwork, election statements, CTI and face-to-face timeliness, orders, and documentation requirements

• Hold regular reviews with each agency covering claim holds, unbilled days, NOE timeliness, and denials, with clear owners and follow-up

Process, Systems, and People

• Standardize workflows, SOPs, and controls across all sites, and build dashboards that turn data into action

• Find system and workflow gaps in the EMR ([HCHB / WellSky / Axxess / MatrixCare]) and clearinghouse, and evaluate automation and AI opportunities responsibly

• Build and develop the revenue cycle team through clear expectations, coaching, and performance management

• Work with Finance on month-end close, reserves, cash forecasting, and Cap liability, and maintain compliance with the Hospice CoPs, CMS/MAC and state Medicaid rules, HIPAA, and internal policies

Job Qualifications:

• Bachelor's degree in healthcare administration, business, finance, or a related field, or equivalent experience

• 10+ years of healthcare revenue cycle experience, including 5+ years in leadership. Hospice revenue cycle experience is required.

• Experience leading the full revenue cycle for a multi-site hospice organization, preferably across multiple states

• Expert knowledge of the Medicare Hospice Benefit and hospice billing, from eligibility and NOE through payment, denials, and final resolution

• Experience managing a third-party RCM or billing vendor through SLAs, scorecards, and audits

• Experience working with agency or field leadership to reduce claim holds and improve documentation

• Proven ability to build or turn around revenue cycle operations, with strong analytical skills and a track record of leading teams through change and growth

Preferred Qualifications:

• Master's degree in healthcare administration, business, or finance

• Experience with hospice acquisitions, de novo locations or system conversions

• Experience with multiple MACs, state Medicaid programs, Hospice Cap, and medical review

• Experience with hospice EMRs (HCHB, WellSky, Axxess, MatrixCare) and revenue cycle automation

• Certification such as CHFP, CRCR, CHPCA, or CHPC

Physical Demands:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit or stand. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds.

Equal Employment Opportunity:

Luminary Hospice is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. We do not discriminate against any applicant or employee based on race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. We are committed to providing a work environment free from discrimination and harassment, where all individuals are treated with respect and dignity. All employment decisions at Luminary Hospice are based on business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications.

Compensation and Benefits:

Luminary Hospice offers a competitive compensation package, along with a comprehensive benefits package that includes health, dental, and vision insurance, retirement savings options, and more. Our benefits are designed to support your health, well-being, and long-term financial goals.

jobs.title: Senior Radar Algorithms Engineer
jobs.description:
Radar Reinvented.

Echodyne offers the world’s first compact solid-state true beam-steering radar for a wide range of industries and applications. Our high-performance radars work in all weather and are designed for autonomous vehicles, uncrewed aircraft & drones, and security of borders, critical infrastructure, and smart cities. The company combines the patented technology of metamaterials with powerful software to create a radar sensor with unprecedented performance at commercial price points. Echodyne offers its radars to companies working in Automotive, Transportation, Critical Infrastructure Protection, Border Security, Smart Cities, Uncrewed Aircraft Systems (UAS), and Airspace Management including Urban Air Mobility (UTM).

Echodyne is seeking a Senior Radar Algorithms Engineer to join our fast-growing team.

ROLE OVERVIEW

The Senior Radar Algorithms Engineer will play a key role in advancing the performance and capability of Echodyne’s current and future radar systems. This position focuses on the research, design, and development of radar algorithms—from concept and simulation to system validation. The ideal candidate combines deep radar domain knowledge with strong analytical and problem-solving skills, using simulation and real-world data to innovate in areas such as clutter mitigation, interference suppression, and field calibration.

Working within a small, highly collaborative radar algorithms team, this individual will partner closely with experts in antennas, electrical engineering, software engineering, and data analysis to ensure that new algorithmic approaches translate effectively to high-performing radar systems. This role is ideal for a radar algorithms engineer who enjoys exploring novel solutions, building models and simulations, and developing a deep understanding of radar phenomenology to push the boundaries of sensing performance.

RESPONSIBILITIES

• Contribute to the design, simulation, and prototyping of advanced radar signal processing and control algorithms for FMCW and pulsed radar systems.

• Develop MATLAB/Python simulations to design, test, and evaluate algorithms for radar performance, clutter suppression, interference mitigation, and system control.

• Analyze radar data to characterize performance, identify failure modes, and derive insights that guide algorithmic and system-level improvements.

• Collaborate with Electromagnetics, Electrical Engineering, Software, and Data teams to ensure algorithms complement real-world hardware and environmental constraints and are implemented correctly in production code.

• Support the bring-up and verification of next-generation radar hardware and signal processing chains.

• Participate in architecture discussions, code reviews, and technical mentorship across the algorithms team.

• Document and communicate algorithm design rationale, performance results, and system implications across technical teams.

REQUIRED SKILLS / EXPERIENCE

• Deep understanding of radar systems, including waveform design, signal processing, and system-level architecture.

• Strong background in radar signal processing for LFM high gain, analog beam-forming

• Strong proficiency in MATLAB and/or Python for simulation and algorithm prototyping.

• Practical understanding of electromagnetics, antennas, wave propagation, and classical mechanics.

• Has demonstrated ability to take problem statement to algorithm prototype.

• Experience working collaboratively across hardware and software disciplines.

• Proficiency with modern software development practices, including source control, testing, and documentation.

DESIRED SKILLS / EXPERIENCE
(Looking for one or more as a complement to the core skills)

• Strong mathematical foundation, including statistical signal processing, estimation theory, and linear algebra.

• Experience with multi-sensor or multi-radar coexistence, frequency management, or cognitive radar concepts.

• Experience with sensor fusion, tracking, or state estimation (e.g., Kalman filtering).

• Familiarity with object detection and classification using radar data.

• Experience with embedded systems, real-time signal processing, or RTOS environments.

• Exposure to IMU/GPS integration or motion compensation techniques.

• Experience with instrument control and automated test systems.

QUALIFICATIONS

• BS in Electrical Engineering, Physics, Applied Math, or a related field with 5+ years of experience, or MS with 4+ years, or PhD with 2+ years.

Echodyne’s technology is export controlled by the U.S. Government and we must evaluate an applicant’s eligibility to handle export-controlled information or obtain required Government authorizations.  Therefore, we will ask you as part of the application process to identify whether you are a U.S. Citizen or green card holder, or have asylum/refugee status in the U.S.

WHAT WE OFFER

This is an exempt role.

$137,196—$205,382 USD

If your skills generally align but not perfectly, please apply anyway. There may be another role that’s a great fit for you!

jobs.title: Product Marketing Manager
jobs.description:
What We’re Building

Honeycomb is a service for the near and present future, defining observability and raising expectations of what developer tools can do! We’re working with well known companies like HelloFresh, Slack, LaunchDarkly, and Vanguard and more across a range of industries. This is an exciting time in our trajectory, we’ve closed Series D funding, scaled past the 200-person mark, and were named to Forbes’ America’s Best Startups of 2022 and 2023!

If you want to see what we’ve been up to, please check out these blog posts and Honeycomb.io press releases.

Who We Are

We come for the impact, and stay for the culture! We’re a talented, opinionated, passionate, fiercely inclusive, and responsible group of bees. We have conviction and we strive to live our values every day. We want our people to do what they truly love amongst a team of highly talented (but humble) peers.

How We Work

We are a fully distributed company, which means we believe it is not where you sit, but how you deliver that matters most. We invest in our people and care about how you orient to our culture and processes. At the same time we imbue a lot of trust, autonomy, and accountability from Day 1. #LI-Remote

Little more about the team:

Product marketing at Honeycomb is a small team with a wide surface area. We decide how Honeycomb is positioned, what we say at launch, what the sales team brings into a deal, and how an engineer who has never heard of us understands the product in the first two minutes. Because the team is small, the work is broad: in one week you might rewrite a product page, build a competitive one-pager, interview a customer, and run the launch checklist for a new feature.

This role is built for someone early in a product marketing career who wants to systematically improve the customer buying journey. As a product and messaging expert, you will partner with go-to-market teams to drive business impact through sales and marketing campaigns. You will get real ownership of real launches, and you will have senior product marketers, a technical field team, and engineers who like explaining their work close at hand. Our audience is engineers and platform teams, so the bar is accuracy first: we would rather be precise and useful than clever.

What you’ll do in the role:

You will support and execute product marketing across Honeycomb's core products, with a generalist mix of messaging, launches, content, enablement, and competitive work. Expect to start by contributing to pieces of each and to own more of them over your first year.

Responsibilities

• Messaging and positioning: Write and maintain messaging for features and product areas, from the one-sentence version an engineer reads on a web page to the slide a sales engineer uses in a technical conversation. Keep it accurate and grounded in what the product actually does.

• Launches: Run launch execution for small and mid-sized releases and support the larger ones. Build the plan, write the assets, coordinate Product, Marketing, Sales Engineering, and Customer Success, and report on how the launch performed.

• Content: Produce the practical material that helps people evaluate and adopt Honeycomb: blog posts, solution briefs, web copy, demo scripts, FAQs, and customer-facing one-pagers.

• Sales enablement: Equip the field with what they need to run a good conversation, including pitch narratives, objection handling, battlecards, and release updates. Join customer calls, listen to recorded ones, and fix the material that isn't landing.

• Competitive and market intelligence: Track the observability market and competitor moves. Maintain competitive assets and keep them current and honest, so the field trusts them.

• Voice of customer and proof points: Talk to customers and prospects, turn what you hear into case studies, quotes, and proof points, and bring the patterns back to Product and Marketing.

• Measurement: Help define what success looks like for your work, pull the data, and share what you learn, including the things that didn't work.

What you’ll bring to the role:

• 2 to 5 years of experience in product marketing, or in a closely adjacent go-to-market role such as content marketing, sales engineering, technical writing, developer relations, or product management, with at least some of it in B2B SaaS.

• Strong writing. You can take a dense technical explanation and turn it into something short, accurate, and useful, and you can tell the difference between the two yourself.

• Curiosity about technical products and the patience to learn how they work. You ask engineers questions until you actually understand the answer, and you are comfortable in a product that assumes a technical user.

• Passion about the team winning: Sales, marketing, and product teams will depend on you to succeed. Their success is your success, but you’re not simply an order taker: you look for the smart solutions and don’t wait to be asked.

• The ability to run a project across teams without formal authority: setting a timeline, chasing the open items, and telling people clearly when something has slipped.

• Comfort with ambiguity and a bias toward shipping. Our priorities move, the team is small, and the best work here comes from people who start rather than wait for a brief.

• Willingness to use data to decide and to evaluate your own work honestly.

• Demonstrated experience applying AI tooling in your work.

Nice to have

• Exposure to observability, developer tools, distributed tracing, OpenTelemetry, platform engineering, or reliability and SLO practices. We will teach this, but a head start helps.

• Experience marketing to engineers as the primary audience.

• Hands-on familiarity with AI and LLM tooling, including coding agents and MCP-based workflows.

• Experience with webinars, conference talks, or community programs.

• Experience working in a fully distributed company.

Base Salary based on level of experience

$125,000—$190,000 USD

What you'll get when you join the Hive:

• A stake in our success - generous equity with employee-friendly stock program

• It’s not about how strong of a negotiator you are - our pay is based on transparent levels relative to experience

• Time to recharge with unlimited PTO

• A distributed-first mindset and culture (really!)

• Home office, co-working, and internet stipend

• Full benefits coverage for employees, with additional coverage available for dependents

• Up to 16 weeks of paid parental leave, regardless of path to parenthood

• Annual development allowance

• And much more...

Please note we cannot currently sponsor or support visa transfers at this time. Additionally, in compliance with applicable law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work.

Phishing and Recruitment Scam Warning:

We take your security seriously. Please be aware that recruitment scams are increasingly common and scammers may create email addresses or websites to impersonate Honeycomb employees. To help protect you:

• All communications will come from an @honeycomb.io email address We occasionally work with external recruiting agencies. These partners will use legitimate business email addresses—never personal accounts like Gmail or Yahoo.

• Our recruiting process will never ask you to provide financial or sensitive personal information, including but not limited to: Social security or tax identification numbers Credit card numbers Bank account information

Diversity & Accommodations:

We're committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and equitable workplace—where people of all backgrounds, identities, experiences, and abilities are welcomed, valued, and supported. We recognize that there is no single path to success and embrace nontraditional career journeys and diverse perspectives as key to building stronger, more innovative teams.

We strive to ensure an inclusive experience throughout every stage of our hiring process and are happy to provide reasonable accommodations as needed. If you require accommodations or accessible formats at any point during our hiring process, please let your recruiter know.

As an equal opportunity employer our hiring process is designed to put you at ease and help you show your best work. If there’s anything we can do to improve your experience, we’re always open to feedback.

Privacy Notice:

If you apply for a job at Honeycomb and your application is unsuccessful (or you withdraw from the process or decline our offer), Honeycomb will retain your information after your application for a period of time in accordance with local laws. We retain this information for various reasons, including in case we face a legal challenge in respect of a recruitment decision, to consider you for other current or future jobs at Honeycomb, and to help us better understand, analyze and improve our recruitment processes.

For more information regarding our privacy practices please see the Honeycomb Privacy Notice.

If you do not want us to retain your information, or want us to update it, please contact privacy@honeycomb.io. Please note, however, that we may retain some information if required by law or as necessary to protect ourselves from legal claims.

jobs.description:
About Culligan Quench
Culligan Quench’s purpose is to impact people’s lives and improve the earth by helping to eliminate the 500 million plastic bottles consumed each year. We play a front-line role in the battle against single-use plastic water bottles by delivering on-demand filtered water solutions to more than 120,000 healthy and environmentally conscious customers across North America. Our bottle-free water coolers, ice machines, sparkling water dispensers and coffee brewers purify the existing water supply, providing an endless supply of clean water and water-based beverages for a fixed monthly fee, typically under a long term bundled service and rental subscription agreement.  Culligan Quench has grown from a small regional company to an international leader that had a successful NYSE public offering in 2016 and is now a strategic company owned by private equity backed Culligan.  Headquartered in King of Prussia, PA, Quench has more than 1,600 team members operating out of more than 90 locations across North America and Puerto Rico. For more information visit https://quench.culligan.com/
 
About Culligan
 There’s nothing more fundamental to life on Earth than water.  At Culligan, we believe transforming water can transform the world. That's why we offer expert water services and industry-leading solutions globally. Local Culligan teams deliver better drinking water to people at work, at home and on the go. With expertise across service, science and sustainability, Culligan turns water you can live with into water you can love.  For more information visit www.culligan.com. 
 
Values: 5Cs
Culligan as One
Customers come first
Commitment to Innovation
Courage to do what's right
Consistently deliver exceptional results

The Senior Account Manager is responsible for the satisfaction, loyalty and retention of Quench's largest customers. As such, each Sr. Customer Care Account Manager is specially trained to handle any questions or escalated concerns within their customer base and work with Quench's Leadership and Sales Partners on broad scale solutions when necessary.  
 
 
Position is full time and salaried: Base salary is $50,000 annually

Position Summary

The Sales Representative I, will call on veterinary customers and work with distributor partners to grow product sales, while increasing category market share within the animal health industry. Equal Opportunity Employer

Apply today to join an employee-owned organization dedicated to supporting animal health through expertise, service, and innovation.

jobs.title: Field Services Engineer II
jobs.description:
Proconex is the exclusive Emerson Impact Partner for Emerson Automation Solutions in the Mid-Atlantic region. We provide a full portfolio of Process Automation Control Systems, Valves and Control Devices, and related technologies and services to a range of customers—in the Life Sciences, Chemical, Power, Refining, Oil & Gas, Food & Beverage, Paper, Metals, and other industries, as well as commercial enterprises and campus facilities. With three strategically located offices, Proconex maintains a deep dedication to its 200+ employees, a sharp focus on safety and quality, and the drive to deliver.

Job Title

Field Services Engineer II

Job Overview

The Field Services Engineer II provides field-based engineering services to support the maintenance, troubleshooting, deployment, lifecycle management, and optimization of industrial automation systems. This role independently executes preventative maintenance, software and hardware deployments, system upgrades, troubleshooting, and commissioning activities while supporting the planning and execution of customer service engagements. The position requires strong technical expertise, sound judgment, and the ability to effectively manage priorities while delivering high-quality customer service.

Key Responsibilities

• Independently support customer service engagements, including planning, coordination, scheduling, and execution activities.

• Build and maintain strong customer relationships by communicating project status, technical findings, recommendations, and risks throughout service engagements.

• Perform preventative maintenance activities and system health assessments on medium- to high-complexity industrial automation systems to improve reliability and reduce downtime.

• Troubleshoot and resolve intermediate automation, hardware, software, instrumentation, server, workstation, and network issues, escalating advanced issues when appropriate.

• Execute software installations, upgrades, patches, migrations, and system deployment activities in accordance with engineering standards and manufacturer requirements.

• Configure, deploy, and troubleshoot servers, workstations, virtual environments, and associated hardware components to support automation system performance and reliability.

• Support lifecycle planning initiatives by identifying system risks, developing corrective action recommendations, and executing defined lifecycle improvement activities.

• Contribute to project execution activities, including system setup, testing, Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), Site Acceptance Testing (SAT), commissioning, startup, and migration support.

• Develop customer-ready technical documentation, service reports, redlines, and system records in accordance with company and customer standards.

• Apply industrial networking, cybersecurity, and software architecture principles during maintenance, troubleshooting, and deployment activities.

• Identify project risks, scope gaps, and additional customer needs while communicating opportunities and concerns to appropriate stakeholders.

• Maintain required technical training, certifications, and professional development activities while supporting a culture of safety, quality, and continuous improvement.

This role requires regular travel to customer sites and the ability to support field-based service activities as business needs require.

Basic Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Engineering Technology, Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related technical field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

• 3+ years of experience supporting industrial automation systems, instrumentation, controls, field service operations, or related technical environments.

• 3+ years of experience troubleshooting automation hardware, software, instrumentation, networking, or computer systems.

• 3+ years of experience working with Microsoft Windows operating systems, software deployments, and system upgrades.

• 3+ years of experience independently executing customer-facing technical service or support engagements.

• 3+ years of experience following technical procedures, quality standards, cybersecurity requirements, and safety protocols.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with Emerson DeltaV or other Distributed Control Systems (DCS).

• Experience supporting PLC, SCADA, or industrial automation systems.

• Experience configuring and deploying servers, workstations, and virtualized environments.

• Working knowledge of industrial networking, cybersecurity, and software architecture principles.

• Experience with Windows Server administration.

• Familiarity with SQL databases and database management concepts.

• Knowledge of industrial electrical systems, instrumentation, and wiring practices.

• Experience supporting commissioning, startup, migration, or lifecycle management activities in industrial process environments.

• Experience participating in an industrial on-call support rotation.

We are proud to be an employee-owned organization. Through our ESOP, every team member shares in the growth and success of the company, fostering a culture of collaboration, accountability, and long-term rewards.

Proconex offers a standout culture, fantastic work environment, and has very competitive benefits to include premium medical, 401K match, tuition reimbursement, and other unique incentives.

jobs.title: Principal Manufacturing Engineer (Integration)
jobs.description:
About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About This Role

As the Principal Manufacturing Engineer (Integration) at Varda, you will be the central orchestrator of spacecraft final assembly — responsible for the processes, sequence, and documentation that bring every subsystem together into a complete, flight-ready vehicle. You will own integration procedures from subassembly mating through final closeout, working at the convergence of structures, propulsion, avionics, and TPS to ensure every build is executed accurately, safely, and on schedule. This role demands exceptional situational awareness, meticulous attention to process discipline, and the confidence to resolve conflicts between subsystems in real time on the factory floor. If you thrive on complexity and find satisfaction in watching a spacecraft come together under your direction, this is the role for you.

Responsibilities

• Own spacecraft integration sequences and procedures from subassembly mating through final vehicle closeout and acceptance

• Develop, maintain, and continuously improve assembly travelers and integration work instructions that sequence all subsystem interfaces correctly

• Serve as the primary interface between manufacturing and all engineering disciplines (structures, propulsion, avionics, TPS) during vehicle integration

• Identify and resolve interface conflicts, clearance issues, and assembly sequence problems before they impact build schedule

• Lead integration readiness reviews and ensure all pre-integration checkpoints — cleanliness, FOD sweeps, torque records, pin-to-pin checks — are completed and documented

• Drive root cause analysis and RCCA for integration non-conformances; disposition MRBs in coordination with design engineering

• Track integration metrics (planned vs. actual cycle time, NCR rates, rework hours) and implement targeted improvements to hit cadence goals

• Define tooling and lifting/handling equipment requirements for safe vehicle integration operations

Basic Qualifications

• B.S. in Mechanical or Systems Engineering, or a related discipline, with consideration given to equivalent professional experience (typically 6–10+ years)

• 6+ years of experience in vehicle or system-level integration roles or final assembly within aerospace, defense, robotics or similar industries

• Strong understanding of how multiple subsystems (mechanical, electrical, fluid) interface within a vehicle assembly

• Experience developing and executing complex assembly or integration procedures

• Ability to manage competing priorities and make sound, real-time decisions on the production floor

• Exceptional communication and coordination skills across multi-discipline teams

• Must be physically able to regularly lift 25 lbs., bend, stoop, and stand for extended periods while working directly with flight hardware

Preferred Skills and Experience

• M.S. degree in Mechanical Engineering or Electrical Engineering specialized in Embedded Systems, Mechatronics, Control Theory, or similar, or related discipline, with consideration given to equivalent professional experience

• Experience as a lead integration engineer or integration ME on a launch vehicle, satellite, or spacecraft program

• Familiarity with integration and test (I&T) flows for complex aerospace vehicles, including functional testing at each integration milestone

• Background managing integration of flight hardware from multiple subsystem suppliers or internal teams into a single vehicle

• Experience with configuration management and build record documentation in a regulated aerospace environment

• Knowledge of cleanliness and contamination control requirements for propulsion, optical, or precision mechanism integration

• Hands-on experience with vehicle handling — cranes, slings, rotation fixtures, and precision alignment tooling

• Prior work in a manufacturing environment actively scaling from unit builds to multi-vehicle concurrent production

• Experience conducting integration readiness reviews, pre-mate inspections, and post-integration functional checkouts

Pay Range

• Salary Range: $181,913 - $262,763/per year

• This role is on-site in El Segundo, CA

• Leveling and base salary is determined by job-related skills, education level, experience level, and job performance

• You will be eligible for incentives in the form of stock options and/or long-term cash awards

ITAR Requirements

Varda, like all employers, must ensure that its employees working in the United States are lawfully authorized to work in the U.S. Additionally, our employees are exposed to and have access to certain export-controlled items. Because our employees are provided access to export-controlled items, our policy is to only hire “U.S. persons” who are permitted to have access to our technology without an export license.

“US person” means: U.S. citizen, U.S. lawful permanent resident, or protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3) (i.e., individual admitted to the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum).

jobs.title: Automotive Detail Supervisor
jobs.description:
About Carvana
At Carvana, we sell cars but we aren’t car salesmen. Our promise is simple: we won’t sell a car to a customer that we wouldn’t sell to our own Mom. Period. To make sure our cars are in first-rate condition, we’ve built multiple vehicle Reconditioning Centers around the country, where our cars are inspected, perfected, and photographed before reaching the Carvana website. Using our Carvana Certified 150-point inspection process, we’re able to verify that every vehicle meets our rigorous mechanical and cosmetic standards.

We strive to provide only the highest quality vehicles to our customers in our mission to deliver a no-hassle, better car buying experience. We are actively looking for passionate and talented individuals who can help us deliver on that promise.

Think you’ve got what it takes to join our team? Keep reading below to see what we’re looking for!

Position Overview:
Line Lead is a front-line supervisor role, responsible for directly managing and developing a team of hourly associates in an Inspection Center to regularly achieve production targets.

What you’ll be doing:

• Manage the movement of cars into and out of the Inspection Center safely for repairs, while meeting or exceeding set production and quality goals.

• Meet or exceed inventory production goals on a daily, weekly and monthly basis.

• Oversee day-to-day activities of assigned team; identify team’s strengths and weaknesses; determine areas of opportunity and the appropriate steps to improve.

• Engage assigned team, provide appropriate coaching, development and performance management; offer feedback and demonstrate desired skills.

• Create a work and team environment that inspires positive communication, team cohesion, and adherence to Carvana’s Values.

• Proactively communicate information to team members, providing clear understanding of expectations, performance measures, and goals.

• Prevent and resolve conflict among team members.

• Monitor and ensure adherence to systems, policies, procedures, and performance standards.

• Review and approve identified mechanical and physical defects of incoming inventory.

• Lead a team of production associates and partner with the Inspection Center General Manager to repair or reject inventory based on estimated cost of repairs and/or the overall quality of the vehicle.

• Train a team of production associates using Quality Control standards to identify and complete repairs effectively and efficiently the first time, minimizing re-checks and delays in production.

• Identify and complete repairs effectively and efficiently the first time, to minimize re-work and delays in production.

• Conscientiously work in ways that decrease the possibility of injury to yourself or other team members in the shop due to spills or other preventable hazardous conditions.

• Effectively manage multiple associates, including ensuring appropriate employee development and performance management.

What the job requires:
To be able to do your job at Carvana, there are some basic requirements we want to share with you.

• High School Diploma or GED equivalent

• Experience using computers

• Must be at least 18 years of age

• Demonstrated functional expertise in one or more areas pertaining to Carvana’s reconditioning process

• Demonstrated understanding of our current reconditioning processes and lean principles

• Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record (no DUIs and no more than two moving violations in the last 3 years).

• Must be able to lift up to 60 pounds independently; majority of lifting from knee to shoulder heights; other lifting required from various levels

• Requires standing for extended periods of time with frequent stretching, reaching, walking, stooping, pushing, and/or pulling in an environment that may be cold, hot, noisy, and wet and may have fumes or odors due to vehicle maintenance.

• Requires use of safety equipment that may include but not limited to face shield or goggles, non-slip shoes, gloves, mask, and other protective garments and equipment.

• Ability to maintain high volume and high-quality content in a fast-paced environment.

• Ability to effectively delegate tasks to team members.

• Ability to communicate and interact with others effectively in a professional, courteous manner.

• Ability to communicate clearly and concisely, both written and oral.

• Ability to maintain high volume and high-quality content in a fast-paced environment.

• Ability to multitask and prioritize effectively.

• Ability to resolve complex issues with guidance from others.

• Ability to work overtime and on weekends.

• Ability to work variable schedule(s) as necessary.

Of course, we’ll make any reasonable accommodations for those with disabilities to perform the essential functions of their jobs.

What we’ll offer in return

• Full-Time Position with a competitive salary

• Medical, Dental, and Vision benefits

• 401K with company match

• A multitude of perks including student loan payments, discounts on vehicles, benefits for your pets, and much more

• A great wellness program to keep you healthy and happy, both physically and mentally

• Access to opportunities to expand your skillset and share your knowledge with others across the organization

• A company culture of promotions from within, with a start-up atmosphere allowing for varied and rapid career development

• A seat in one of the fastest-growing companies in the country

Legal stuff

jobs.title: iOS Engineer, Identity
jobs.description: • Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career. About the team Before Stripe, every growing internet platform needed a payments team. Today, every growing internet platform needs a way to establish trust in its users. Identity verification is a core piece of economic infrastructure for online businesses. Stripe Identity enables businesses to digitally verify their users through identity documents and other signals for fraud prevention, regulatory, and trust and safety use cases. We are building the future of identity verification and trust in the digital economy. The Identity Product Experience team owns Stripe Identity’s mobile SDKs for iOS, Android, and React Native. These SDKs enable businesses to embed secure, high-quality identity-verification experiences directly in their mobile applications. Our work spans mobile user experience, reusable SDK architecture, camera and document-capture experiences, developer experience, security, accessibility, reliability, and integration with Stripe’s backend systems. Why Stripe Identity? Build mobile experiences that help establish trust between businesses and their users. Solve challenging product and technical problems involving mobile platforms, sensitive data, fraud prevention, and global scale. Create SDKs used by developers across industries, including fintech, marketplaces, and online platforms. Help shape the future of digital identity and make verification easier, safer, and more accessible. Our vision is to build the world’s most trusted store of verified identities, enabling frictionless identity verification across Stripe and beyond. We’re looking for engineers who care deeply about mobile craft and the entire user journey. You should enjoy translating complex technical and regulatory requirements into simple, polished experiences; working through ambiguity; and learning new technologies and systems. Join us to build mobile identity-verification experiences that businesses can integrate easily and that their users can trust. What you’ll do Responsibilities As an iOS engineer on the Identity team, you will: Design, build, and maintain Stripe Identity’s mobile SDKs and verification experiences across iOS, Android, and React Native. Create intuitive, polished experiences for complex flows such as identity-document and selfie capture, while accounting for accessibility, device capabilities, and varied real-world conditions. Build reliable and extensible SDK APIs and reusable components that make it easy for developers to integrate Stripe Identity into their applications. Work across mobile clients, supporting APIs, and services to deliver features end to end rather than treating the mobile application as an isolated layer. Improve SDK performance, reliability, observability, testing, release processes, and backward compatibility. Make thoughtful architectural decisions that balance user experience, developer experience, security, privacy, and long-term maintainability. Partner closely with product managers, designers, machine-learning engineers, backend engineers, user researchers, and other mobile teams. Work with Stripe users and field teams to understand integration challenges and turn their feedback into product and platform improvements. Help establish and evolve mobile-engineering practices across Identity and Stripe. Operate and maintain the systems and SDKs the team owns, including diagnosing production issues and improving them based on what we learn. Who you are We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. Minimum requirements 3+ years of professional software-development experience, including meaningful experience building and shipping mobile applications or SDKs. Experience developing for at least one major mobile platform using technologies such as Swift or Objective-C for iOS Strong software-design fundamentals and experience creating maintainable APIs, components, or frameworks. Experience delivering mobile functionality beyond an isolated UI layer for example, integrating with APIs and services, handling local state, or working with device capabilities. Experience testing, debugging, monitoring, and improving mobile software in production. Ability to collaborate effectively with engineering, product, design, and other technical and non-technical partners. A demonstrated commitment to building high-quality user and developer experiences. Preferred qualifications Experience building mobile SDKs, shared libraries, or developer-facing APIs used outside your immediate team. Experience with both iOS and Android, or with cross-platform technologies such as React Native or Kotlin Multiplatform. Experience with camera, image-processing, document-capture, biometrics, or other device-integrated mobile experiences. Experience designing mobile software that handles sensitive data and applies security and privacy principles by default. Familiarity with accessibility, internationalization, mobile performance, and unreliable network conditions. Experience with mobile CI, automated testing, release automation, observability, or developer-productivity tooling. Experience contributing to backend APIs or services that support mobile products. Ability to simplify complex requirements and favor durable, scalable solutions. Comfort reasoning clearly and moving with urgency in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment. Familiarity with Stripe’s products, ideally through integrating Stripe APIs or SDKs into another application.

jobs.title: Principal Manufacturing Engineer (Structures)
jobs.description:
About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About This Role

As the Principal Manufacturing Engineer (Structures) at Varda, you will own the manufacturing processes for primary and secondary structural assemblies that form the backbone of our reentry capsules and spacecraft. From composite layup and cure operations to machined metallic substructures and bonded panel assemblies, you will bridge the gap between structural design intent and production reality. You will work shoulder-to-shoulder with structural design engineers and a skilled technician team to drive process discipline, eliminate rework, and steadily increase vehicle build cadence. This is a hands-on role for someone who understands how parts are actually made, not just how they are designed, and who is energized by the challenge of scaling a complex aerospace manufacturing operation.

Responsibilities

• Own manufacturing processes for composite structures (wet layup, prepreg, autoclave/oven cure), machined metallic components, and bonded assemblies

• Develop and maintain detailed work instructions, process specifications, and manufacturing travelers for all structural build operations

• Provide DFM feedback to structural design engineers on composite part design, tooling accessibility, bond joint design, and fastener patterns

• Implement and enforce cleanliness, FOD prevention, and contamination control procedures for composite and bonded structure operations

• Lead non-conformance investigations and root cause corrective actions for structural build defects and materials issues, including dimensional discrepancies and tolerance stackups, coating failures or damage to structure or protective coatings

• Define and procure tooling — drill jigs, assembly fixtures — required to support production scaling

• Refine floor layouts and product flow for structural subassembly work cells to reduce travel time and improve throughput

• Coordinate with supply chain on incoming material inspection requirements for composite materials, adhesives, and structural raw stock

Basic Qualifications

• B.S. in Mechanical or Materials Engineering, or a related discipline, with consideration given to equivalent professional experience (typically 6–10+ years)

• 6+ years of manufacturing experience with structural assembly or manufacturing — Riveted or welded structures, machined metals, or composites and bonded structures

• Strong understanding of structural static loads analysis, mechanical properties of materials and processes used to assemble riveted and bolted structures.

• Hands-on experience assembling and fabricating structural assemblies, such as welding, adhesive bonding, or riveting.

• Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, GD&T callouts, and structural assembly models

• Experience writing and maintaining manufacturing process documentation and work instructions

• Strong problem-solving skills; able to diagnose structural build defects and drive corrective action through to closure

• Must be physically able to regularly lift 25 lbs., bend, stoop, and stand for extended periods while working directly with hardware

Preferred Skills and Experience

• M.S. degree in Mechanical engineering specialized in Materials Science, Structural Analysis, or related discipline, with consideration given to equivalent professional experience

• Experience manufacturing primary flight structures for launch vehicles, satellites, or reentry systems

• Familiarity and strong understanding of dynamic and vibrational loads analysis

• Background in transitioning structural assemblies from R&D/prototype to rate production, including tooling qualification

• Knowledge of and familiarity with the manufacture of aerospace structural materials like aluminum alloys, titanium, and steel in a manufacturing context

• Experience with 3D CAD tools (CATIA, SolidWorks, NX) for tooling design and assembly model review

• Familiarity with first article inspection (FAI) processes and FAIR documentation requirements

• Prior experience at a new-space or defense prime where structural production cadence was actively being increased

Pay Range

• Salary Range: $181,913 - $262,763/per year

• This role is on-site in El Segundo, CA

• Leveling and base salary is determined by job-related skills, education level, experience level, and job performance

• You will be eligible for incentives in the form of stock options and/or long-term cash awards

ITAR Requirements

Varda, like all employers, must ensure that its employees working in the United States are lawfully authorized to work in the U.S. Additionally, our employees are exposed to and have access to certain export-controlled items. Because our employees are provided access to export-controlled items, our policy is to only hire “U.S. persons” who are permitted to have access to our technology without an export license.

“US person” means: U.S. citizen, U.S. lawful permanent resident, or protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3) (i.e., individual admitted to the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum).
